The Berry-connection matrix is Hermitian in band indices:
`(A_mn)⁎ = A_nm`.  In particular, off-diagonal entries are not asserted to be real.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  {ι : Type u_2} [inst_3 : Fintype ι] {κ : Type u_3} (data : BerryGeometry.MultidirectionalEigenbasisData κ ι H)
  [inst_4 : DecidableEq ι] (μ ν : κ) (n : ι),
  (∀ (m : ι), m ≠ n → data.energy m ≠ data.energy n) →
    data.berryCurvature μ ν n =
      ∑ m,
        if m = n then 0
        else
          2 *
            (data.hamiltonianDerivativeMatrixElement μ m n / ↑(data.energy n - data.energy m) *
                (data.hamiltonianDerivativeMatrixElement ν n m / ↑(data.energy n - data.energy m))).im
name: BerryGeometry.MultidirectionalEigenbasisData.berryCurvature_eq_sum_hamiltonianDerivativeMatrixElements
docString:
Force/Hamiltonian-derivative matrix-element representation of Berry curvature for a
nondegenerate band.

This is the finite-dimensional pointwise formula needed by the clean anomalous-Hall consumer.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  {ι : Type u_2} [inst_3 : Fintype ι] {κ : Type u_3} (data : BerryGeometry.MultidirectionalEigenbasisData κ ι H)
  (μ ν : κ) (n : ι),
  data.berryCurvature μ ν n =
    ∑ m,
      -2 *
        (inner ℂ (data.eigenvectorDerivative μ n) (data.eigenbasis m) *
            inner ℂ (data.eigenbasis m) (data.eigenvectorDerivative ν n)).im
name: BerryGeometry.MultidirectionalEigenbasisData.berryCurvature_eq_sum_innerProducts
docString:
Completeness of the finite orthonormal eigenbasis expands the derivative-state curvature into
band-resolved inner-product terms.

docString: Berry curvature is antisymmetric in its two parameter directions.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  {ι : Type u_2} [inst_3 : Fintype ι] {κ : Type u_3} (data : BerryGeometry.MultidirectionalEigenbasisData κ ι H)
  (μ ν : κ) {m n : ι},
  m ≠ n →
    data.energy m ≠ data.energy n →
      -2 *
          (inner ℂ (data.eigenvectorDerivative μ n) (data.eigenbasis m) *
              inner ℂ (data.eigenbasis m) (data.eigenvectorDerivative ν n)).im =
        2 *
          (data.hamiltonianDerivativeMatrixElement μ m n / ↑(data.energy n - data.energy m) *
              (data.hamiltonianDerivativeMatrixElement ν n m / ↑(data.energy n - data.energy m))).im
name: BerryGeometry.MultidirectionalEigenbasisData.curvatureInnerTerm_eq_hamiltonianDerivativeMatrixElements
docString:
An off-diagonal completeness term equals the conventional force-matrix Berry-curvature term.
The two real level-spacing factors are intentionally kept separate here; a downstream consumer may
normalize them to a squared denominator if desired.

    ∀ (moment : (n : ℕ) → (Fin (2 * n) → α) → R) (pairValue : α → α → R)
      (Admissible : (n : ℕ) → (Fin (2 * n) → α) → Prop),
      (∀ (C : Fin 0 → α), moment 0 C = 1) →
        (∀ (n : ℕ) (C : Fin (2 * (n + 1)) → α),
            Admissible (n + 1) C → ∀ (j : Fin (2 * n + 1)), Admissible n fun i => C (j.succAbove i).succ) →
          (∀ (n : ℕ) (C : Fin (2 * (n + 1)) → α),
              Admissible (n + 1) C →
                moment (n + 1) C =
                  ∑ j, ζ ^ ↑j * pairValue (C 0) (C j.succ) * moment n fun i => C (j.succAbove i).succ) →
            ∀ (n : ℕ) (C : Fin (2 * n) → α),
              Admissible n C → moment n C = ∑ P, ζ ^ P.crossingCount * ∏ pr ∈ P.pairs, pairValue (C pr.1) (C pr.2)

  0 < m →
    ∑ x, Combinatorics.singleCycleContribution ζ (fun a b => K (x a) (x b)) Finset.univ =
      ζ ^ (m - 1) * (↑(m - 1).factorial * (K ^ m).trace)

`ζ^(m-1) (m-1)! tr(K^m)` for positive label count `m`. This is the public trace bridge; the raw
assignment-kernel and cycle-enumeration objects remain implementation details.

  d f = 0 → δ (Q f) = B.source f
name: ConservationLaw.IntrinsicBalanceLaw.evolution_eq_source_of_differential_eq_zero
docString: If the differential test vanishes, only the source can change the localized quantity.

statement:
∀ {𝕜 : Type u_1} {Test : Type u_2} {OneForm : Type u_3} {Obs : Type u_4} [inst : CommSemiring 𝕜]
  [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid Test] [inst_2 : _root_.Module 𝕜 Test] [inst_3 : AddCommMonoid OneForm]
  [inst_4 : _root_.Module 𝕜 OneForm] [inst_5 : AddCommMonoid Obs] [inst_6 : _root_.Module 𝕜 Obs] {δ : Obs →ₗ[𝕜] Obs}
  {Q : Test →ₗ[𝕜] Obs} {d : Test →ₗ[𝕜] OneForm} (B : ConservationLaw.IntrinsicBalanceLaw δ Q d),
  B.source = 0 → ∀ (f : Test), B.transport f = δ (Q f)
name: ConservationLaw.IntrinsicBalanceLaw.sourceFreeFlux_eq_evolution
docString: In a source-free law, intrinsic flux is exactly the localized evolution.

statement:
∀ {𝕜 : Type u_1} {Test : Type u_2} {OneForm : Type u_3} {Obs : Type u_4} [inst : CommSemiring 𝕜]
  [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid Test] [inst_2 : _root_.Module 𝕜 Test] [inst_3 : AddCommMonoid OneForm]
  [inst_4 : _root_.Module 𝕜 OneForm] [inst_5 : AddCommMonoid Obs] [inst_6 : _root_.Module 𝕜 Obs] {δ : Obs →ₗ[𝕜] Obs}
  {Q : Test →ₗ[𝕜] Obs} {d : Test →ₗ[𝕜] OneForm} (B₁ B₂ : ConservationLaw.IntrinsicBalanceLaw δ Q d),
  B₁.source = 0 → B₂.source = 0 → ∀ (f : Test), B₁.transport f = B₂.transport f
name: ConservationLaw.IntrinsicBalanceLaw.sourceFreeFlux_unique
docString: Source-free intrinsic flux is unique for fixed evolution, localized quantity, and differential.

statement:
∀ {𝕜 : Type u_1} {Test : Type u_2} {OneForm : Type u_3} {Obs : Type u_4} [inst : CommSemiring 𝕜]
  [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid Test] [inst_2 : _root_.Module 𝕜 Test] [inst_3 : AddCommMonoid OneForm]
  [inst_4 : _root_.Module 𝕜 OneForm] [inst_5 : AddCommMonoid Obs] [inst_6 : _root_.Module 𝕜 Obs] {δ : Obs →ₗ[𝕜] Obs}
  {Q : Test →ₗ[𝕜] Obs} {d : Test →ₗ[𝕜] OneForm} (self : ConservationLaw.IntrinsicBalanceLaw δ Q d),
  ConservationLaw.DependsOnlyOnDifferential d self.transport
name: ConservationLaw.IntrinsicBalanceLaw.transport_depends
docString: Transport is insensitive to changes of a test object that leave its differential fixed.

statement:
∀ {𝕜 : Type u_1} {Test : Type u_2} {OneForm : Type u_3} {Obs : Type u_4} [inst : CommSemiring 𝕜]
  [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid Test] [inst_2 : _root_.Module 𝕜 Test] [inst_3 : AddCommMonoid OneForm]
  [inst_4 : _root_.Module 𝕜 OneForm] [inst_5 : AddCommMonoid Obs] [inst_6 : _root_.Module 𝕜 Obs] {δ : Obs →ₗ[𝕜] Obs}
  {Q : Test →ₗ[𝕜] Obs} {d : Test →ₗ[𝕜] OneForm} (B : ConservationLaw.IntrinsicBalanceLaw δ Q d) {f : Test},
  d f = 0 → B.transport f = 0
name: ConservationLaw.IntrinsicBalanceLaw.transport_eq_zero_of_differential_eq_zero
docString: Intrinsic transport vanishes on test objects annihilated by the differential.

name: ConservationLaw.LocalCurrentDensityRepresentation.currentDensityEquivalent
docString:
Any two densities representing the same transport functional are weakly equivalent on exact
test 1-forms.

name: ConservationLaw.LocalCurrentDensityRepresentation.represents
docString: The transport functional is the pairing of `currentDensity` with `d f`.

statement:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup V] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (S T : V →ₗ[ℂ] V),
  (ConservationLaw.commutatorEvolution S) T = ConservationLaw.linearCommutator S T
name: ConservationLaw.commutatorEvolution_apply

statement:
∀ {Test : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup Test] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ Test] (V : Type u_3) [inst_2 : AddCommGroup V]
  [inst_3 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (h : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (M : Test →ₗ[ℂ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (m : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (f : Test),
  (ConservationLaw.commutatorEvolution h) ((ConservationLaw.localizedQuantityFunctional V M m) f) =
    (ConservationLaw.transportFunctional V h M m) f + (ConservationLaw.sourceFunctional V h M m) f
name: ConservationLaw.commutatorEvolution_localizedQuantityFunctional
docString: The packaged localized quantity satisfies the same transport/source decomposition.

statement:
∀ {OneForm : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup OneForm] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ OneForm] (V : Type u_2)
  [inst_2 : AddCommGroup V] [inst_3 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (velocity m : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (N : OneForm →ₗ[ℂ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V)
  (α : OneForm),
  (ConservationLaw.conventionalSymmetrizedCurrentFlux V velocity m N) α =
    ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct (N α) (ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct velocity m)
name: ConservationLaw.conventionalSymmetrizedCurrentFlux_apply

statement: ∀ {a b : ℝ} {f : ℝ → ℝ}, tsupport f ⊆ Set.Ioo a b → f a = 0 ∧ f b = 0
name: ConservationLaw.endpoint_values_eq_zero_of_tsupport_subset_Ioo
docString:
A function whose topological support is strictly inside an interval vanishes at both
endpoints.

statement: ∀ {a b : ℝ} {f g : ℝ → ℝ}, tsupport f ⊆ Set.Ioo a b → ∫ (x : ℝ) in a..b, deriv f x * g x = ∫ (x : ℝ), deriv f x * g x
name: ConservationLaw.integral_deriv_mul_eq_integral_of_tsupport_subset_Ioo
docString:
The derivative of a function supported strictly inside an interval has the same support
window for the purpose of multiplying by an arbitrary function.

statement: ∀ {a b : ℝ} {f g : ℝ → ℝ}, tsupport f ⊆ Set.Ioo a b → ∫ (x : ℝ) in a..b, f x * g x = ∫ (x : ℝ), f x * g x
name: ConservationLaw.integral_mul_eq_integral_of_tsupport_subset_Ioo
docString:
A function supported strictly inside an interval makes its product with any function
interval-integrable and whole-space integrable through the interval support theorem.

statement:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup V] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (S T : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (v : V),
  (ConservationLaw.linearCommutator S T) v = S (T v) - T (S v)
name: ConservationLaw.linearCommutator_apply

statement:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup V] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (M A B : V →ₗ[ℂ] V),
  ConservationLaw.linearCommutator M (A ∘ₗ B) =
    ConservationLaw.linearCommutator M A ∘ₗ B + A ∘ₗ ConservationLaw.linearCommutator M B
name: ConservationLaw.linearCommutator_comp_right
docString:
Leibniz rule for a commutator with a composition on the right:
`[M, A B] = [M,A] B + A [M,B]`.

statement:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup V] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (S T : V →ₗ[ℂ] V),
  ConservationLaw.linearCommutator S T = LinearMap.zetaCommutator 1 S T
name: ConservationLaw.linearCommutator_eq_zetaCommutator
docString: The ordinary commutator is the `ζ = 1` specialization of the generic `ζ`-commutator.

statement:
∀ {Test : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup Test] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ Test] (V : Type u_3) [inst_2 : AddCommGroup V]
  [inst_3 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (h : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (M : Test →ₗ[ℂ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (m : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (f : Test),
  ConservationLaw.linearCommutator h (ConservationLaw.localizedQuantity V M m f) =
    ConservationLaw.transportCommutator V h M m f + ConservationLaw.sourceCommutator V h M m f
name: ConservationLaw.linearCommutator_localizedQuantity
docString: The commutator is a derivation on symmetric localization, giving transport plus source.

statement:
∀ {Test : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup Test] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ Test] (V : Type u_3) [inst_2 : AddCommGroup V]
  [inst_3 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (h : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (M : Test →ₗ[ℂ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (m : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (f : Test),
  ConservationLaw.linearCommutator h m = 0 →
    ConservationLaw.linearCommutator h (ConservationLaw.localizedQuantity V M m f) =
      ConservationLaw.transportCommutator V h M m f
name: ConservationLaw.linearCommutator_localizedQuantity_of_commutes
docString: For a conserved quantity, the localized balance identity contains only transport.

statement:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup V] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (M X Y Px Py : V →ₗ[ℂ] V),
  ConservationLaw.linearCommutator M (ConservationLaw.orbitalAngularMomentumZ X Y Px Py) =
    ConservationLaw.linearCommutator M X ∘ₗ Py + X ∘ₗ ConservationLaw.linearCommutator M Py -
      (ConservationLaw.linearCommutator M Y ∘ₗ Px + Y ∘ₗ ConservationLaw.linearCommutator M Px)
name: ConservationLaw.linearCommutator_orbitalAngularMomentumZ
docString: Expansion of a localization commutator with algebraic orbital angular momentum.

statement:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup V] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (M X Y Px Py Dx Dy : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (ℏ : ℝ),
  ConservationLaw.linearCommutator M X = 0 →
    ConservationLaw.linearCommutator M Y = 0 →
      ConservationLaw.linearCommutator M Px = (Complex.I * ↑ℏ) • Dx →
        ConservationLaw.linearCommutator M Py = (Complex.I * ↑ℏ) • Dy →
          ConservationLaw.linearCommutator M (ConservationLaw.orbitalAngularMomentumZ X Y Px Py) =
            X ∘ₗ ((Complex.I * ↑ℏ) • Dy) - Y ∘ₗ ((Complex.I * ↑ℏ) • Dx)
name: ConservationLaw.linearCommutator_orbitalAngularMomentumZ_continuum_sign
docString:
Continuum-sign specialization for `Pᵢ = -i ℏ ∂ᵢ`:
`[M_f,L_z] = X (iℏ D_y) - Y (iℏ D_x)` once the momentum commutators have been identified with
multiplication by the derivatives of the localizer.

statement:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup V] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (M X Y Px Py : V →ₗ[ℂ] V),
  ConservationLaw.linearCommutator M X = 0 →
    ConservationLaw.linearCommutator M Y = 0 →
      (ConservationLaw.linearCommutator M (ConservationLaw.orbitalAngularMomentumZ X Y Px Py) ≠ 0 ↔
        X ∘ₗ ConservationLaw.linearCommutator M Py - Y ∘ₗ ConservationLaw.linearCommutator M Px ≠ 0)
name: ConservationLaw.linearCommutator_orbitalAngularMomentumZ_ne_zero_iff
docString:
Exact nonvanishing criterion under position-localizer commutation.

This makes the obstruction explicit: continuum-like `L_z` fails to commute with localization exactly
when the derivative-localization combination on the right is nonzero.

statement:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup V] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (M X Y Px Py : V →ₗ[ℂ] V),
  ConservationLaw.linearCommutator M X = 0 →
    ConservationLaw.linearCommutator M Y = 0 →
      ConservationLaw.linearCommutator M (ConservationLaw.orbitalAngularMomentumZ X Y Px Py) =
        X ∘ₗ ConservationLaw.linearCommutator M Py - Y ∘ₗ ConservationLaw.linearCommutator M Px
name: ConservationLaw.linearCommutator_orbitalAngularMomentumZ_of_commutes_position
docString:
If localization commutes with position, its orbital commutator is controlled entirely by the
momentum-localization commutators:

`[M,L_z] = X [M,Pᵧ] - Y [M,Pₓ]`.

statement:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup V] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (M X Y Px Py Dx Dy : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (c : ℂ),
  ConservationLaw.linearCommutator M X = 0 →
    ConservationLaw.linearCommutator M Y = 0 →
      ConservationLaw.linearCommutator M Px = c • Dx →
        ConservationLaw.linearCommutator M Py = c • Dy →
          ConservationLaw.linearCommutator M (ConservationLaw.orbitalAngularMomentumZ X Y Px Py) =
            X ∘ₗ (c • Dy) - Y ∘ₗ (c • Dx)
name: ConservationLaw.linearCommutator_orbitalAngularMomentumZ_of_derivative_localizers
docString:
Specialization when the momentum-localization commutators are represented by supplied
"derivative localizer" operators `Dx` and `Dy` with a common scalar coefficient `c`.

For continuum momentum `Pᵢ = -i ℏ ∂ᵢ`, the physical coefficient is `c = i ℏ` and `Di` is
multiplication by `∂ᵢ f`.

statement:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup V] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (S : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (q : ℂ),
  ConservationLaw.linearCommutator S (q • LinearMap.id) = 0
name: ConservationLaw.linearCommutator_smul_id_right
docString: A scalar multiple of the identity commutes with every complex-linear endomorphism.

statement:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup V] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (q : ℂ) (S T : V →ₗ[ℂ] V),
  ConservationLaw.linearCommutator S (q • T) = q • ConservationLaw.linearCommutator S T
name: ConservationLaw.linearCommutator_smul_right
docString: The ordinary commutator is linear in its right argument.

statement:
∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup V] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (M A B : V →ₗ[ℂ] V),
  ConservationLaw.linearCommutator M (A - B) =
    ConservationLaw.linearCommutator M A - ConservationLaw.linearCommutator M B
name: ConservationLaw.linearCommutator_sub_right
docString: A commutator is additive over subtraction in its second argument.

statement:
∀ {W : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup W] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ W] (h A B : W →ₗ[ℂ] W),
  ConservationLaw.linearCommutator h (ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct A B) =
    ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct (ConservationLaw.linearCommutator h A) B +
      ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct A (ConservationLaw.linearCommutator h B)
name: ConservationLaw.linearCommutator_symmetrizedProduct
docString: The commutator acts as a derivation on the symmetrized product.

statement:
∀ {𝕜 : Type u_1} {Test : Type u_2} {OneForm : Type u_3} {Obs : Type u_4} {CurrentDensity : Type u_5}
  [inst : CommSemiring 𝕜] [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid Test] [inst_2 : _root_.Module 𝕜 Test] [inst_3 : AddCommMonoid OneForm]
  [inst_4 : _root_.Module 𝕜 OneForm] [inst_5 : AddCommMonoid Obs] [inst_6 : _root_.Module 𝕜 Obs]
  [inst_7 : AddCommMonoid CurrentDensity] [inst_8 : _root_.Module 𝕜 CurrentDensity] {d : Test →ₗ[𝕜] OneForm}
  {Φ : Test →ₗ[𝕜] Obs} {pairing : ConservationLaw.LocalCurrentPairing},
  ConservationLaw.SeparatesCurrentDensities d pairing →
    ∀ (R₁ R₂ : ConservationLaw.LocalCurrentDensityRepresentation d Φ pairing), R₁.currentDensity = R₂.currentDensity
name: ConservationLaw.localCurrentDensity_unique_of_separates
docString:
A local current density is unique when the concrete differential tests and pairing separate
current densities.

statement:
∀ {Test : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup Test] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ Test] (V : Type u_3) [inst_2 : AddCommGroup V]
  [inst_3 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (h : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (M : Test →ₗ[ℂ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (f : Test),
  (ConservationLaw.localizationCommutatorFunctional V h M) f = ConservationLaw.linearCommutator h (M f)
name: ConservationLaw.localizationCommutatorFunctional_apply

statement:
∀ {OneForm : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup OneForm] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ OneForm] (V : Type u_2)
  [inst_2 : AddCommGroup V] [inst_3 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (velocity m : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (N : OneForm →ₗ[ℂ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V)
  (α : OneForm),
  (ConservationLaw.localizationCorrectionCurrentFlux V velocity m N) α =
    (1 / 4) • ConservationLaw.linearCommutator velocity (ConservationLaw.linearCommutator (N α) m)
name: ConservationLaw.localizationCorrectionCurrentFlux_apply

statement:
∀ {OneForm : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup OneForm] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ OneForm] (V : Type u_2)
  [inst_2 : AddCommGroup V] [inst_3 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (velocity m : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (N : OneForm →ₗ[ℂ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V),
  (∀ (α : OneForm), ConservationLaw.linearCommutator (N α) m = 0) →
    ConservationLaw.localizationCorrectionCurrentFlux V velocity m N = 0
name: ConservationLaw.localizationCorrectionCurrentFlux_eq_zero_of_commutes
docString: If every supplied localizer commutes with `m`, the localization correction vanishes.

statement:
∀ {OneForm : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup OneForm] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ OneForm] (V : Type u_2)
  [inst_2 : AddCommGroup V] [inst_3 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (velocity : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (N : OneForm →ₗ[ℂ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (q : ℂ),
  ConservationLaw.localizationCorrectionCurrentFlux V velocity (q • LinearMap.id) N = 0
name: ConservationLaw.localizationCorrectionCurrentFlux_smul_id
docString: Charge-like transported quantities `q I` have no localization correction.

statement:
∀ {Test : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup Test] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ Test] (V : Type u_3) [inst_2 : AddCommGroup V]
  [inst_3 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (M : Test →ₗ[ℂ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (m : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (f : Test),
  (ConservationLaw.localizedQuantityFunctional V M m) f = ConservationLaw.localizedQuantity V M m f
name: ConservationLaw.localizedQuantityFunctional_apply

statement:
∀ {Test : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup Test] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ Test] (V : Type u_3) [inst_2 : AddCommGroup V]
  [inst_3 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (M : Test →ₗ[ℂ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (m : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (f : Test),
  ConservationLaw.linearCommutator (M f) m = 0 → ConservationLaw.localizedQuantity V M m f = M f ∘ₗ m
name: ConservationLaw.localizedQuantity_eq_comp_of_commutes
docString: When localization commutes with the quantity, symmetric localization reduces to `M f ∘ m`.

statement:
∀ {Test : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup Test] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ Test] (V : Type u_3) [inst_2 : AddCommGroup V]
  [inst_3 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (M : Test →ₗ[ℂ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (q : ℂ) (f : Test),
  ConservationLaw.localizedQuantity V M (q • LinearMap.id) f = q • M f
name: ConservationLaw.localizedQuantity_smul_id
docString: Charge-like quantities `q I` reduce to scalar multiplication under symmetric localization.

statement:
∀ {OneForm : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup OneForm] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ OneForm] (V : Type u_2)
  [inst_2 : AddCommGroup V] [inst_3 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (velocity m : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (N : OneForm →ₗ[ℂ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V)
  (α : OneForm),
  (ConservationLaw.nestedSymmetrizedCurrentFlux V velocity m N) α =
    ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct (ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct (N α) velocity) m
name: ConservationLaw.nestedSymmetrizedCurrentFlux_apply

statement:
∀ {OneForm : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup OneForm] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ OneForm] (V : Type u_2)
  [inst_2 : AddCommGroup V] [inst_3 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (velocity m : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (N : OneForm →ₗ[ℂ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V),
  ConservationLaw.nestedSymmetrizedCurrentFlux V velocity m N =
    ConservationLaw.conventionalSymmetrizedCurrentFlux V velocity m N +
      ConservationLaw.localizationCorrectionCurrentFlux V velocity m N
name: ConservationLaw.nestedSymmetrizedCurrentFlux_eq_conventional_add_correction
docString: The nested flux is exactly conventional/symmetrized flux plus localization correction.

statement:
∀ {Test : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup Test] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ Test] (V : Type u_3) [inst_2 : AddCommGroup V]
  [inst_3 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (h : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (M : Test →ₗ[ℂ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (m : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (f : Test),
  ConservationLaw.linearCommutator h m = 0 → ConservationLaw.sourceCommutator V h M m f = 0
name: ConservationLaw.sourceCommutator_eq_zero_of_commutes
docString: A conserved one-body quantity has no local source/torque contribution.

statement:
∀ {Test : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup Test] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ Test] (V : Type u_3) [inst_2 : AddCommGroup V]
  [inst_3 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (h : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (M : Test →ₗ[ℂ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (q : ℂ) (f : Test),
  ConservationLaw.sourceCommutator V h M (q • LinearMap.id) f = 0
name: ConservationLaw.sourceCommutator_smul_id
docString: Charge-like quantities have no source/torque term.

statement:
∀ {Test : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup Test] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ Test] (V : Type u_3) [inst_2 : AddCommGroup V]
  [inst_3 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (h : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (M : Test →ₗ[ℂ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (m : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (f : Test),
  (ConservationLaw.sourceFunctional V h M m) f = ConservationLaw.sourceCommutator V h M m f
name: ConservationLaw.sourceFunctional_apply

statement:
∀ (V : Type u_3) [inst : AddCommGroup V] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ V] (m A : V →ₗ[ℂ] V),
  (ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProductRightLinear V m) A = ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct A m
name: ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProductRightLinear_apply

statement:
∀ {W : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup W] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ W] (A B : W →ₗ[ℂ] W) (v : W),
  (ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct A B) v = (1 / 2) • (A (B v) + B (A v))
name: ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct_apply

statement:
∀ {W : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup W] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ W] (A B : W →ₗ[ℂ] W),
  ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct A B = ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct B A
name: ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct_comm
docString: The symmetrized product is symmetric in its two arguments.

statement:
∀ {W : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup W] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ W] (A B : W →ₗ[ℂ] W),
  ConservationLaw.linearCommutator A B = 0 → ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct A B = A ∘ₗ B
name: ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct_eq_comp_of_commutes
docString: If two operators commute, their symmetrized product reduces to ordinary composition.

statement:
∀ {W : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup W] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ W] (A B : W →ₗ[ℂ] W),
  ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct A B = (1 / 2) • LinearMap.zetaCommutator (-1) A B
name: ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct_eq_smul_zetaCommutator_neg_one
docString:
The symmetric product is one half of the `ζ = -1` commutator algebraically.

This is only an operator-algebra identity; it does not attach fermionic statistics to
`symmetrizedProduct`.

statement:
∀ {W : Type u_1} [inst : AddCommGroup W] [inst_1 : _root_.Module ℂ W] (A v m : W →ₗ[ℂ] W),
  ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct (ConservationLaw.symmetrizedProduct A v) m =
