A positive compact operator whose lossless diagonal values are summable against one Hilbert
basis has summable nonzero real eigenvalues.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] {T : H →L[ℂ] H} {c : ℝ},
  c ≠ 0 → T.HasSummableRealEigenvalues → (c • T).HasSummableRealEigenvalues
name: ContinuousLinearMap.hasSummableRealEigenvalues_smul
docString: Spectral summability is preserved under multiplication by a nonzero real scalar.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (U T : H →L[ℂ] H),
  star U * U = 1 → U * star U = 1 → T.HasSummableRealEigenvalues → (U.unitaryConjugate T).HasSummableRealEigenvalues
name: ContinuousLinearMap.hasSummableRealEigenvalues_unitaryConjugate
docString:
Absolute summability of real eigenvalues with multiplicity is invariant under unitary
conjugation.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  {T : H →L[ℂ] H} (hT : IsCompactOperator ⇑T),
  (↑T).IsSymmetric →
    ∀ {ι : Type u_2} (b : HilbertBasis ι ℂ H) (j : T.EigenvectorIndex → ι),
      (∀ (a : T.EigenvectorIndex), b (j a) = ContinuousLinearMap.eigenvectorFamily hT a) →
        ∀ x ∉ Set.range j, T (b x) = 0
name: ContinuousLinearMap.hilbertBasis_apply_eq_zero_of_not_mem_eigenvector_range
docString:
A Hilbert-basis vector outside the embedded canonical nonzero-eigenvector family lies in the
kernel of a compact symmetric operator.

name: ContinuousLinearMap.innerHS_eq_of_isHilbertSchmidt
docString:
**`innerHS` is independent of the choice of Hilbert basis.** Applying
`summable_inner_adjoint_apply_and_tsum_eq` with the same basis for both arguments identifies
`innerHS d S T` with `Σᵢ ⟪T† dᵢ, S† dᵢ⟫`; applying it again with `d` and `f` swapped identifies
the latter with `innerHS f S T`.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H] {A : H →L[ℂ] H},
  IsCompactOperator ⇑A →
    (↑A).IsSymmetric →
      A.HasSummableRealEigenvalues →
        ∀ {ι : Type u_2} (d : HilbertBasis ι ℂ H), ContinuousLinearMap.innerHS d 1 A = ↑A.spectralTrace
name: ContinuousLinearMap.innerHS_one_eq_spectralTrace
docString:
For a compact self-adjoint spectrally summable `A`, `innerHS d 1 A` agrees with the spectral
trace of `A`.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] (x y : H),
  IsCompactOperator ⇑(((InnerProductSpace.rankOne ℂ) x) y)
name: ContinuousLinearMap.isCompactOperator_rankOne
docString: Rank-one operators on a Hilbert space are compact.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (U T : H →L[ℂ] H), IsCompactOperator ⇑T → IsCompactOperator ⇑(U.unitaryConjugate T)
name: ContinuousLinearMap.isCompactOperator_unitaryConjugate
docString: Compactness is preserved under bounded unitary conjugation.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] {ι : Type u_2} (d : HilbertBasis ι ℂ H)
  (B : H →L[ℂ] H) {T : H →L[ℂ] H},
  ContinuousLinearMap.IsHilbertSchmidtWrt d T → ContinuousLinearMap.IsHilbertSchmidtWrt d (B * T)
name: ContinuousLinearMap.isHilbertSchmidtWrt_comp_left
docString:
**Composing a Hilbert–Schmidt operator with a bounded operator on the left stays
Hilbert–Schmidt**, with respect to the same basis, by the comparison test against the operator
norm bound `‖B (T dᵢ)‖ ≤ ‖B‖ * ‖T dᵢ‖`.

name: ContinuousLinearMap.isHilbertSchmidtWrt_iff
docString: **`IsHilbertSchmidtWrt` is independent of the choice of Hilbert basis.**

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  {T : H →L[ℂ] H}, T.IsHilbertSchmidt → (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint T).IsHilbertSchmidt
name: ContinuousLinearMap.isHilbertSchmidt_adjoint
docString:
**Hilbert–Schmidt-ness is preserved by taking the adjoint.** A direct consequence of the
basis-independence computation: `T` being Hilbert–Schmidt with respect to `d` already gives that
`T†` is Hilbert–Schmidt with respect to that *same* `d` (no basis change needed for this
direction).

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] (B : H →L[ℂ] H) {T : H →L[ℂ] H},
  T.IsHilbertSchmidt → (B * T).IsHilbertSchmidt
name: ContinuousLinearMap.isHilbertSchmidt_comp_left

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H] {T : H →L[ℂ] H},
  T.IsHilbertSchmidt → ∀ (B : H →L[ℂ] H), (T * B).IsHilbertSchmidt
name: ContinuousLinearMap.isHilbertSchmidt_comp_right
docString:
**Composing a Hilbert–Schmidt operator with a bounded operator on the right stays
Hilbert–Schmidt.** Reduced to the left-composition case via the adjoint identity
`(T * B)† = B† * T†`: `T†` is Hilbert–Schmidt (`isHilbertSchmidt_adjoint`), so `B† * T†` is
Hilbert–Schmidt (`isHilbertSchmidt_comp_left`), so its adjoint `T * B` is Hilbert–Schmidt
(`isHilbertSchmidt_adjoint` again, using `T†† = T`).

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H] {ι : Type u_2}
  (d : HilbertBasis ι ℂ H) (T : H →L[ℂ] H), T.IsHilbertSchmidt ↔ ContinuousLinearMap.IsHilbertSchmidtWrt d T
name: ContinuousLinearMap.isHilbertSchmidt_iff_isHilbertSchmidtWrt

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] {α : Type u_2} {l : Filter α} [l.NeBot]
  {F : α → H →L[ℂ] H} {T : H →L[ℂ] H}, Filter.Tendsto F l (nhds T) → (∀ᶠ (i : α) in l, (F i).IsPositive) → T.IsPositive
name: ContinuousLinearMap.isPositive_of_tendsto
docString: Positivity is closed under convergence in the continuous-linear-map topology.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  {T : H →L[ℂ] H} (hT : IsCompactOperator ⇑T),
  (↑T).IsSymmetric →
    (Module.End.eigenspace (↑T) 0 ⊔
          Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range (ContinuousLinearMap.eigenvectorFamily hT))).topologicalClosure =
      ⊤
name: ContinuousLinearMap.kernel_sup_span_eigenvectorFamily_dense
docString:
**The kernel and `eigenvectorFamily`'s span together are dense.** Their (algebraic) sum
equals the sum of *all* eigenspaces of `T` (over `ℂ`), which is dense by
`orthogonalComplement_iSup_eigenspaces_eq_bot` — since a self-adjoint operator's eigenvalues are
always real, no eigenspace outside `ℝ` (hence outside the kernel-or-nonzero-real split) is ever
missed. The second of the two structural facts combined by
`orthogonal_closure_span_eigenvectorFamily`.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  {T : H →L[ℂ] H} (hT : IsCompactOperator ⇑T),
  (↑T).IsSymmetric →
    (Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range (ContinuousLinearMap.eigenvectorFamily hT))).topologicalClosureᗮ =
      Module.End.eigenspace (↑T) 0
name: ContinuousLinearMap.orthogonal_closure_span_eigenvectorFamily
docString:
**The closure of the nonzero-eigenspace part and the kernel are exactly each other's
orthogonal complements.** The key structural fact enabling the `tsum` reconstruction of `T`,
combining `span_eigenvectorFamily_le_kernel_orthogonal` (mutual orthogonality) with
`kernel_sup_span_eigenvectorFamily_dense` (density of their sum).

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  {T : H →L[ℂ] H},
  IsCompactOperator ⇑T →
    ∀ (hTpos : T.IsPositive),
      T.HasSummableRealEigenvalues →
        ∀ {ι : Type u_2} {d : ι → H},
          Orthonormal ℂ d →
            (∀ (v : H), ‖v‖ = 1 → 0 < T.diagonalExpectationValue ⋯ v) →
              ∑' (i : ι), T.diagonalExpectationValue ⋯ (d i) = T.spectralTrace → (Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range d))ᗮ = ⊥
name: ContinuousLinearMap.orthogonal_span_eq_bot_of_sum_diagonalExpectationValue_eq_spectralTrace
docString:
If a positive operator has strictly positive diagonal value on every unit vector, an
orthonormal family can saturate its spectral trace only when its span has trivial orthogonal
complement.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  {T : H →L[ℂ] H} (hT : IsCompactOperator ⇑T),
  (↑T).IsSymmetric → Orthonormal ℂ (ContinuousLinearMap.eigenvectorFamily hT)
name: ContinuousLinearMap.orthonormal_eigenvectorFamily

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  {T : H →L[ℂ] H} (hT : IsCompactOperator ⇑T),
  Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range (ContinuousLinearMap.eigenvectorFamily hT)) = ⨆ μ, Module.End.eigenspace ↑T ↑↑μ
name: ContinuousLinearMap.span_eigenvectorFamily
docString:
The (algebraic) span of `eigenvectorFamily` is exactly the sum of all the nonzero
eigenspaces: each per-eigenspace `stdOrthonormalBasis` spans its own (finite-dimensional)
eigenspace, and these are glued together in the same way as the index type.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  {T : H →L[ℂ] H} (hT : IsCompactOperator ⇑T),
  (↑T).IsSymmetric →
    Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range (ContinuousLinearMap.eigenvectorFamily hT)) ≤ (Module.End.eigenspace (↑T) 0)ᗮ
name: ContinuousLinearMap.span_eigenvectorFamily_le_kernel_orthogonal
docString:
**`eigenvectorFamily`'s span lies inside the orthogonal complement of the kernel.** Each
eigenvector `eigenvectorFamily hT a` lies in a *nonzero*-eigenvalue eigenspace, which is
orthogonal to the eigenvalue-`0` eigenspace `ker T` (`IsSymmetric.orthogonalFamily_eigenspaces`),
so their span is too. The first of the two structural facts combined by
`orthogonal_closure_span_eigenvectorFamily`.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H] {T T' : H →L[ℂ] H},
  IsCompactOperator ⇑T →
    (↑T).IsSymmetric →
      IsCompactOperator ⇑T' →
        (↑T').IsSymmetric →
          IsCompactOperator ⇑(T + T') →
            (↑(T + T')).IsSymmetric →
              T.HasSummableRealEigenvalues →
                T'.HasSummableRealEigenvalues →
                  (T + T').HasSummableRealEigenvalues → (T + T').spectralTrace = T.spectralTrace + T'.spectralTrace
name: ContinuousLinearMap.spectralTrace_add
docString: Additivity of `spectralTrace`.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H] {T T' : H →L[ℂ] H},
  (↑T).IsSymmetric →
    (↑T').IsSymmetric →
      IsCompactOperator ⇑(T * T') →
        (↑(T * T')).IsSymmetric →
          IsCompactOperator ⇑(T' * T) →
            (↑(T' * T)).IsSymmetric →
              (T * T').HasSummableRealEigenvalues →
                (T' * T).HasSummableRealEigenvalues → (T * T').spectralTrace = (T' * T).spectralTrace
name: ContinuousLinearMap.spectralTrace_comp_comm
docString: Cyclicity of `spectralTrace` for two products satisfying the required hypotheses.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] {T : H →L[ℂ] H} {c : ℝ},
  c ≠ 0 →
    T.HasSummableRealEigenvalues → (c • T).HasSummableRealEigenvalues → (c • T).spectralTrace = c * T.spectralTrace
name: ContinuousLinearMap.spectralTrace_smul
docString: `spectralTrace` is homogeneous under multiplication by a nonzero real scalar.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (U T : H →L[ℂ] H),
  star U * U = 1 →
    U * star U = 1 →
      T.HasSummableRealEigenvalues →
        (U.unitaryConjugate T).HasSummableRealEigenvalues → (U.unitaryConjugate T).spectralTrace = T.spectralTrace
name: ContinuousLinearMap.spectralTrace_unitaryConjugate
docString: The spectral trace is invariant under unitary conjugation.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  {T : H →L[ℂ] H},
  IsCompactOperator ⇑T →
    ∀ (hTpos : T.IsPositive),
      T.HasSummableRealEigenvalues →
        ∀ {ι : Type u_2} {d : ι → H},
          Orthonormal ℂ d →
            (Summable fun i => T.diagonalExpectationValue ⋯ (d i)) ∧
              ∑' (i : ι), T.diagonalExpectationValue ⋯ (d i) ≤ T.spectralTrace
name: ContinuousLinearMap.sum_diagonalExpectationValue_le_spectralTrace
docString:
The sum of lossless diagonal expectation values of a positive spectrally summable operator
against any orthonormal family is at most its spectral trace.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] {S : H →L[ℂ] H},
  S.HasSummableRealEigenvalues → Summable fun a => ↑a.fst
name: ContinuousLinearMap.summable_eigenvectorIndex

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  {ι : Type u_2} {κ : Type u_3} (d : HilbertBasis ι ℂ H) (f : HilbertBasis κ ℂ H) {S T : H →L[ℂ] H},
  ContinuousLinearMap.IsHilbertSchmidtWrt d S →
    ContinuousLinearMap.IsHilbertSchmidtWrt d T →
      (Summable fun j => inner ℂ ((ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint T) (f j)) ((ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint S) (f j))) ∧
        ∑' (j : κ), inner ℂ ((ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint T) (f j)) ((ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint S) (f j)) =
          ∑' (i : ι), inner ℂ (S (d i)) (T (d i))
name: ContinuousLinearMap.summable_inner_adjoint_apply_and_tsum_eq
docString:
**The core Fubini computation underlying basis-independence of `innerHS`.** For `S`, `T`
Hilbert–Schmidt with respect to a basis `d`, and *any* other basis `f`, the double sum
`Σᵢⱼ ⟪S dᵢ, fⱼ⟫ ⟪fⱼ, T dᵢ⟫` (`summable_inner_resolution_product`) can be summed either row-first
(giving `Σᵢ ⟪S dᵢ, T dᵢ⟫`, via the resolution of the identity along `f`) or column-first (giving
`Σⱼ ⟪T† fⱼ, S† fⱼ⟫`, via the resolution of the identity along `d`, after rewriting each factor
with the adjoint).

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] {ι : Type u_2} (d : HilbertBasis ι ℂ H)
  {S T : H →L[ℂ] H},
  ContinuousLinearMap.IsHilbertSchmidtWrt d S →
    ContinuousLinearMap.IsHilbertSchmidtWrt d T → Summable fun i => inner ℂ (S (d i)) (T (d i))
name: ContinuousLinearMap.summable_inner_apply_of_isHilbertSchmidtWrt

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] {ι : Type u_2} {κ : Type u_3}
  (d : HilbertBasis ι ℂ H) (f : HilbertBasis κ ℂ H) {S T : H →L[ℂ] H},
  ContinuousLinearMap.IsHilbertSchmidtWrt d S →
    ContinuousLinearMap.IsHilbertSchmidtWrt d T →
      Summable fun p => inner ℂ (S (d p.1)) (f p.2) * inner ℂ (f p.2) (T (d p.1))
name: ContinuousLinearMap.summable_inner_resolution_product
docString:
**Absolute summability of the "resolution of the identity" double product**
`⟪S dᵢ, fⱼ⟫⟪fⱼ, T dᵢ⟫`, for `S`, `T` Hilbert–Schmidt with respect to `d` and *any* other basis
`f`. Established via the AM–GM bound `|ab| ≤ (|a|² + |b|²) / 2` (rather than
`summable_prod_of_nonneg` applied to the family itself, since the summands here are complex, not
nonnegative). The absolute-summability half of
`summable_inner_adjoint_apply_and_tsum_eq`'s argument, isolated since it doesn't need the
row/column identification that follows it.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  {ι : Type u_2} {κ : Type u_3} (d : HilbertBasis ι ℂ H) (f : HilbertBasis κ ℂ H) (T : H →L[ℂ] H),
  (Summable fun i => ‖T (d i)‖ ^ 2) →
    (Summable fun j => ‖(ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint T) (f j)‖ ^ 2) ∧
      ∑' (j : κ), ‖(ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint T) (f j)‖ ^ 2 = ∑' (i : ι), ‖T (d i)‖ ^ 2
name: ContinuousLinearMap.summable_norm_sq_adjoint_apply_and_tsum_eq
docString:
**The core basis-independence computation.** If `T` is Hilbert–Schmidt with respect to a
basis `d`, then its adjoint `T†` is Hilbert–Schmidt with respect to *any* basis `f`, with the same
sum of squared norms. This is what makes `IsHilbertSchmidtWrt` (and, applying this twice via
`T†† = T`, comparisons between *any* two bases for `T` itself) basis-independent.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H] {ι : Type u_2}
  {κ : Type u_3} (d : HilbertBasis ι ℂ H) (f : HilbertBasis κ ℂ H) (T : H →L[ℂ] H),
  (Summable fun i => ‖T (d i)‖ ^ 2) →
    (Summable fun j => ‖T (f j)‖ ^ 2) ∧ ∑' (j : κ), ‖T (f j)‖ ^ 2 = ∑' (i : ι), ‖T (d i)‖ ^ 2
name: ContinuousLinearMap.summable_norm_sq_apply_and_tsum_eq
docString:
**The same basis-independence, phrased for `T` itself rather than its adjoint.** Applying
`summable_norm_sq_adjoint_apply_and_tsum_eq` twice — once for `T`, once for `T†` — and using
`T†† = T` transports the sum of squared norms of `T` from any one basis to any other. This is
the public-facing form of the basis-independence computation: callers wanting to compare `T`
across bases (`isHilbertSchmidtWrt_iff`) should use this rather than reasoning about `T†`
directly.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] {T : H →L[ℂ] H},
  (↑T).IsPositive → 0 ≤ T.spectralTrace
name: ContinuousLinearMap.trace_nonneg
docString: The spectral trace of a positive spectrally summable operator is nonnegative.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] {S : H →L[ℂ] H},
  (Summable fun a => ↑a.fst) →
    ∑' (a : S.EigenvectorIndex), ↑a.fst =
      ∑' (μ : { ν // ν ≠ 0 }), ↑(Module.finrank ℂ ↥(Module.End.eigenspace ↑S ↑↑μ)) * ↑μ
name: ContinuousLinearMap.tsum_eigenvectorIndex_eq_tsum_mul_finrank
docString:
Splits the spectral-trace `tsum` over `EigenvectorIndex S` into an outer sum over the
base nonzero eigenvalues and an inner finite sum over each eigenspace's basis vectors.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (U : H →L[ℂ] H) (x y : H),
  U.unitaryConjugate (((InnerProductSpace.rankOne ℂ) x) y) = ((InnerProductSpace.rankOne ℂ) (U x)) (U y)
name: ContinuousLinearMap.unitaryConjugate_rankOne
docString:
Conjugation transports a rank-one operator by applying the conjugating operator to both
vectors.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] (V : ℝ → A) (n : ℕ),
  Dyson.coeff V n 0 = if n = 0 then 1 else 0
name: Dyson.coeff_at_zero
docString: At the initial time, only the zeroth Dyson coefficient survives.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] (V : ℝ → A) (τ : ℝ),
  Dyson.coeff V 1 τ = -∫ (σ : ℝ) in 0..τ, V σ
name: Dyson.coeff_one
docString: The first generic Dyson coefficient is the negative integral of the interaction.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] (V : ℝ → A) (n : ℕ) (τ : ℝ),
  Dyson.coeff V (n + 1) τ = -∫ (σ : ℝ) in 0..τ, V σ * Dyson.coeff V n σ
name: Dyson.coeff_succ
docString: The defining successor recursion for generic Dyson coefficients.

statement: ∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] (V : ℝ → A) (τ : ℝ), Dyson.coeff V 0 τ = 1
name: Dyson.coeff_zero

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] [CompleteSpace A] (K : A) (lam : ℂ) (τ : ℝ),
  Dyson.constantExponential K lam τ = 1 - lam • ∫ (σ : ℝ) in 0..τ, K * Dyson.constantExponential K lam σ
name: Dyson.constantExponential_eq_one_sub_integral
docString: The constant exponential candidate satisfies the constant-generator Volterra equation.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] [CompleteSpace A] {V : ℝ → A},
  Continuous V →
    ∀ {β M : ℝ},
      ‖1‖ ≤ 1 →
        0 ≤ M →
          (∀ σ ∈ Set.Icc 0 β, ‖V σ‖ ≤ M) → ∀ (lam : ℂ), ContinuousOn (fun τ => Dyson.evolution V lam τ) (Set.Icc 0 β)
name: Dyson.continuousOn_evolution_of_bound
docString:
A continuous bounded interaction family has a continuous Dyson evolution on the compact
nonnegative interval where the uniform bound is available.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] [CompleteSpace A] {V : ℝ → A},
  Continuous V → ∀ (n : ℕ), Continuous (Dyson.coeff V n)
name: Dyson.continuous_coeff
docString: Continuous interaction families have continuous generic Dyson coefficients.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] [CompleteSpace A] (K : A) (lam : ℂ),
  Continuous (Dyson.constantExponential K lam)
name: Dyson.continuous_constantExponential
docString: The constant exponential candidate is continuous in time.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] [CompleteSpace A] {V : ℝ → A},
  Continuous V → ∀ (lam : ℂ) (n : ℕ), Continuous (Dyson.integrand V lam n)
name: Dyson.continuous_integrand
docString: Every generic Volterra-integrand term is continuous for a continuous interaction family.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] [CompleteSpace A] {V : ℝ → A},
  Continuous V → ∀ (lam : ℂ) (n : ℕ), Continuous fun τ => Dyson.term V lam τ n
name: Dyson.continuous_term
docString: Perturbatively weighted Dyson coefficients are continuous in time.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] [CompleteSpace A] {V U : ℝ → A},
  Continuous V →
    ∀ {β M : ℝ},
      0 ≤ β →
        ‖1‖ ≤ 1 →
          0 ≤ M →
            (∀ t ∈ Set.Icc 0 β, ‖V t‖ ≤ M) →
              ∀ (lam : ℂ),
                ContinuousOn U (Set.Icc 0 β) →
                  (∀ t ∈ Set.Icc 0 β, U t = 1 - lam • ∫ (σ : ℝ) in 0..t, V σ * U σ) →
                    Set.EqOn U (fun t => Dyson.evolution V lam t) (Set.Icc 0 β)
name: Dyson.eqOn_evolution_of_volterra_of_bound
docString:
The generic Dyson evolution is the unique continuous solution of its bounded Volterra equation
on `[0, β]`.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] [CompleteSpace A] {V U W : ℝ → A},
  Continuous V →
    ∀ {β M : ℝ},
      0 ≤ β →
        (∀ t ∈ Set.Icc 0 β, ‖V t‖ ≤ M) →
          ∀ (lam : ℂ),
            ContinuousOn U (Set.Icc 0 β) →
              ContinuousOn W (Set.Icc 0 β) →
                (∀ t ∈ Set.Icc 0 β, U t = 1 - lam • ∫ (σ : ℝ) in 0..t, V σ * U σ) →
                  (∀ t ∈ Set.Icc 0 β, W t = 1 - lam • ∫ (σ : ℝ) in 0..t, V σ * W σ) → Set.EqOn U W (Set.Icc 0 β)
name: Dyson.eqOn_of_volterra_of_bound
docString: Two continuous solutions of the same bounded Dyson–Volterra equation agree on `[0, β]`.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] [CompleteSpace A] (K : A) (lam : ℂ) {τ : ℝ},
  0 ≤ τ → ‖1‖ ≤ 1 → Dyson.evolution (fun x => K) lam τ = NormedSpace.exp (-((τ • lam) • K))
name: Dyson.evolution_const_eq_exp_of_nonneg
docString:
On nonnegative time, the Dyson evolution for a constant interaction is the corresponding
Banach-algebra exponential.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] [CompleteSpace A] {V : ℝ → A},
  Continuous V →
    ∀ {β M τ : ℝ},
      ‖1‖ ≤ 1 →
        0 ≤ M →
          (∀ t ∈ Set.Icc 0 β, ‖V t‖ ≤ M) →
            τ ∈ Set.Icc 0 β →
              ∀ (lam : ℂ), Dyson.evolution V lam τ = 1 - lam • ∫ (σ : ℝ) in 0..τ, V σ * Dyson.evolution V lam σ
name: Dyson.evolution_eq_one_sub_integral_of_bound
docString: The generic Dyson evolution solves the interaction-picture Volterra equation.

statement: ∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] (V : ℝ → A) (lam : ℂ), Dyson.evolution V lam 0 = 1
name: Dyson.evolution_zero
docString: The generic Dyson evolution starts at the algebra unit.

statement: ∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] (V : ℝ → A) (τ : ℝ), Dyson.evolution V 0 τ = 1
name: Dyson.evolution_zero_coupling
docString: The generic Dyson evolution is the algebra unit at zero scalar coupling.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] [CompleteSpace A] (K : A) (lam : ℂ) (τ : ℝ),
  HasDerivAt (Dyson.constantExponential K lam) (-(lam • (K * Dyson.constantExponential K lam τ))) τ
name: Dyson.hasDerivAt_constantExponential
docString:
The constant exponential candidate solves the expected interaction-picture differential
equation.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] [CompleteSpace A] (V : ℝ → A) {β M τ : ℝ},
  ‖1‖ ≤ 1 →
    0 ≤ M →
      (∀ σ ∈ Set.Icc 0 β, ‖V σ‖ ≤ M) →
        τ ∈ Set.Icc 0 β →
          ∀ (κ : ℂ), HasDerivAt (fun lam => Dyson.evolution V (↑lam * κ) τ) (-κ • ∫ (σ : ℝ) in 0..τ, V σ) 0
name: Dyson.hasDerivAt_evolution_linear_coupling_zero_of_bound
docString:
A Dyson evolution whose complex scalar coupling depends linearly on a real parameter is
differentiable at zero. The derivative is the exact first Dyson coefficient multiplied by the
linear coupling constant.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] [CompleteSpace A] {V U : ℝ → A},
  Continuous V →
    ∀ {β τ : ℝ},
      0 ≤ β →
        τ ∈ Set.Ico 0 β →
          ∀ (lam : ℂ),
            ContinuousOn U (Set.Icc 0 β) →
              (∀ u ∈ Set.Icc 0 β, U u = 1 - lam • ∫ (σ : ℝ) in 0..u, V σ * U σ) →
                HasDerivWithinAt U (-(lam • (V τ * U τ))) (Set.Ici τ) τ
name: Dyson.hasDerivWithinAt_of_volterra
docString:
A continuous solution of the Volterra equation satisfies the corresponding right-derivative
initial-value problem on the half-open interval.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] [CompleteSpace A] (V : ℝ → A) {β M : ℝ},
  ‖1‖ ≤ 1 →
    0 ≤ M →
      (∀ σ ∈ Set.Icc 0 β, ‖V σ‖ ≤ M) →
        ∀ (lam : ℂ),
          HasSumUniformlyOn (fun n τ => Dyson.term V lam τ n) (fun τ => Dyson.evolution V lam τ) (Set.Icc 0 β)
name: Dyson.hasSumUniformlyOn_evolution_of_bound
docString: On a bounded nonnegative interval, the generic Dyson series converges uniformly in norm.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] [CompleteSpace A] (V : ℝ → A) {β M : ℝ},
  ‖1‖ ≤ 1 →
    0 ≤ M →
      (∀ σ ∈ Set.Icc 0 β, ‖V σ‖ ≤ M) →
        ∀ (lam : ℂ) {τ : ℝ}, τ ∈ Set.Icc 0 β → HasSum (Dyson.term V lam τ) (Dyson.evolution V lam τ)
name: Dyson.hasSum_evolution_of_bound
docString: The defining series has sum `evolution` whenever the interaction is uniformly bounded.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] [CompleteSpace A] (V : ℝ → A) {β M σ : ℝ},
  ‖1‖ ≤ 1 →
    0 ≤ M →
      (∀ t ∈ Set.Icc 0 β, ‖V t‖ ≤ M) →
        σ ∈ Set.Icc 0 β →
          ∀ (lam : ℂ), HasSum (fun n => Dyson.integrand V lam n σ) (lam • (V σ * Dyson.evolution V lam σ))
name: Dyson.hasSum_integrand_of_bound
docString:
Left multiplication by the interaction and scalar multiplication carry the Dyson sum to the
pointwise Volterra integrand.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] [CompleteSpace A] {V : ℝ → A},
  Continuous V →
    ∀ {β M τ : ℝ},
      ‖1‖ ≤ 1 →
        0 ≤ M →
          (∀ t ∈ Set.Icc 0 β, ‖V t‖ ≤ M) →
            τ ∈ Set.Icc 0 β →
              ∀ (lam : ℂ),
                HasSum (fun n => ∫ (σ : ℝ) in 0..τ, Dyson.integrand V lam n σ)
                  (∫ (σ : ℝ) in 0..τ, lam • (V σ * Dyson.evolution V lam σ))
name: Dyson.hasSum_intervalIntegral_integrand_of_bound
docString: The generic Volterra integrand series may be exchanged with the Bochner interval integral.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] [CompleteSpace A] {V : ℝ → A},
  Continuous V →
    ∀ {β M τ : ℝ},
      ‖1‖ ≤ 1 →
        0 ≤ M →
          (∀ t ∈ Set.Icc 0 β, ‖V t‖ ≤ M) →
            τ ∈ Set.Icc 0 β →
              ∀ (lam : ℂ),
                HasSum (fun n => Dyson.term V lam τ (n + 1)) (-∫ (σ : ℝ) in 0..τ, lam • (V σ * Dyson.evolution V lam σ))
name: Dyson.hasSum_tail_of_bound
docString: The positive-order generic Dyson tail sums to the negative Volterra integral.

statement: ∀ (M τ : ℝ) (n : ℕ), ∫ (σ : ℝ) in 0..τ, M * Dyson.majorant M σ n = Dyson.majorant M τ (n + 1)
name: Dyson.integral_mul_majorant
docString: Integrating one more bounded interaction factor advances the factorial majorant by one order.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] (V : ℝ → A) (τ : ℝ) (lam : ℂ) (n : ℕ),
  ∫ (σ : ℝ) in 0..τ, Dyson.integrand V lam n σ = -Dyson.term V lam τ (n + 1)
name: Dyson.intervalIntegral_integrand
docString: Integrating the `n`th generic Volterra term gives the negative `(n+1)`st Dyson term.

statement: ∀ {M τ β : ℝ}, 0 ≤ M → 0 ≤ τ → τ ≤ β → ∀ (n : ℕ), Dyson.majorant M τ n ≤ Dyson.majorant M β n
name: Dyson.majorant_mono_time
docString: The factorial majorant is monotone in nonnegative time.

statement: ∀ {M τ : ℝ}, 0 ≤ M → 0 ≤ τ → ∀ (n : ℕ), 0 ≤ Dyson.majorant M τ n
name: Dyson.majorant_nonneg
docString: The Dyson majorant is nonnegative for nonnegative `M` and `τ`.

statement:
∀ {r M τ : ℝ},
  0 ≤ r → r ≤ 1 → 0 ≤ M → 0 ≤ τ → ∀ (n : ℕ), Dyson.majorant (r * M) τ (n + 2) ≤ r ^ 2 * Dyson.majorant M τ (n + 2)
name: Dyson.majorant_norm_mul_le_sq_mul_majorant
docString:
On the unit coupling ball, each shifted majorant term factors out two powers of the coupling
norm.

statement: ∀ (M τ : ℝ), Dyson.majorant M τ 0 = 1
name: Dyson.majorant_zero

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] (V : ℝ → A) {β M : ℝ},
  ‖1‖ ≤ 1 →
    0 ≤ M →
      (∀ σ ∈ Set.Icc 0 β, ‖V σ‖ ≤ M) → ∀ (n : ℕ) {τ : ℝ}, τ ∈ Set.Icc 0 β → ‖Dyson.coeff V n τ‖ ≤ Dyson.majorant M τ n
name: Dyson.norm_coeff_le_of_bound
docString:
An explicit uniform bound on the interaction family implies the standard factorial estimate for
all generic Dyson coefficients on `[0, β]`.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] [CompleteSpace A] (V : ℝ → A) {β M : ℝ},
  ‖1‖ ≤ 1 →
    0 ≤ M →
      (∀ σ ∈ Set.Icc 0 β, ‖V σ‖ ≤ M) →
        ∀ (lam : ℂ) {τ : ℝ},
          τ ∈ Set.Icc 0 β →
            ‖Dyson.evolution V lam τ - (1 + Dyson.term V lam τ 1)‖ ≤ ∑' (n : ℕ), Dyson.majorant (‖lam‖ * M) τ (n + 2)
name: Dyson.norm_evolution_sub_one_add_term_one_le_of_bound
docString:
The part of the bounded Dyson evolution beyond first order is controlled by the corresponding
shifted factorial-majorant series.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] [CompleteSpace A] (V : ℝ → A) {β M : ℝ},
  ‖1‖ ≤ 1 →
    0 ≤ M →
      (∀ σ ∈ Set.Icc 0 β, ‖V σ‖ ≤ M) →
        ∀ (lam : ℂ),
          ‖lam‖ ≤ 1 →
            ∀ {τ : ℝ},
              τ ∈ Set.Icc 0 β →
                ‖Dyson.evolution V lam τ - (1 + Dyson.term V lam τ 1)‖ ≤
                  ‖lam‖ ^ 2 * ∑' (n : ℕ), Dyson.majorant M τ (n + 2)
name: Dyson.norm_evolution_sub_one_add_term_one_le_sq_mul_of_bound
docString:
On the unit coupling ball, the complete Dyson remainder beyond first order is quadratic in the
coupling norm, with an explicit coupling-independent factorial tail.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] (V : ℝ → A) {β M σ : ℝ},
  ‖1‖ ≤ 1 →
    0 ≤ M →
      (∀ t ∈ Set.Icc 0 β, ‖V t‖ ≤ M) →
        σ ∈ Set.Icc 0 β → ∀ (lam : ℂ) (n : ℕ), ‖Dyson.integrand V lam n σ‖ ≤ Dyson.integrandMajorant M β lam n
name: Dyson.norm_integrand_le_of_bound
docString: Uniform pointwise norm control of every generic Volterra-integrand term on `[0, β]`.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] (V : ℝ → A) {β M : ℝ},
  ‖1‖ ≤ 1 →
    0 ≤ M →
      (∀ σ ∈ Set.Icc 0 β, ‖V σ‖ ≤ M) →
        ∀ (lam : ℂ) (n : ℕ) {τ : ℝ}, τ ∈ Set.Icc 0 β → ‖Dyson.term V lam τ n‖ ≤ Dyson.majorant (‖lam‖ * M) τ n
name: Dyson.norm_term_le_of_bound
docString:
The weighted `n`th coefficient is controlled by the factorial majorant with interaction bound
`‖λ‖ M`.

statement: ∀ (M β : ℝ) (lam : ℂ), Summable (Dyson.integrandMajorant M β lam)
name: Dyson.summable_integrandMajorant
docString: The generic Volterra-integrand majorant is summable.

statement: ∀ (M τ : ℝ), Summable (Dyson.majorant M τ)
name: Dyson.summable_majorant
docString: The scalar factorial majorant is summable for every real `M` and `τ`.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] [CompleteSpace A] (V : ℝ → A) {β M : ℝ},
  ‖1‖ ≤ 1 →
    0 ≤ M → (∀ σ ∈ Set.Icc 0 β, ‖V σ‖ ≤ M) → ∀ (lam : ℂ) {τ : ℝ}, τ ∈ Set.Icc 0 β → Summable (Dyson.term V lam τ)
name: Dyson.summable_term_of_bound
docString: The weighted generic Dyson coefficients are summable at each time in a bounded interval.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] (V : ℝ → A) (lam : ℂ) (n : ℕ),
  Dyson.term V lam 0 n = if n = 0 then 1 else 0
name: Dyson.term_at_zero
docString: At the initial time, all positive-order weighted coefficients vanish.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] (V : ℝ → A) (lam : ℂ) (τ : ℝ),
  Dyson.term V lam τ 1 = -lam • ∫ (σ : ℝ) in 0..τ, V σ
name: Dyson.term_one
docString: The first weighted Dyson term.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : NormedRing A] [inst_1 : NormedAlgebra ℂ A] (V : ℝ → A) (lam : ℂ) (τ : ℝ),
  Dyson.term V lam τ 0 = 1
name: Dyson.term_zero

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {s : Finset α} (π : Finpartition s) (order : Fin s.card ≃ ↥s)
  (orders : π.PartOrders) (h : π.PartOrdersCompatible order orders),
  π.assembleOrder orders (π.shuffleOfOrder order orders h) = order
name: Finpartition.assembleOrder_shuffleOfOrder
docString:
Reassembling a global order from compatible part-local orders and its extracted shuffle is the
original global order.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {a : Finset α} (P : Finpartition a)
  (Q : (i : Finset α) → i ∈ P.parts → Finpartition i), P.bind Q ≤ P
name: Finpartition.bind_le
docString: A partition obtained by independently refining every block refines the original partition.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {a : Finset α} {σ π : Finpartition a},
  π ≤ σ → (σ.bind fun _B hB => π.restrict ⋯) = π
name: Finpartition.bind_restrict_eq_of_le
docString: Restricting a refinement to every block and binding the results recovers the refinement.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {s : Finset α} (π : Finpartition s) (order : Fin s.card ≃ ↥s) (B : ↥π.parts),
  (π.partGlobalSlots order B).card = (↑B).card
name: Finpartition.card_partGlobalSlots
docString: A part occupies exactly as many ambient slots as it has elements.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {m : Finset α → ℂ} {A B : Finset α},
  Finpartition.IsIndependentAcross m A B →
    ∀ {T : Finset α}, T ⊆ A ⊔ B → T ≠ ⊥ → Finpartition.cumulantFromMoment m T = Finpartition.splitCumulant m A B T
name: Finpartition.cumulantFromMoment_eq_splitCumulant_of_le
docString: The true cumulant agrees with `splitCumulant` on every nonempty subset of the two regions.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {m : Finset α → ℂ} {A B : Finset α},
  Finpartition.IsIndependentAcross m A B → A ≠ ⊥ → B ≠ ⊥ → Finpartition.cumulantFromMoment m (A ⊔ B) = 0
name: Finpartition.cumulantFromMoment_eq_zero_of_isIndependentAcross
docString: The cumulant of a union of two nonempty independent regions vanishes.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {m : Finset α → ℂ} {A B : Finset α},
  Finpartition.IsIndependentAcross m A B →
    ∀ {T : Finset α}, T ⊆ A ⊔ B → ¬T ⊆ A → ¬T ⊆ B → Finpartition.cumulantFromMoment m T = 0
name: Finpartition.cumulantFromMoment_eq_zero_of_straddles
docString: Any set straddling both independent regions has vanishing cumulant.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq α] [inst_1 : CommRing R] (κ : Finset α → R) {S : Finset α},
  S ≠ ⊥ → Finpartition.cumulantFromMoment (Finpartition.momentFromCumulant κ) S = κ S
name: Finpartition.cumulantFromMoment_momentFromCumulant
docString: Pointwise Möbius inversion, away from the empty finite set.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {a : Finset α} {σ : Finpartition a} {A B B' : Finset α},
  B ∈ σ.parts → B' ∈ σ.parts → A ⊆ B → A ⊆ B' → A ≠ ⊥ → B = B'
name: Finpartition.eq_of_inf_ne_bot
docString: Two blocks containing the same nonempty finite set coincide.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {a b : Finset α} {P : Finpartition a} {hb : b ⊆ a} {d : Finset α},
  d ∈ (P.restrict hb).parts ↔ d ≠ ⊥ ∧ ∃ A ∈ P.parts, A ⊓ b = d
name: Finpartition.mem_restrict_iff
docString: Membership in a restricted partition.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq α] [inst_1 : CommRing R] (m : Finset α → R) {S : Finset α},
  S ≠ ⊥ → Finpartition.momentFromCumulant (Finpartition.cumulantFromMoment m) S = m S
name: Finpartition.momentFromCumulant_cumulantFromMoment
docString: Reverse pointwise inversion, away from the empty finite set.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {R : Type u_2} [inst_1 : CommSemiring R] (κ : Finset α → R) {s : Finset α}
  {a : α}, a ∈ s → Finpartition.momentFromCumulant κ s = ∑ B, κ ↑B * Finpartition.momentFromCumulant κ (s \ ↑B)
name: Finpartition.momentFromCumulant_eq_sum_blockContaining
docString: The moment sum splits by the block containing a distinguished element.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {m : Finset α → ℂ} {A B : Finset α},
  Finpartition.IsIndependentAcross m A B →
    ∀ T ⊆ A ⊔ B, Finpartition.momentFromCumulant (Finpartition.splitCumulant m A B) T = m T
name: Finpartition.momentFromCumulant_splitCumulant_eq

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {m : Finset α → ℂ} {A B T : Finset α},
  T ≠ ⊥ → T ⊆ A → Finpartition.momentFromCumulant (Finpartition.splitCumulant m A B) T = m T
name: Finpartition.momentFromCumulant_splitCumulant_of_le_left

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {m : Finset α → ℂ} {A B T : Finset α},
  T ≠ ⊥ → T ⊆ B → Finpartition.momentFromCumulant (Finpartition.splitCumulant m A B) T = m T
name: Finpartition.momentFromCumulant_splitCumulant_of_le_right

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {S : Finset α},
  S ≠ ∅ → (IncidenceAlgebra.mu ℤ) ⊥ ⊤ = (-1) ^ (S.card - 1) * ↑(S.card - 1).factorial
name: Finpartition.mu_bot_top_eq_factorial
docString:
For a nonempty finite set, the Möbius coefficient from the discrete partition to the
indiscrete partition is `(-1)^(n - 1) (n - 1)!`.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] (S : Finset α),
  (IncidenceAlgebra.mu ℤ) ⊥ ⊤ = if S = ∅ then 1 else (-1) ^ (S.card - 1) * ↑(S.card - 1).factorial
name: Finpartition.mu_bot_top_eq_factorial_ite
docString: Total bottom-to-top formula, including the empty partition lattice.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {S : Finset α} {π σ : Finpartition S},
  π ≤ σ →
    (IncidenceAlgebra.mu ℤ) π σ =
      ∏ B, (-1) ^ ((π.restrict ⋯).parts.card - 1) * ↑((π.restrict ⋯).parts.card - 1).factorial
name: Finpartition.mu_eq_prod_factorial
docString: Explicit product formula for every interval in a finite set-partition lattice.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {a : Finset α} {R : Type u_2} [inst_1 : CommRing R] {π σ : Finpartition a},
  π ≤ σ → (IncidenceAlgebra.mu R) π σ = ∏ B, (IncidenceAlgebra.mu R) (π.restrict ⋯) ⊤
name: Finpartition.mu_eq_prod_restrict
docString: The partition-lattice Möbius function factors over the blocks of the coarser partition.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {S : Finset α} (π : Finpartition S),
  S ≠ ∅ → (IncidenceAlgebra.mu ℤ) π ⊤ = (-1) ^ (π.parts.card - 1) * ↑(π.parts.card - 1).factorial
name: Finpartition.mu_to_top_eq_factorial
docString: The Möbius coefficient from a partition to the top is determined by its number of blocks.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {a : Finset α} {R : Type u_2} [inst_1 : CommRing R] (π : Finpartition a),
  (IncidenceAlgebra.mu R) π ⊤ = (IncidenceAlgebra.mu R) ⊥ ⊤
name: Finpartition.mu_to_top_eq_mu_bot_top_parts
docString: The Möbius function from a partition to the top depends only on its block set.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {s : Finset α} (π : Finpartition s) (order : Fin s.card ≃ ↥s) (B : ↥π.parts),
  Function.Injective (π.partGlobalSlot order B)
name: Finpartition.partGlobalSlot_injective
docString: Distinct elements of one part occupy distinct ambient slots.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {s : Finset α} (π : Finpartition s) (order : Fin s.card ≃ ↥s) (B : ↥π.parts)
  (v : ↥↑B), π.partGlobalSlot order B v ∈ π.partGlobalSlots order B
name: Finpartition.partGlobalSlot_mem_partGlobalSlots

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {s : Finset α} (π : Finpartition s) (order : Fin s.card ≃ ↥s) (B : ↥π.parts)
  (slot : ↥(π.partGlobalSlots order B)), π.partGlobalSlot order B ((π.partGlobalSlotEquiv order B).symm slot) = ↑slot
name: Finpartition.partGlobalSlot_partGlobalSlotEquiv_symm

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {s : Finset α} (π : Finpartition s) (order : Fin s.card ≃ ↥s) (B : ↥π.parts)
  (i : Fin (↑B).card),
  π.partGlobalSlot order B ((π.partOrderOfOrder order B) i) = ↑(((π.partGlobalSlots order B).orderIsoOfFin ⋯) i)
name: Finpartition.partGlobalSlot_partOrderOfOrder

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {s : Finset α} (π : Finpartition s) (order : Fin s.card ≃ ↥s) (B : ↥π.parts),
  StrictMono fun i => π.partGlobalSlot order B ((π.partOrderOfOrder order B) i)
name: Finpartition.partOrderOfOrder_strictMono
docString: The canonical local order on each part is strictly increasing in ambient slot number.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {s : Finset α} (π : Finpartition s) (order : Fin s.card ≃ ↥s) (B : ↥π.parts)
  (localOrder : Fin (↑B).card ≃ ↥↑B),
  (StrictMono fun i => π.partGlobalSlot order B (localOrder i)) → localOrder = π.partOrderOfOrder order B
name: Finpartition.partOrder_eq_of_strictMono
docString: A compatible order on one part must be its canonical increasing-slot order.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {s : Finset α} (π : Finpartition s) (orders : π.PartOrders)
  (shuffle : π.PartShuffle), π.PartOrdersCompatible (π.assembleOrder orders shuffle) orders
name: Finpartition.partOrdersCompatible_assembleOrder
docString: The local orders used to assemble a global order are compatible with that assembled order.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {s : Finset α} (π : Finpartition s) (order : Fin s.card ≃ ↥s),
  π.PartOrdersCompatible order (π.partOrdersOfOrder order)
name: Finpartition.partOrdersCompatible_partOrdersOfOrder
docString: The canonical part-local orders are compatible with the ambient order.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {s : Finset α} (π : Finpartition s) (order : Fin s.card ≃ ↥s)
  (orders : π.PartOrders), π.PartOrdersCompatible order orders → orders = π.partOrdersOfOrder order
name: Finpartition.partOrders_eq_of_compatible
docString: A compatible family of part-local orders is uniquely determined by the ambient order.

name: Finpartition.partitionProduct_bind
docString: Block products factor over a partition constructed by `bind`.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {m : Finset α → ℂ} {A B : Finset α},
  Finpartition.IsIndependentAcross m A B →
    ∀ (π : Finpartition (A ⊔ B)),
      Finpartition.partitionProduct m π =
        Finpartition.partitionProduct m (π.restrict ⋯) * Finpartition.partitionProduct m (π.restrict ⋯)
name: Finpartition.partitionProduct_eq_mul_of_isIndependentAcross
docString: Partition products factor across independent regions.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {S : Finset α} (π : Finpartition S) {b : Finset α} (hb : b ⊆ S)
  {m : Finset α → ℂ}, m ⊥ = 1 → Finpartition.partitionProduct m (π.restrict hb) = ∏ C ∈ π.parts, m (C ⊓ b)
name: Finpartition.partitionProduct_restrict_eq_prod_inf
docString: A restricted partition product is the product of the corresponding intersections.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq α] [inst_1 : CommRing R] {S : Finset α},
  S ≠ ∅ → ∀ (f : Finset α → R), Finpartition.partitionProduct f ⊤ = f S
name: Finpartition.partitionProduct_top

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq α] [inst_1 : CommMonoid M] {s : Finset α} (π : Finpartition s)
  (a : M), a ^ s.card = ∏ B, a ^ (↑B).card
name: Finpartition.pow_card_eq_prod_parts
docString:
A power indexed by `s.card` factors into powers indexed by the cardinalities of the partition
parts.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq α] [inst_1 : CommMonoid M] {s : Finset α} (π : Finpartition s)
  (f : ↥s → M), ∏ x, f x = ∏ B, ∏ x, f (π.equivSigmaParts.symm ⟨B, x⟩)
name: Finpartition.prod_eq_prod_parts
docString: A product over `s` is the iterated product over the parts of a finite partition of `s`.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {a : Finset α} (σ : Finpartition a)
  (Q : (B : Finset α) → B ∈ σ.parts → Finpartition B) {B : Finset α} (hB : B ∈ σ.parts), (σ.bind Q).restrict ⋯ = Q B hB
name: Finpartition.restrict_bind_eq
docString: Binding blockwise partitions and restricting to one original block recovers that partition.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {a : Finset α} {P P' : Finpartition a},
  P ≤ P' → ∀ {b : Finset α} (hb : b ⊆ a), P.restrict hb ≤ P'.restrict hb
name: Finpartition.restrict_mono
docString: Restriction is monotone with respect to refinement.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq α] {a : Finset α} (σ : Finpartition a) {B : Finset α} (hB : B ∈ σ.parts),
  σ.restrict ⋯ = ⊤
name: Finpartition.restrict_self_part_eq_top
docString: A partition restricted to one of its own blocks is the indiscrete partition of that block.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq α] [inst_1 : CommRing R] (m : Finset α → R) {S : Finset α}
  (π : Finpartition S),
  ∑ ρ ≤ π, (IncidenceAlgebra.mu R) ρ π * Finpartition.partitionProduct m ρ =
    Finpartition.partitionProduct (Finpartition.cumulantFromMoment m) π
name: Finpartition.sum_Iic_mu_partitionProduct_eq
docString: Möbius-weighted refinement sums factor into blockwise cumulants.

name: Finpartition.sum_Iic_partitionProduct_eq
docString: Sum of block products over refinements factors into blockwise moments.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [inst : CommSemiring R] (s : Finset α),
  ∀ a ∈ s, ∀ (f : ℕ → R), ∑ B, f (↑B).card = ∑ k ∈ Finset.range s.card, ↑((s.card - 1).choose k) * f (k + 1)
name: Finpartition.sum_blockContaining_card
docString: Reindex a cardinality-dependent sum over distinguished blocks by their size.

statement:
∀ {α : Type u_1} (T : Finset α) (R : α → α → Prop) [inst : DecidableRel R],
  {pq ∈ T.product T | R pq.1 pq.2}.card = ∑ p ∈ T, {q ∈ T | R p q}.card
name: Finset.card_filter_product_eq_sum_card_filter

statement:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [inst : NormedCommRing R] [NormOneClass R] [CompleteSpace R] [inst_3 : Fintype ι]
  (f : ι → ℕ → R) (a : ι → R),
  (∀ (i : ι), HasSum (f i) (a i)) → (∀ (i : ι), Summable fun k => ‖f i k‖) → HasSum (fun n => ∏ i, f i (n i)) (∏ i, a i)
name: Finsupp.hasSum_prod
docString:
**A finite product of absolutely convergent series converges** as a `Finsupp`-indexed
multi-series.

statement:
∀ {R : Type u_3} [inst : NormedField R] [CompleteSpace R] {ι : Type u_4} [inst_2 : Fintype ι] (q : ι → R),
  (∀ (i : ι), ‖q i‖ < 1) → HasSum (fun n => ∏ i, q i ^ n i) (∏ i, (1 - q i)⁻¹)
name: Finsupp.hasSum_prod_geometric
docString: **The geometric-series specialization**.

statement:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype ι] (g : ι → ℕ → ℝ) (b : ι → ℝ),
  (∀ (i : ι), HasSum (g i) (b i)) → (∀ (i : ι) (n : ℕ), 0 ≤ g i n) → HasSum (fun n => ∏ i, g i (n i)) (∏ i, b i)
name: Finsupp.hasSum_prod_nonneg
docString:
**The nonnegative-real finite product of series converges** to the product of the individual
sums, as a `Finsupp`-indexed multi-series.

statement:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {H : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H]
  [Finite ι] (b : HilbertBasis ι ℂ H) (coeff : ι → ℂ), Fredholm.diagonalDet coeff = (1 + b.diagonalOp coeff).det
name: Fredholm.diagonalDet_eq_det_one_add_diagonalOp
docString:
On a finite Hilbert basis, the diagonal Fredholm determinant agrees with Mathlib's ordinary
determinant of `1 + diagonalOp b coeff`.

statement:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} (coeff : ι → ℂ) (s : Finset ι),
  (∀ i ∉ s, coeff i = 0) → Fredholm.diagonalDet coeff = ∏ i ∈ s, (1 + coeff i)
name: Fredholm.diagonalDet_eq_finsetProd
docString:
If the coefficient family vanishes outside a finite set, the Fredholm determinant reduces to
that finite product.

statement: ∀ {ι : Type u_1} (coeff : ι → ℂ), (Summable fun i => ‖coeff i‖) → (Fredholm.diagonalDet coeff = 0 ↔ ∃ i, coeff i = -1)
name: Fredholm.diagonalDet_eq_zero_iff_exists_coeff_eq_neg_one
docString:
For absolutely summable diagonal data, the determinant vanishes exactly when one coefficient is
`-1`, equivalently when one factor `1 + coeff i` vanishes.

statement: ∀ {ι : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype ι] (coeff : ι → ℂ), Fredholm.diagonalDet coeff = ∏ i, (1 + coeff i)
name: Fredholm.diagonalDet_fintype
docString:
On a finite index type, the diagonal Fredholm determinant is the ordinary finite product of the
diagonal factors.

statement: ∀ {ι : Type u_1} (coeff : ι → ℂ), (Summable fun i => ‖coeff i‖) → Multipliable fun i => 1 + coeff i
name: Fredholm.diagonalDet_multipliable
docString: Absolute summability of diagonal coefficients guarantees convergence of the defining product.

statement:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} (coeff : ι → ℂ),
  (Summable fun i => ‖coeff i‖) → (∀ (i : ι), 1 + coeff i ≠ 0) → Fredholm.diagonalDet coeff ≠ 0
name: Fredholm.diagonalDet_ne_zero
docString: If no diagonal factor vanishes, the absolutely convergent determinant is nonzero.

statement:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2} (e : κ ≃ ι) (coeff : ι → ℂ),
  Fredholm.diagonalDet (coeff ∘ ⇑e) = Fredholm.diagonalDet coeff
name: Fredholm.diagonalDet_reindex
docString: Equivalent enumerations of the same diagonal coefficients give the same determinant.

statement: ∀ {ι : Type u_1}, (Fredholm.diagonalDet fun x => 0) = 1
name: Fredholm.diagonalDet_zero
docString: The determinant of the zero diagonal perturbation is one.

statement:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {H : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H]
  (b : HilbertBasis ι ℂ H) (a : ι → ℝ),
  (Summable fun i => ‖a i‖) → (∀ (i : ι), 0 ≤ a i) → (b.diagonalOp fun i => ↑(a i)).SpectralTraceClass
name: HilbertBasis.diagonalOpSpectralTraceClass
docString: Bundle a diagonal operator with summable nonnegative real weights as spectral-trace-class.

statement:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {H : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
  [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H] (b : HilbertBasis ι ℂ H) (a : ι → ℝ) (ha : Summable fun i => ‖a i‖)
  (ha_nonneg : ∀ (i : ι), 0 ≤ a i), ⋯.trace = ∑' (i : ι), a i
name: HilbertBasis.diagonalOpSpectralTraceClass_trace
docString: The spectral trace of a diagonal operator with nonnegative weights is their sum.

statement:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {H : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H]
  (b : HilbertBasis ι ℂ H) (a : ι → ℂ), (Summable fun i => ‖a i‖) → ∀ (j : ι), (b.diagonalOp a) (b j) = a j • b j
name: HilbertBasis.diagonalOp_apply_basis
docString: The diagonal operator acts on each basis vector by its corresponding coefficient.

statement:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {H : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H]
  (b : HilbertBasis ι ℂ H) (a : ι → ℂ), (Summable fun i => ‖a i‖) → IsCompactOperator ⇑(b.diagonalOp a)
name: HilbertBasis.diagonalOp_isCompact
docString: A diagonal operator with absolutely summable coefficients is compact.

statement:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {H : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H]
  (b : HilbertBasis ι ℂ H) (a : ι → ℝ),
  (Summable fun i => ‖a i‖) → (∀ (i : ι), 0 ≤ a i) → (b.diagonalOp fun i => ↑(a i)).IsPositive
name: HilbertBasis.diagonalOp_isPositive
docString: A diagonal operator with summable real nonnegative coefficients is positive.

statement:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {H : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
  [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H] (b : HilbertBasis ι ℂ H) (a : ι → ℝ),
  (Summable fun i => ‖a i‖) → (∀ (i : ι), 0 ≤ a i) → IsSelfAdjoint (b.diagonalOp fun i => ↑(a i))
name: HilbertBasis.diagonalOp_isSelfAdjoint
docString: A diagonal operator with summable real nonnegative coefficients is self-adjoint.

statement:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {H : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] (b : HilbertBasis ι ℂ H)
  (a : ι → ℂ) (i : ι), IsCompactOperator ⇑(b.diagonalTerm a i)
name: HilbertBasis.diagonalTerm_isCompact
docString: Every term of the diagonal operator series is compact.

statement:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {H : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H]
  (b : HilbertBasis ι ℂ H) (a : ι → ℂ), (Summable fun i => ‖a i‖) → HasSum (b.diagonalTerm a) (b.diagonalOp a)
name: HilbertBasis.hasSum_diagonalTerm
docString: The defining diagonal rank-one series converges to `diagonalOp`.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] {ι : Type u_2} (d : HilbertBasis ι ℂ H)
  (x : H), HasSum (fun i => ‖inner ℂ x (d i)‖ ^ 2) (‖x‖ ^ 2)
name: HilbertBasis.hasSum_norm_sq_inner
docString:
**Parseval's identity for a Hilbert basis, in norm-squared form.** For any `x : H`, the
squared-magnitude Fourier coefficients of `x` against a Hilbert basis `d` sum unconditionally to
`‖x‖ ^ 2`.

statement:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {H : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H]
  (b : HilbertBasis ι ℂ H) (coeff : ι → ℂ),
  (Summable fun i => ‖coeff i‖) → ∀ (i : ι), (1 + b.diagonalOp coeff) (b i) = (1 + coeff i) • b i
name: HilbertBasis.one_add_diagonalOp_apply_basis
docString: `1 + diagonalOp b coeff` acts diagonally with factors `1 + coeff i`.

statement:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {H : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H]
  (b : HilbertBasis ι ℂ H) (coeff : ι → ℂ),
  (Summable fun i => ‖coeff i‖) → ∀ (i : ι), coeff i = -1 → ∃ x, x ≠ 0 ∧ (1 + b.diagonalOp coeff) x = 0
name: HilbertBasis.one_add_diagonalOp_has_nonzero_kernel_vector_of_coeff_eq_neg_one
docString:
A coefficient `coeff i = -1` produces a nonzero kernel vector of
`1 + diagonalOp b coeff`.

statement:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {H : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H]
  (b : HilbertBasis ι ℂ H) (coeff : ι → ℂ),
  (Summable fun i => ‖coeff i‖) → Fredholm.diagonalDet coeff = 0 → ∃ x, x ≠ 0 ∧ (1 + b.diagonalOp coeff) x = 0
name: HilbertBasis.one_add_diagonalOp_has_nonzero_kernel_vector_of_diagonalDet_eq_zero
docString:
Vanishing of the absolutely summable diagonal Fredholm determinant produces a nonzero kernel
vector of `1 + diagonalOp b coeff`.

statement:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {H : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H]
  (b : HilbertBasis ι ℂ H) (a : ι → ℂ), (Summable fun i => ‖a i‖) → Summable (b.diagonalTerm a)
name: HilbertBasis.summable_diagonalTerm
docString:
Absolute summability of the coefficients implies summability of the diagonal rank-one
operator series in operator norm.

statement:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {S : Type u_2} {α : Type u_3} [inst : Ring R] [inst_1 : Ring S] [inst_2 : PartialOrder α]
  [inst_3 : LocallyFiniteOrder α] [inst_4 : DecidableEq α] (φ : R →+* S) (x y : α),
  φ ((IncidenceAlgebra.mu R) x y) = (IncidenceAlgebra.mu S) x y
name: IncidenceAlgebra.map_mu_apply
docString: Ring homomorphisms preserve the Möbius function.

statement:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {α : Type u_2} {β : Type u_3} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : PartialOrder α] [inst_2 : PartialOrder β]
  [inst_3 : LocallyFiniteOrder α] [inst_4 : LocallyFiniteOrder β] [inst_5 : DecidableEq α] [inst_6 : DecidableEq β]
  (e : α ≃o β) (x y : α), (IncidenceAlgebra.mu R) (e x) (e y) = (IncidenceAlgebra.mu R) x y
name: IncidenceAlgebra.mu_orderIso_apply
docString: The Möbius function is invariant under an order isomorphism.

statement:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_2} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : DecidableEq ι] (β : ι → Type u_3)
  [inst_2 : (i : ι) → PartialOrder (β i)] [inst_3 : (i : ι) → LocallyFiniteOrder (β i)]
  [inst_4 : (i : ι) → DecidableEq (β i)] (t : Finset ι) (x y : (i : ↥t) → β ↑i),
  (IncidenceAlgebra.mu R) x y = ∏ i, (IncidenceAlgebra.mu R) (x i) (y i)
name: IncidenceAlgebra.mu_pi_finset_apply
docString:
The Möbius function of a finite dependent product is the product of the factor Möbius
functions.

statement:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {α : Type u_2} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : Fintype α] [inst_2 : PartialOrder α]
  [inst_3 : LocallyFiniteOrder α] [inst_4 : DecidableEq α] {z : α} (x y : { t // z ≤ t }),
  (IncidenceAlgebra.mu R) x y = (IncidenceAlgebra.mu R) ↑x ↑y
name: IncidenceAlgebra.mu_subtype_ge_apply
docString:
The Möbius function computed in a finite principal upper interval agrees with the ambient
Möbius function.

statement:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {α : Type u_2} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : Fintype α] [inst_2 : PartialOrder α]
  [inst_3 : LocallyFiniteOrder α] [inst_4 : DecidableEq α] {z : α} (x y : { t // t ≤ z }),
  (IncidenceAlgebra.mu R) x y = (IncidenceAlgebra.mu R) ↑x ↑y
name: IncidenceAlgebra.mu_subtype_le_apply
docString:
The Möbius function computed in a finite principal lower interval agrees with the ambient
Möbius function.

statement:
∀ (u v : InternalSpace.PauliAxis → ℂ),
  u ⬝ᵥ v =
    u InternalSpace.PauliAxis.x * v InternalSpace.PauliAxis.x +
        u InternalSpace.PauliAxis.y * v InternalSpace.PauliAxis.y +
      u InternalSpace.PauliAxis.z * v InternalSpace.PauliAxis.z
name: InternalSpace.dotProduct_pauliAxis
docString:
The ordinary bilinear dot product on Pauli coefficients is the sum of the three semantic
components. No complex conjugation is introduced.

statement:
∀ (a b : ℂ) (u v : InternalSpace.PauliAxis → ℂ),
  (a • 1 + InternalSpace.pauliCombination u) * (b • 1 + InternalSpace.pauliCombination v) =
    (a * b + u ⬝ᵥ v) • 1 + InternalSpace.pauliCombination (a • v + b • u + Complex.I • InternalSpace.pauliCross u v)
name: InternalSpace.pauliAffine_mul_pauliAffine
docString: Product of two scalar-plus-Pauli forms.

statement:
∀ (u v : InternalSpace.PauliAxis → ℂ),
  InternalSpace.pauliCombination (u + v) = InternalSpace.pauliCombination u + InternalSpace.pauliCombination v
name: InternalSpace.pauliCombination_add
docString: Pauli synthesis commutes with addition of indexed coefficient families.

statement:
∀ (u v : InternalSpace.PauliAxis → ℂ),
  InternalSpace.pauliCombination u * InternalSpace.pauliCombination v =
    (u ⬝ᵥ v) • 1 + Complex.I • InternalSpace.pauliCombination (InternalSpace.pauliCross u v)
name: InternalSpace.pauliCombination_mul_pauliCombination
docString:
Product of two synthesized Pauli vectors:
`(u·σ)(v·σ) = (u·v) I + i (u×v)·σ`.

statement: ∀ (u : InternalSpace.PauliAxis → ℂ), InternalSpace.pauliCombination u * InternalSpace.pauliCombination u = (u ⬝ᵥ u) • 1
name: InternalSpace.pauliCombination_mul_self
docString: The square of a Pauli synthesis is its bilinear coefficient square times the identity.

statement: ∀ (u : InternalSpace.PauliAxis → ℝ), Matrix.IsHermitian (InternalSpace.pauliCombination fun axis => ↑(u axis))
name: InternalSpace.pauliCombination_ofReal_isHermitian
docString: A Pauli synthesis with real axis coefficients is Hermitian.

statement:
∀ (c : ℂ) (u : InternalSpace.PauliAxis → ℂ),
  InternalSpace.pauliCombination (c • u) = c • InternalSpace.pauliCombination u
name: InternalSpace.pauliCombination_smul
docString: Pauli synthesis commutes with scalar multiplication of the indexed coefficient family.

statement:
∀ (a x y z : ℂ),
  a ^ 2 - x ^ 2 - y ^ 2 - z ^ 2 ≠ 0 →
    (a • 1 - (x • InternalSpace.pauliX + y • InternalSpace.pauliY + z • InternalSpace.pauliZ)) *
        (a ^ 2 - x ^ 2 - y ^ 2 - z ^ 2)⁻¹ •
          (a • 1 + (x • InternalSpace.pauliX + y • InternalSpace.pauliY + z • InternalSpace.pauliZ)) =
      1
name: InternalSpace.pauliShiftMatrix_mul_closedInverse
docString:
A coordinate Pauli shift `a I - (x σₓ + y σᵧ + z σ_z)` has the inverse-scaled companion as a
right inverse whenever its quadratic denominator is nonzero.

statement:
∀ (a : ℂ) (u : InternalSpace.PauliAxis → ℂ),
  (a • 1 - InternalSpace.pauliCombination u) * (a • 1 + InternalSpace.pauliCombination u) = (a ^ 2 - u ⬝ᵥ u) • 1
name: InternalSpace.pauliShift_mul_companion
docString:
Multiplying opposite-sign Pauli shifts eliminates the Pauli part and leaves the quadratic
bilinear invariant.

name: InternalSpace.pauliZ_one_one

name: LinearPMap.IsFormalAdjoint.im_inner_self_apply_eq_zero
docString: For a symmetric partial operator, the quadratic form `⟪x, A x⟫` is real on the domain.

statement:

name: LinearPMap.apply_nonrealResolvent_sub_smul
docString: The bounded resolvent is a right inverse of the nonreal shift.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]

    LinearPMap.approximationCoefficient✝ r •
      ((A.nonrealResolvent hA (LinearPMap.imaginaryParameter✝ r) ⋯) y +
        (A.nonrealResolvent hA (star (LinearPMap.imaginaryParameter✝ r)) ⋯) y)

statement:

name: LinearPMap.boundedSelfAdjointApproximation_apply_domain
docString:
On the original domain, the bounded generator approximation is the regularized generator:
`Aᵣ x = Jᵣ (A x)`.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]

name: LinearPMap.boundedSelfAdjointApproximation_commute
docString: Bounded self-adjoint resolvent approximants at two positive scales commute.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]

statement:

docString:
Every bounded self-adjoint resolvent approximant commutes with every nonreal resolvent of the
original self-adjoint operator.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]

docString: The bounded generator approximants converge to the original generator on its domain.

∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H] (B : H →L[ℂ] H)

statement:

statement:

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]

docString: A bounded self-adjoint exponential preserves the norm of every vector.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H] (B : H →L[ℂ] H),
  Continuous (LinearPMap.boundedUnitaryEvolution B)
name: LinearPMap.boundedUnitaryEvolution_continuous
docString:
The bounded exponential group is continuous in operator norm, hence in particular strongly
continuous on every vector.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]

statement:

docString: The operator-norm derivative of the bounded unitary evolution.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]

docString: For self-adjoint `B`, the adjoint evolution is evolution at negative time.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] (B : H →L[ℂ] H),

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]

name: LinearPMap.cayleyTransform_adjoint_comp
docString: The Cayley transform is unitary: its adjoint is a left inverse.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]

∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]

docString: The Cayley transform is unitary: its adjoint is a right inverse.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (z : ℂ) (hz : z.im ≠ 0),
  A.cayleyTransform hA z hz ∘SL A.cayleyTransform hA (star z) ⋯ = 1

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]

  A.cayleyTransform hA (star z) ⋯ ∘SL A.cayleyTransform hA z hz = 1
name: LinearPMap.cayleyTransform_conj_comp
docString: The Cayley transforms at `z` and `star z` are mutual inverses in this order.

∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (z : ℂ) (hz : z.im ≠ 0) (u : ↥A.domain),

For a densely defined symmetric partial operator, self-adjointness is equivalent to the reverse
adjoint-domain inclusion. The forward inclusion is already supplied by symmetry.

∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] {A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H}

name: LinearPMap.isSelfAdjoint_shiftDomainMap_bijective
docString: Every nonreal shift of a self-adjoint operator is bijective on its operator domain.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] {A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H}
  [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H], IsSelfAdjoint A → ∀ {z : ℂ}, z.im ≠ 0 → Function.Injective ⇑(A.shiftDomainMap z)
name: LinearPMap.isSelfAdjoint_shiftDomainMap_injective
docString: The domain-level nonreal shift of a self-adjoint operator is injective.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] {A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H}

name: LinearPMap.isSelfAdjoint_shiftDomainMap_range_dense
docString: The range of a nonreal shift of a self-adjoint operator is dense.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] {A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H}
  [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H], IsSelfAdjoint A → ∀ {z : ℂ}, z.im ≠ 0 → IsClosed (Set.range ⇑(A.shiftDomainMap z))
name: LinearPMap.isSelfAdjoint_shiftDomainMap_range_isClosed
docString:
The range of a nonreal shift of a self-adjoint operator is closed.

If `(A - z) xₙ` converges, the nonreal-shift lower bound makes `xₙ` a Cauchy sequence. Completeness
provides a limit `x`, and the closed graph of the self-adjoint operator recovers `x ∈ D(A)` together
with the limiting value of `A x`.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] {A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H}
  [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H], IsSelfAdjoint A → ∀ {z : ℂ}, z.im ≠ 0 → (A.shiftDomainMap z).rangeᗮ = ⊥
name: LinearPMap.isSelfAdjoint_shiftDomainMap_range_orthogonal_eq_bot
docString: The orthogonal complement of the range of a nonreal self-adjoint shift is trivial.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] {A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H}
  [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H], IsSelfAdjoint A → ∀ {z : ℂ}, z.im ≠ 0 → Function.Surjective ⇑(A.shiftDomainMap z)
name: LinearPMap.isSelfAdjoint_shiftDomainMap_surjective
docString: Every nonreal shift of a self-adjoint operator is surjective.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] {A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H}
  [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H], IsSelfAdjoint A → ∀ {z : ℂ}, z.im ≠ 0 → ∀ (x : ↥A.domain), ↑A x - z • ↑x = 0 ↔ x = 0
name: LinearPMap.isSelfAdjoint_sub_smul_eq_zero_iff
docString: A nonreal shift of a self-adjoint operator has trivial kernel on its domain.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (z : ℂ) (hz : z.im ≠ 0),

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (z : ℂ) (hz : z.im ≠ 0) (y : H),

∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]

name: LinearPMap.nonrealResolvent_commute
docString: `Commute`-packaged form of pairwise nonreal resolvent commutation.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (z : ℂ) (hz : z.im ≠ 0) (y : H), (A.nonrealResolvent hA z hz) y ∈ A.domain
name: LinearPMap.nonrealResolvent_mem_domain
docString: The resolvent value lies in the original unbounded operator domain.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (z w : ℂ) (hz : z.im ≠ 0) (hw : w.im ≠ 0),

name: LinearPMap.nonrealResolvent_mul_comm
docString: Bounded nonreal resolvents of one self-adjoint operator commute pairwise.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (z : ℂ) (hz : z.im ≠ 0) (x : ↥A.domain),

name: LinearPMap.nonrealResolvent_shift_apply
docString: The bounded resolvent is also a left inverse of the nonreal shift on the original domain.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (z w : ℂ) (hz : z.im ≠ 0) (hw : w.im ≠ 0) (y : H),

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (z : ℂ) (hz : z.im ≠ 0) (x : ↥A.domain),

∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]

∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (B : H →L[ℂ] H), IsSelfAdjoint B → ∀ (t : ℝ) (x : H), ‖(LinearPMap.boundedUnitaryEvolution B t) x - x‖ ≤ ‖B x‖ * |t|

The displacement under bounded self-adjoint evolution is controlled by the generator on the
initial vector.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (z : ℂ) (hz : z.im ≠ 0) (y : H),
  ‖(A.nonrealShiftInverseDomain hA z hz) y‖ ≤ |z.im|⁻¹ * ‖y‖

docString: The bounded inverse obeys the standard nonreal resolvent estimate pointwise.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (r t : ℝ) (x : ↥A.domain),
  ‖(A.resolventApproximationEvolutionAtScale hA r t) ↑x - ↑x‖ ≤ ‖↑A x‖ * |t|
name: LinearPMap.norm_resolventApproximationEvolutionAtScale_apply_sub_le_domain
docString:
On the original generator domain, every totalized bounded approximant has displacement bounded
uniformly in the approximation scale by the original generator.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (r s : ℝ) (hr : 0 < r) (hs : 0 < s) (t : ℝ) (x : H),
  ‖(A.resolventApproximationEvolution hA r hr t) x - (A.resolventApproximationEvolution hA s hs t) x‖ ≤
    ‖(A.boundedSelfAdjointApproximation hA r hr - A.boundedSelfAdjointApproximation hA s hs) x‖ * |t|
name: LinearPMap.norm_resolventApproximationEvolution_sub_le
docString: Difference estimate for the bounded resolvent-approximation evolutions.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (t : ℝ) (x : ↥A.domain),
  ‖(A.resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator hA t) ↑x - ↑x‖ ≤ ‖↑A x‖ * |t|
name: LinearPMap.norm_resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator_apply_sub_le_domain
docString:
The limiting Stone evolution inherits the domain displacement estimate
`‖U(t)x - x‖ ≤ ‖A x‖ |t|`.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (r : ℝ) (hr : 0 < r) (t : ℝ) (x : ↥A.domain),
  ‖(A.resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator hA t) ↑x - (A.resolventApproximationEvolution hA r hr t) ↑x‖ ≤
    ‖(A.boundedSelfAdjointApproximation hA r hr) ↑x - ↑A x‖ * |t|
name: LinearPMap.norm_resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator_sub_resolventApproximationEvolution_le
docString:
A fixed bounded approximating evolution differs from the limiting evolution by at most its
generator error times `|t|`, on the original generator domain.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (r : ℝ) (hr : 0 < r) (y : H), ‖(A.resolventRegularizer hA r hr) y‖ ≤ ‖y‖
name: LinearPMap.norm_resolventRegularizer_le
docString: The resolvent regularizers are contractions, uniformly in the positive scale `r`.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (r : ℝ) (hr : 0 < r) (x : ↥A.domain),
  ‖(A.resolventRegularizer hA r hr) ↑x - ↑x‖ ≤ r⁻¹ * ‖↑A x‖
name: LinearPMap.norm_resolventRegularizer_sub_le
docString: Quantitative domain estimate for the regularizer error.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (r t s : ℝ),
  A.resolventApproximationEvolutionAtScale hA r (t + s) =
    A.resolventApproximationEvolutionAtScale hA r t * A.resolventApproximationEvolutionAtScale hA r s
name: LinearPMap.resolventApproximationEvolutionAtScale_add
docString: The totalized bounded approximants retain the additive one-parameter group law.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (t : ℝ) (x : H),
  CauchySeq fun r => (A.resolventApproximationEvolutionAtScale hA r t) x
name: LinearPMap.resolventApproximationEvolutionAtScale_apply_cauchySeq
docString:
For every fixed time and vector, the totalized resolvent approximations are a Cauchy sequence
as the real scale tends to `+∞`.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (r t : ℝ) (x : H), ‖(A.resolventApproximationEvolutionAtScale hA r t) x‖ = ‖x‖
name: LinearPMap.resolventApproximationEvolutionAtScale_apply_norm
docString: The totalized bounded approximating evolution preserves vector norms.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (r t : ℝ) (x y : H),

    dist x y
name: LinearPMap.resolventApproximationEvolutionAtScale_dist_eq
docString: The totalized bounded approximants preserve distances.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]

name: LinearPMap.resolventApproximationEvolutionAtScale_nonrealResolvent_commute
docString: The totalized positive-scale bounded evolution commutes with every nonreal resolvent.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (r : ℝ), A.resolventApproximationEvolutionAtScale hA r 0 = 1
name: LinearPMap.resolventApproximationEvolutionAtScale_zero
docString: The totalized bounded approximants retain the zero-time identity.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (r : ℝ) (hr : 0 < r) (t s : ℝ),

name: LinearPMap.resolventApproximationEvolution_add
docString: Each bounded resolvent approximation gives a one-parameter group.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (r : ℝ) (hr : 0 < r) (t : ℝ) (x : H),
