    ((A.resolventApproximationEvolution hA r hr t * -Complex.I • A.boundedSelfAdjointApproximation hA r hr) x) t
name: LinearPMap.resolventApproximationEvolution_apply_hasDerivAt
docString: The resolvent-approximating evolution satisfies its bounded-generator equation vectorwise.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (x : H) (t ε : ℝ),
  0 < ε →
    ∃ R,
      0 < R ∧
        ∀ (r s : ℝ),
          R ≤ r →
            R ≤ s →
              ∀ (hr : 0 < r) (hs : 0 < s),
                ‖(A.resolventApproximationEvolution hA r hr t) x - (A.resolventApproximationEvolution hA s hs t) x‖ < ε
name: LinearPMap.resolventApproximationEvolution_cauchy
docString:
The resolvent-approximating evolutions are strongly Cauchy on every vector, not only on the
original generator domain.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (r : ℝ) (hr : 0 < r), Continuous (A.resolventApproximationEvolution hA r hr)
name: LinearPMap.resolventApproximationEvolution_continuous
docString: Each approximating unitary group is continuous in operator norm.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (r : ℝ) (hr : 0 < r) (t : ℝ) (x y : H),
  dist ((A.resolventApproximationEvolution hA r hr t) x) ((A.resolventApproximationEvolution hA r hr t) y) = dist x y
name: LinearPMap.resolventApproximationEvolution_dist_eq
docString: Each resolvent-approximating unitary evolution is an isometry.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (x : ↥A.domain) (t ε : ℝ),
  0 < ε →
    ∃ R,
      0 < R ∧
        ∀ (r s : ℝ),
          R ≤ r →
            R ≤ s →
              ∀ (hr : 0 < r) (hs : 0 < s),
                ‖(A.resolventApproximationEvolution hA r hr t) ↑x - (A.resolventApproximationEvolution hA s hs t) ↑x‖ <
                  ε
name: LinearPMap.resolventApproximationEvolution_domain_cauchy
docString:
On the original domain, the bounded resolvent evolutions are strongly Cauchy at each fixed
real time.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (r : ℝ) (hr : 0 < r) (t : ℝ),
  HasDerivAt (fun τ => A.resolventApproximationEvolution hA r hr τ)
    (A.resolventApproximationEvolution hA r hr t * -Complex.I • A.boundedSelfAdjointApproximation hA r hr) t
name: LinearPMap.resolventApproximationEvolution_hasDerivAt
docString:
The bounded approximating evolution satisfies its bounded-generator differential equation in
operator norm.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (r : ℝ) (hr : 0 < r) (t : ℝ),
  A.resolventApproximationEvolution hA r hr t * star (A.resolventApproximationEvolution hA r hr t) = 1
name: LinearPMap.resolventApproximationEvolution_mul_star
docString: The approximating evolution is unitary, right-inverse form.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (r : ℝ) (hr : 0 < r) (t : ℝ) (z : ℂ) (hz : z.im ≠ 0),
  Commute (A.resolventApproximationEvolution hA r hr t) (A.nonrealResolvent hA z hz)
name: LinearPMap.resolventApproximationEvolution_nonrealResolvent_commute
docString:
Exponentiating a bounded resolvent approximant preserves its commutation with every nonreal
resolvent.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (r : ℝ) (hr : 0 < r) (t : ℝ),

name: LinearPMap.resolventApproximationEvolution_star
docString: The adjoint of an approximating evolution reverses time.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (r : ℝ) (hr : 0 < r) (t : ℝ),
  star (A.resolventApproximationEvolution hA r hr t) * A.resolventApproximationEvolution hA r hr t = 1
name: LinearPMap.resolventApproximationEvolution_star_mul
docString: The approximating evolution is unitary, left-inverse form.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (r : ℝ) (hr : 0 < r), A.resolventApproximationEvolution hA r hr 0 = 1
name: LinearPMap.resolventApproximationEvolution_zero

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (t s : ℝ),
  A.resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator hA (t + s) =
    A.resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator hA t * A.resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator hA s
name: LinearPMap.resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator_add
docString: The bundled strong-limit operators form an additive one-parameter group.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (t : ℝ),
  ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (A.resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator hA t) =
    A.resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator hA (-t)
name: LinearPMap.resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator_adjoint
docString: The Hilbert-space adjoint of the limiting evolution is negative-time evolution.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (t : ℝ) (x : H),
  (A.resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator hA t) x = A.resolventEvolutionStrongLimit hA t x
name: LinearPMap.resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator_apply

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (x : H), Continuous fun t => (A.resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator hA t) x
name: LinearPMap.resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator_apply_continuous
docString: The limiting unitary group is strongly continuous: every orbit `t ↦ U(t)x` is continuous.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (x : H) (s : ℝ),
  ContinuousAt (fun t => (A.resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator hA t) x) s
name: LinearPMap.resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator_apply_continuousAt
docString: The limiting evolution is strongly continuous at every time, for every vector.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (y : H),
  ContinuousAt (fun t => (A.resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator hA t) y) 0
name: LinearPMap.resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator_apply_continuousAt_zero
docString: The limiting evolution is continuous at time zero on every Hilbert-space vector.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (x : ↥A.domain),
  ContinuousAt (fun t => (A.resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator hA t) ↑x) 0
name: LinearPMap.resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator_apply_continuousAt_zero_domain
docString: For a vector in the generator domain, the limiting evolution is continuous at time zero.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (t : ℝ) (x : ↥A.domain),
  ↑A ⟨(A.resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator hA t) ↑x, ⋯⟩ = (A.resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator hA t) (↑A x)
name: LinearPMap.resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator_apply_domain
docString:
On its original domain, the unbounded self-adjoint generator intertwines with the limiting
Stone evolution.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (x : ↥A.domain) (t : ℝ),

name: LinearPMap.resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator_apply_hasDerivAt
docString: Strong Stone derivative on the preserved generator domain.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (x : ↥A.domain) (s : ℝ),

    (-Complex.I • (A.resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator hA s) (↑A x)) s
name: LinearPMap.resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator_apply_hasDerivAt_intertwined
docString:
The limiting evolution satisfies its strong generator equation at arbitrary time, with the
right-hand side written as the evolved generator.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (x : ↥A.domain),
  HasDerivAt (fun t => (A.resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator hA t) ↑x) (-Complex.I • ↑A x) 0
name: LinearPMap.resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator_apply_hasDerivAt_zero
docString: At zero time, the strong Stone evolution has infinitesimal generator `-i A` on `A.domain`.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (t : ℝ) (x y : H),
  dist ((A.resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator hA t) x) ((A.resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator hA t) y) = dist x y
name: LinearPMap.resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator_dist_eq
docString: The bundled limiting evolution is an isometry.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (t s : ℝ) (x : H),
  dist ((A.resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator hA t) x) ((A.resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator hA s) x) =
    dist ((A.resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator hA (t - s)) x) x
name: LinearPMap.resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator_dist_time_eq_sub
docString:
Time differences for the limiting unitary group reduce isometrically to a displacement from
zero time.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (t : ℝ) (x y : H),

    inner ℂ x y
name: LinearPMap.resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator_inner_map_map
docString: The limiting evolution preserves the Hilbert-space inner product.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (t : ℝ) (x : ↥A.domain),
  (A.resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator hA t) ↑x ∈ A.domain
name: LinearPMap.resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator_mem_domain
docString: The limiting Stone evolution preserves the original self-adjoint operator domain.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (t : ℝ),

name: LinearPMap.resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator_mul_neg
docString: Negative time is a right inverse.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (t : ℝ),
  A.resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator hA t * star (A.resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator hA t) = 1
name: LinearPMap.resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator_mul_star
docString: The limiting evolution is unitary, right-inverse form.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (t : ℝ),

name: LinearPMap.resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator_neg_mul
docString: Negative time is a left inverse.

name: LinearPMap.resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator_nonrealResolvent_apply
docString: Nonreal resolvent commutation passes through the vectorwise strong limit.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (t : ℝ) (z : ℂ) (hz : z.im ≠ 0),

name: LinearPMap.resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator_nonrealResolvent_mul_comm
docString: Operator form of nonreal resolvent commutation for the limiting Stone evolution.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (t : ℝ),
  star (A.resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator hA t) = A.resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator hA (-t)
name: LinearPMap.resolventEvolutionStrongLimitOperator_star
docString: Star/adjoint reverses time for the limiting evolution.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]

  ℏ ≠ 0 →
    ∀ {s : Set ℝ} {bound : ℝ → ℝ} (ψ : ℝ → SchwartzMap ℝ ℂ) {ψt : ℝ → ℝ → ℂ} {potential : ℝ → ℝ},
      s ∈ nhds t →
        (∀ τ ∈ s,
            MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable
              (fun x => QuantumMechanics.SingleParticle.Continuum.probabilityDensityValue ((ψ τ) x))
              MeasureTheory.volume) →
          MeasureTheory.Integrable
              (fun x => QuantumMechanics.SingleParticle.Continuum.probabilityDensityValue ((ψ t) x))
              MeasureTheory.volume →
            MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable
                (fun x =>
                  QuantumMechanics.SingleParticle.Continuum.probabilityDensityTimeDerivativeValue ((ψ t) x) (ψt t x))
                MeasureTheory.volume →
              (∀ (x τ : ℝ),
                  τ ∈ s →
                    ‖QuantumMechanics.SingleParticle.Continuum.probabilityDensityTimeDerivativeValue ((ψ τ) x)
                          (ψt τ x)‖ ≤
                      bound x) →
                MeasureTheory.Integrable bound MeasureTheory.volume →
                  (∀ (x τ : ℝ), τ ∈ s → HasDerivAt (fun u => ((ψ u) x).re) (ψt τ x).re τ) →
                    (∀ (x τ : ℝ), τ ∈ s → HasDerivAt (fun u => ((ψ u) x).im) (ψt τ x).im τ) →
                      (∀ (x : ℝ),
                          Complex.I * ↑ℏ * ψt t x =
                            -↑κ *
                                (QuantumMechanics.SingleParticle.Continuum.schwartzSpatialSecondDerivative1D (ψ t)) x +
                              ↑(potential x) * (ψ t) x) →
                        deriv (fun τ => QuantumMechanics.SingleParticle.Continuum.totalProbability1D ⇑(ψ τ)) t = 0

∀ (t ℏ κ : ℝ),
  ℏ ≠ 0 →
    ∀ {s : Set ℝ} {bound : ℝ → ℝ} (ψ : ℝ → SchwartzMap ℝ ℂ) {ψt : ℝ → ℝ → ℂ} {potential : ℝ → ℝ},
      s ∈ nhds t →
        (∀ τ ∈ s,
            MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable
              (fun x => QuantumMechanics.SingleParticle.Continuum.probabilityDensityValue ((ψ τ) x))
              MeasureTheory.volume) →
          MeasureTheory.Integrable
              (fun x => QuantumMechanics.SingleParticle.Continuum.probabilityDensityValue ((ψ t) x))
              MeasureTheory.volume →
            MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable
                (fun x =>
                  QuantumMechanics.SingleParticle.Continuum.probabilityDensityTimeDerivativeValue ((ψ t) x) (ψt t x))
                MeasureTheory.volume →
              (∀ (x τ : ℝ),
                  τ ∈ s →
                    ‖QuantumMechanics.SingleParticle.Continuum.probabilityDensityTimeDerivativeValue ((ψ τ) x)
                          (ψt τ x)‖ ≤
                      bound x) →
                MeasureTheory.Integrable bound MeasureTheory.volume →
                  (∀ (x τ : ℝ), τ ∈ s → HasDerivAt (fun u => ((ψ u) x).re) (ψt τ x).re τ) →
                    (∀ (x τ : ℝ), τ ∈ s → HasDerivAt (fun u => ((ψ u) x).im) (ψt τ x).im τ) →
                      (∀ (x : ℝ),
                          Complex.I * ↑ℏ * ψt t x =
                            -↑κ *
                                (QuantumMechanics.SingleParticle.Continuum.schwartzSpatialSecondDerivative1D (ψ t)) x +
                              ↑(potential x) * (ψ t) x) →
                        HasDerivAt (fun τ => QuantumMechanics.SingleParticle.Continuum.totalProbability1D ⇑(ψ τ)) 0 t

∀ (a b t q ℏ mass : ℝ),
  ℏ ≠ 0 →
    mass ≠ 0 →
      ∀ {s : Set ℝ} {bound test vectorPotential vectorPotentialDerivative : ℝ → ℝ} {ψ ψt : ℝ → ℝ → ℂ} {ψx ψxx : ℝ → ℂ}
        {scalarPotential : ℝ → ℝ},
        tsupport test ⊆ Set.Ioo a b →
          Differentiable ℝ test →
            s ∈ nhds t →
              (∀ τ ∈ s,
                  MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable
                    (fun x => test x * QuantumMechanics.SingleParticle.Continuum.probabilityDensityValue (ψ τ x))
                    (MeasureTheory.volume.restrict (Set.uIoc a b))) →
                IntervalIntegrable
                    (fun x => test x * QuantumMechanics.SingleParticle.Continuum.probabilityDensityValue (ψ t x))
                    MeasureTheory.volume a b →
                  MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable
                      (fun x =>
                        test x *
                          QuantumMechanics.SingleParticle.Continuum.probabilityDensityTimeDerivativeValue (ψ t x)
                            (ψt t x))
                      (MeasureTheory.volume.restrict (Set.uIoc a b)) →
                    (∀ x ∈ Set.uIoc a b,
                        ∀ τ ∈ s,
                          ‖test x *
                                QuantumMechanics.SingleParticle.Continuum.probabilityDensityTimeDerivativeValue (ψ τ x)
                                  (ψt τ x)‖ ≤
                            bound x) →
                      IntervalIntegrable bound MeasureTheory.volume a b →
                        (∀ x ∈ Set.uIoc a b, ∀ τ ∈ s, HasDerivAt (fun u => (ψ u x).re) (ψt τ x).re τ) →
                          (∀ x ∈ Set.uIoc a b, ∀ τ ∈ s, HasDerivAt (fun u => (ψ u x).im) (ψt τ x).im τ) →
                            (∀ x ∈ Set.uIcc a b, HasDerivAt vectorPotential (vectorPotentialDerivative x) x) →
                              (∀ x ∈ Set.uIcc a b, HasDerivAt (fun y => (ψ t y).re) (ψx x).re x) →
                                (∀ x ∈ Set.uIcc a b, HasDerivAt (fun y => (ψ t y).im) (ψx x).im x) →
                                  (∀ x ∈ Set.uIcc a b, HasDerivAt (fun y => (ψx y).re) (ψxx x).re x) →
                                    (∀ x ∈ Set.uIcc a b, HasDerivAt (fun y => (ψx y).im) (ψxx x).im x) →
                                      (∀ (x : ℝ),
                                          Complex.I * ↑ℏ * ψt t x =
                                            QuantumMechanics.SingleParticle.Continuum.minimallyCoupledSchrodingerRhsValue1D
                                              q ℏ mass (vectorPotential x) (vectorPotentialDerivative x)
                                              (scalarPotential x) (ψ t x) (ψx x) (ψxx x)) →
                                        IntervalIntegrable (deriv test) MeasureTheory.volume a b →
                                          IntervalIntegrable
                                              (fun x =>
                                                QuantumMechanics.SingleParticle.Continuum.electromagneticProbabilityCurrentDivergenceValue1D
                                                  q ℏ mass (vectorPotential x) (vectorPotentialDerivative x) (ψ t x)
                                                  (ψx x) (ψxx x))
                                              MeasureTheory.volume a b →
                                            HasDerivAt
                                              (fun τ =>
                                                QuantumMechanics.SingleParticle.Continuum.wholeSpaceSmearedProbabilityDensity1D
                                                  test (ψ τ))
                                              (QuantumMechanics.SingleParticle.Continuum.wholeSpaceSmearedCurrentPairing1D
                                                (deriv test) fun x =>
                                                QuantumMechanics.SingleParticle.Continuum.electromagneticProbabilityCurrentValue1D
                                                  q ℏ mass (vectorPotential x) (ψ t x) (ψx x))
                                              t

docString:
Under the explicit dominated time-differentiation hypotheses, the scalar-potential Schrödinger
equation gives the derivative of the whole-space compactly supported smeared density:

`d/dt ∫ test * ρ = ∫ (deriv test) * j`.

The support condition is stated as `tsupport test ⊆ Ioo a b`, making the compact support window and
the disappearance of the boundary current explicit at the theorem boundary.

The `L²` expectation of the bounded charge-density observable is exactly the complexification of
`∫ test(x) q |ψ(x)|² dx`.

This is the analytic one-particle charge-density identity required by #1093. The only operator-domain
hypothesis is the explicit `L∞` boundedness of the real test function.

docString:
The expectation of multiplication by a bounded real test function is the complexification of
its whole-space smeared probability density:

`⟪ψ, M_test ψ⟫ = ∫ test(x) |ψ(x)|² dx`.

The `MemLp ... ∞` hypothesis is the explicit boundedness condition needed to make `M_test` a bounded
operator on all of `L²`.

  IntervalIntegrable (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.timeDependentInteractionPerturbation system V) MeasureTheory.volume 0
      t →
    expectation.toContinuousLinearMap
        (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.heisenbergEvolution system A t *
            QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.timeDependentPropagatorFirstVariation system V t -
          QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.timeDependentPropagatorFirstVariation system V t *
            QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.heisenbergEvolution system A t) =

        ∫ (s : ℝ) in 0..t,
          expectation.toContinuousLinearMap
            (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.heisenbergEvolution system A t *
                QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.timeDependentInteractionPerturbation system V s -
              QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.timeDependentInteractionPerturbation system V s *
                QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.heisenbergEvolution system A t)

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (system : QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.BoundedFreeSystem H)
  (expectation : QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.NormalizedExpectation H) {V : ℝ → H →L[ℂ] H},
  (∀ (s : ℝ), IsSelfAdjoint (V s)) →
    ∀ (A₀ A₁ : H →L[ℂ] H) {β M t : ℝ},
      0 ≤ M →
        (∀ s ∈ Set.Icc 0 β, ‖QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.timeDependentInteractionPerturbation system V s‖ ≤ M) →
          t ∈ Set.Icc 0 β →
            IntervalIntegrable (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.timeDependentInteractionPerturbation system V)
                MeasureTheory.volume 0 t →
              HasDerivAt
                (fun lam => QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.affinePerturbedExpectation system expectation V A₀ A₁ lam t)
                ((-(Complex.I / ↑system.hbar) •
                    ∫ (s : ℝ) in 0..t,
                      expectation.toContinuousLinearMap
                        (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.heisenbergEvolution system A₀ t *
                            QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.timeDependentInteractionPerturbation system V s -
                          QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.timeDependentInteractionPerturbation system V s *
                            QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.heisenbergEvolution system A₀ t)) +
                  expectation.toContinuousLinearMap (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.heisenbergEvolution system A₁ t))
                0

is the usual commutator integral plus the explicit observable-variation/contact contribution.

∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]

  (expectation : QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.NormalizedExpectation H) (f : ℝ → ℝ) {B : H →L[ℂ] H},
  IsSelfAdjoint B →
    ∀ (A₀ A₁ : H →L[ℂ] H) {β M t : ℝ},
      0 ≤ M →
        (∀ s ∈ Set.Icc 0 β,
            ‖QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.timeDependentInteractionPerturbation system
                  (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.sourceCoupledPerturbation f B) s‖ ≤
              M) →
          t ∈ Set.Icc 0 β →
            IntervalIntegrable
                (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.timeDependentInteractionPerturbation system
                  (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.sourceCoupledPerturbation f B))
                MeasureTheory.volume 0 t →
              HasDerivAt
                (fun lam =>
                  QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.affinePerturbedExpectation system expectation
                    (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.sourceCoupledPerturbation f B) A₀ A₁ lam t)
                ((∫ (s : ℝ) in 0..t,
                    ↑(f s) * QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.retardedSusceptibility system expectation A₀ B t s) +
                  expectation.toContinuousLinearMap (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.heisenbergEvolution system A₁ t))
                0

docString: Scalar-source specialization written as a causal retarded response plus the contact term.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]

  (expectation : QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.NormalizedExpectation H) (f : ℝ → ℝ) {B : H →L[ℂ] H},
  IsSelfAdjoint B →
    ∀ (A : H →L[ℂ] H) {β M t : ℝ},
      0 ≤ M →
        (∀ s ∈ Set.Icc 0 β,
            ‖QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.timeDependentInteractionPerturbation system
                  (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.sourceCoupledPerturbation f B) s‖ ≤
              M) →
          t ∈ Set.Icc 0 β →
            IntervalIntegrable
                (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.timeDependentInteractionPerturbation system
                  (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.sourceCoupledPerturbation f B))
                MeasureTheory.volume 0 t →
              HasDerivAt
                (fun lam =>
                  (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.timeDependentPerturbedExpectationFunctional system expectation
                      (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.sourceCoupledPerturbation f B) lam t)
                    A)
                ((Complex.I / ↑system.hbar) •
                  ∫ (s : ℝ) in 0..t,
                    ↑(f s) *
                      expectation.toContinuousLinearMap
                        (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.heisenbergEvolution system A t *
                            QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.heisenbergEvolution system B s -
                          QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.heisenbergEvolution system B s *
                            QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.heisenbergEvolution system A t))
                0

`H_λ(t) = H₀ - λ f(t) B`.

statement:

statement:

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]

For a finite spectral index, the countable-series definition reduces to the usual finite
double sum.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  {ι : Type u_2} (system : QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.BoundedFreeSystem H)
  (data : QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.PurePointLehmannData system ι) (A B : H →L[ℂ] H) (τ : ℝ) (mn : ι × ι),
  QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.purePointTimeDomainTerm system data A B τ mn =

docString: The physical transition term written with the explicit energy-difference exponential.

statement:

statement:

docString: The two ordered transition sums combine into the physical `(pₘ - pₙ)` transition series.

Under stationarity, the retarded kernel is the causal extension of a one-time-difference

On the causal half-line, the retarded kernel equals the countable pure-point transition

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (system : QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.BoundedFreeSystem H)
  (expectation : QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.NormalizedExpectation H) (f : ℝ → ℝ) (B A : H →L[ℂ] H) (t : ℝ),
  -(Complex.I / ↑system.hbar) •
      ∫ (s : ℝ) in 0..t,
        expectation.toContinuousLinearMap
          (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.heisenbergEvolution system A t *
              QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.timeDependentInteractionPerturbation system
                (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.sourceCoupledPerturbation f B) s -
            QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.timeDependentInteractionPerturbation system
                (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.sourceCoupledPerturbation f B) s *
              QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.heisenbergEvolution system A t) =
    (Complex.I / ↑system.hbar) •
      ∫ (s : ℝ) in 0..t,
        ↑(f s) *
          expectation.toContinuousLinearMap
            (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.heisenbergEvolution system A t *
                QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.heisenbergEvolution system B s -
              QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.heisenbergEvolution system B s *
                QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.heisenbergEvolution system A t)
name: QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.sourceCoupled_responseIntegral_eq
docString:
Substituting `V(t) = -f(t) B` into the general response integral produces the conventional
positive `i/ℏ` prefactor.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (system : QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.BoundedFreeSystem H)
  (expectation : QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.NormalizedExpectation H) (f : ℝ → ℝ) (B A : H →L[ℂ] H) {t : ℝ},
  0 ≤ t →
    (Complex.I / ↑system.hbar) •
        ∫ (s : ℝ) in 0..t,
          ↑(f s) *
            expectation.toContinuousLinearMap
              (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.heisenbergEvolution system A t *
                  QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.heisenbergEvolution system B s -
                QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.heisenbergEvolution system B s *
                  QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.heisenbergEvolution system A t) =
      ∫ (s : ℝ) in 0..t, ↑(f s) * QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.retardedSusceptibility system expectation A B t s

docString:
The scalar-source response integral is the causal convolution with the retarded
susceptibility.

    ∀ (lam : ℝ) {β M t : ℝ},
      0 ≤ β →
        0 ≤ M →
          Continuous (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.timeDependentInteractionPerturbation system V) →

              t ∈ Set.Icc 0 β →
                star (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.timeDependentInteractionPropagator system V lam t) *
                    QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.timeDependentInteractionPropagator system V lam t =
                  1

For a pointwise Hermitian perturbation, the interaction-picture Dyson propagator satisfies
`U(t)† U(t) = 1` on the compact nonnegative interval where the Volterra hypotheses hold.

            ensemble.freeGreenOfRegulator energy regulator
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble.configurationGreenOfRegulator_eq_secondOrder_add_exactRemainder_right
docString: Exact right-oriented second-order Dyson expansion at an arbitrary nonzero signed regulator.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} {Ω : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
  [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H] [inst_3 : Fintype Ω] (ensemble : QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble)
  (kernel : H →L[ℂ] H),
  ensemble.exactSecondMoment kernel =
    ensemble.operatorAverage fun ω => ↑(ensemble.impurityPotential ω) * kernel * ↑(ensemble.impurityPotential ω)
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble.exactSecondMoment_eq_operatorAverage
docString: The canonical exact second moment is the normalized finite operator average `E[Vω X Vω]`.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} {Ω : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
  [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H] [inst_3 : Fintype Ω] (ensemble : QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble)
  (amplitude : Ω → ℝ),
  (∀ (ω : Ω), ↑(ensemble.impurityPotential ω) = ↑(amplitude ω) • 1) →
    ∀ (kernel : H →L[ℂ] H), ensemble.exactSecondMoment kernel = ensemble.scalarSecondMomentStrength amplitude • kernel
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble.exactSecondMoment_eq_scalarSecondMomentStrength_smul
docString:
If every impurity potential is scalar, `Vω = uω I`, the exact second-moment action is scalar
multiplication by `E[uω²]`.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} {Ω : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
  [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H] [inst_3 : Fintype Ω] (ensemble : QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble)
  (kernel : H →L[ℂ] H), ensemble.exactSecondMoment (star kernel) = star (ensemble.exactSecondMoment kernel)
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble.exactSecondMoment_star
docString:
The exact second-moment action preserves adjoints because every impurity potential is
self-adjoint and every ensemble weight is real.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} {Ω : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
  [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H] [inst_3 : Fintype Ω] (ensemble : QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble)
  (left right : H →L[ℂ] H),
  ensemble.exactSecondMoment (left - right) = ensemble.exactSecondMoment left - ensemble.exactSecondMoment right
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble.exactSecondMoment_sub
docString:
The exact second-moment action preserves subtraction because its canonical realization is
complex-linear.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} {Ω : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
  [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H] [inst_3 : Fintype Ω] (ensemble : QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble)
  (energy regulator : ℝ) (hregulator : regulator ≠ 0),
  QuantumTheory.Transport.IsSelfEnergy (ensemble.freeGreenOfRegulator energy regulator)
    (ensemble.averagedGreenOfRegulator energy regulator)
    (ensemble.exactSelfEnergyOfRegulator energy regulator hregulator)
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble.exactSelfEnergyOfRegulator_isSelfEnergy
docString:
The canonical exact finite-disorder self-energy satisfies the exact two-sided Dyson relation at
any nonzero signed regulator.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} {Ω : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
  [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H] [inst_3 : Fintype Ω] (ensemble : QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble)
  (energy regulator : ℝ) (hregulator : regulator ≠ 0) (selfEnergy : H →L[ℂ] H),
  QuantumTheory.Transport.IsSelfEnergy (ensemble.freeGreenOfRegulator energy regulator)
      (ensemble.averagedGreenOfRegulator energy regulator) selfEnergy ↔
    selfEnergy = ensemble.exactSelfEnergyOfRegulator energy regulator hregulator
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble.isSelfEnergy_iff_eq_exactSelfEnergyOfRegulator
docString:
At a nonzero signed regulator, the canonical exact self-energy is the unique self-energy
satisfying the exact two-sided Dyson relation for the clean and disorder-averaged Green operators.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} {Ω : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
  [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H] [inst_3 : Fintype Ω] (ensemble : QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble)
  (operator : Ω → H →L[ℂ] H),
  (ensemble.operatorAverage fun ω => star (operator ω)) = star (ensemble.operatorAverage operator)
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble.operatorAverage_star
docString: Exact finite operator averaging commutes with adjunction because every ensemble weight is real.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} {Ω : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
  [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H] [inst_3 : Fintype Ω] (self : QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble) (ω : Ω),

name: QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble.probability_nonneg

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} {Ω : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
  [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H] [inst_3 : Fintype Ω] (self : QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble),

name: QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble.probability_sum

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} {Ω : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
  [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H] [inst_3 : Fintype Ω] (ensemble : QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble)
  (retardedGreen advancedGreen vertex : H →L[ℂ] H),
  (ensemble.retardedAdvancedLadderCLM retardedGreen advancedGreen) vertex =
    ensemble.exactSecondMoment (retardedGreen * vertex * advancedGreen)
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble.retardedAdvancedLadderCLM_apply
docString:
Evaluation of the finite covariance ladder is the expected operator insertion
`C₂(Gᴿ Γ Gᴬ)`.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} {Ω : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
  [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H] [inst_3 : Fintype Ω] (ensemble : QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble)
  (energy regulator : ℝ),
  star (ensemble.averagedGreenOfRegulator energy regulator) = ensemble.averagedGreenOfRegulator energy (-regulator)
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble.star_averagedGreenOfRegulator
docString: Adjointing the exact finite disorder-averaged Green operator reverses the signed regulator.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} {Ω : Type u_2} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
  [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H] [inst_3 : Fintype Ω] (ensemble : QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble)
  (energy regulator : ℝ),
  star (ensemble.bornSelfEnergyOfRegulator energy regulator) = ensemble.bornSelfEnergyOfRegulator energy (-regulator)
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.FiniteDisorderEnsemble.star_bornSelfEnergyOfRegulator
docString: Adjointing the first-Born self-energy reverses the signed regulator.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : Ring A] {freeGreen dressedGreen selfEnergy freeInverse dressedInverse : A},
  freeInverse * freeGreen = 1 →
    freeGreen * freeInverse = 1 →
      dressedInverse * dressedGreen = 1 →
        dressedGreen * dressedInverse = 1 →
          (QuantumTheory.Transport.IsSelfEnergy freeGreen dressedGreen selfEnergy ↔
            selfEnergy = freeInverse - dressedInverse)
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.IsSelfEnergy.iff_eq_inverse_sub_inverse
docString:
For two-sided inverses, the two-sided Dyson relation is equivalent to the inverse-difference
definition of self-energy.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : Ring A] {freeGreen dressedGreen selfEnergy : A},
  QuantumTheory.Transport.IsSelfEnergy freeGreen dressedGreen selfEnergy →
    dressedGreen = freeGreen + freeGreen * selfEnergy * dressedGreen
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.IsSelfEnergy.leftDyson
docString: The left-oriented Dyson equation carried by an abstract self-energy relation.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : Ring A] {freeGreen dressedGreen selfEnergy freeShift dressedShift : A},
  freeGreen * freeShift = 1 →
    freeShift * freeGreen = 1 →
      dressedShift * dressedGreen = 1 →
        dressedGreen * dressedShift = 1 →
          freeShift = dressedShift + selfEnergy → QuantumTheory.Transport.IsSelfEnergy freeGreen dressedGreen selfEnergy
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.IsSelfEnergy.of_shift
docString:
A Dyson self-energy follows from two-sided inverse equations for the free and dressed shifts
together with `freeShift = dressedShift + selfEnergy`.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : Ring A] {freeGreen dressedGreen selfEnergy : A},
  QuantumTheory.Transport.IsSelfEnergy freeGreen dressedGreen selfEnergy →
    dressedGreen = freeGreen + dressedGreen * selfEnergy * freeGreen
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.IsSelfEnergy.rightDyson
docString: The right-oriented Dyson equation carried by an abstract self-energy relation.

statement:
∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : Ring A] [inst_1 : StarRing A] {freeGreen dressedGreen selfEnergy : A},
  QuantumTheory.Transport.IsSelfEnergy freeGreen dressedGreen selfEnergy →
    QuantumTheory.Transport.IsSelfEnergy (star freeGreen) (star dressedGreen) (star selfEnergy)
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.IsSelfEnergy.star_closed
docString:
The two-sided Dyson self-energy relation is preserved by adjunction. The two Dyson orientations
are exchanged because `star` reverses noncommutative multiplication order.

name: QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.FiniteScalarDisorderModel.baseHamiltonian_eq
docString: The clean part of the ensemble is the massive-Dirac Hamiltonian at the supplied momentum.

statement:
∀ {Ω : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Ω] {v m px py : ℝ}
  (model : QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.FiniteScalarDisorderModel Ω v m px py) (energy regulator : ℝ),
  model.ensemble.bornSelfEnergyOfRegulator energy regulator =
    model.secondMomentStrength •
      resolvent (QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.hamiltonianOperator v m px py)
        (QuantumTheory.Transport.spectralParameterOfRegulator energy regulator)
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.FiniteScalarDisorderModel.bornSelfEnergyOfRegulator_eq_strength_smul
docString:
Massive-Dirac scalar-disorder first-Born self-energy at an arbitrary signed regulator. This is
the exact finite second moment applied to the corresponding clean propagator, not an exact
disorder-averaged self-energy.

statement:
∀ {Ω : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Ω] {v m px py : ℝ}
  (model : QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.FiniteScalarDisorderModel Ω v m px py)
  (kernel :
    QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.DiracHilbert →L[ℂ]
      QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.DiracHilbert),
  model.ensemble.exactSecondMoment kernel = model.secondMomentStrength • kernel
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.FiniteScalarDisorderModel.exactSecondMoment_eq_strength_smul
docString:
The canonical exact finite second-moment action becomes scalar multiplication when every
impurity potential is scalar in the Dirac internal space.

name: QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.FiniteScalarDisorderModel.impurityPotential_eq
docString: Every impurity potential is proportional to the identity in Dirac internal space.

statement:
∀ (band : QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.Band) (v m px py offset radius : ℝ),

docString:
If `|offset| ≤ radius`, the shifted interband denominator stays at least
`|gap| - radius` away from zero on the real axis.

docString: The massive-Dirac energy is bounded below by the mass magnitude uniformly in momentum.

docString:
In the metallic-or-band-edge regime `|m| ≤ ε_F`, the upper band is occupied exactly below the
explicit Fermi radius. At `ε_F = |m|`, this occupied region is empty and `p_F = 0`.

statement:
∀ (band : QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.Band) (v m px py : ℝ),

          (QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.oppositeBand band) v m px py =
      0
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.bandProjectorOperator_mul_oppositeBand
docString: Opposite-band operator projectors are orthogonal away from the Dirac degeneracy.

statement:
∀ (band : QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.Band) (v m px py : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.energy v m px py ≠ 0 →
    QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.bandProjectorOperator band v m px py *
        QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.bandProjectorOperator band v m px py =
      QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.bandProjectorOperator band v m px py
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.bandProjectorOperator_mul_self
docString: Operator projectors remain idempotent after transport from `2 × 2` matrices.

statement:
∀ (band : QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.Band) (v m px py : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.bandProjector band v m px py +
      QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.bandProjector
        (QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.oppositeBand band) v m px py =
    1
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.bandProjector_add_oppositeBand
docString: Either band projector and its opposite-band partner resolve the identity.

statement:
∀ (band : QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.Band) (v m px py : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.bandProjector band v m px py =
    (1 / 2) •
      (1 +
        InternalSpace.pauliCombination
          (↑(QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.bandSign band /
                QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.energy v m px py) •
            QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.diracPauliCoefficients v m px py))
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.bandProjector_eq_pauliCombination
docString:
Pauli/Bloch form of the massive-Dirac band projector. This is the canonical spectral-layer
bridge from the model Hamiltonian to the shared internal-space Pauli algebra.

statement:
∀ (band : QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.Band) (v m px py : ℝ),

          (QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.oppositeBand band) v m px py =
      0
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.bandProjector_mul_oppositeBand
docString: Away from the band degeneracy, opposite-band projectors are orthogonal in either order.

statement:
∀ (band : QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.Band) (v m px py : ℝ),

name: QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.bandProjector_mul_self
docString: Away from the band degeneracy, each `P_s` is idempotent.

docString: Cyclicity identifies the direct Bastin block with the corresponding projector-first block.

∀ (μ ν : QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.Direction2)
  (source target : QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.Band) (e v m px py : ℝ),

docString: Reversing the current order exchanges the source and target band labels.

statement:
∀ (μ ν : QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.Direction2)
  (band : QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.Band) (e v m px py probeEnergy broadening : ℝ),
  broadening ≠ 0 →
    QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.bastinBandPairContribution μ ν
        (QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.oppositeBand band) band e v m px py probeEnergy broadening =

          ↑(QuantumTheory.Transport.lorentzianSpectralKernel
              (probeEnergy - QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.bandEnergy band v m px py) broadening) *
        QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.interbandSpectatorCurrentFactor μ ν band e v m px py probeEnergy
          broadening

docString:
Exact factorization of one direction-indexed interband Bastin pair into its Lorentzian spectral
pole and regular spectator/current factor.

statement:
∀ (e hbar m εF Λ : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.bastinCleanHallConductivityCutoff e hbar m εF Λ =

docString:
The canonical clean radial Bastin-pair integral has exactly the same finite-cutoff normalization
as the canonical occupation-derived intrinsic Hall conductivity.

statement:
∀ (band : QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.Band) (e v m px py : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.energy v m px py ≠ 0 →
    (QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.bastinInterbandBlockDifference
            QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.Direction2.x
            QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.Direction2.y band e v m px py).im /
        QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.interbandEnergyGap band v m px py ^ 2 =

docString:
The normalized Hall antisymmetric Bastin block is the negative of `e²` times the clean Berry
curvature.

statement:

docString: The antisymmetric interband Bastin block vanishes on equal current directions.

statement:
∀ (μ ν : QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.Direction2)
  (band : QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.Band) (e v m px py : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.bastinInterbandBlockDifference ν μ band e v m px py =

name: QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.bastinInterbandBlockDifference_swap
docString:
Exchanging the two current directions reverses the sign of the interband Bastin block
difference.

statement:
∀ (band : QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.Band) (e v m p : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.energy v m p 0 ≠ 0 →
    QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.bastinBandBlockTrace
        QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.Direction2.x
        QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.Direction2.y
        (QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.oppositeBand band) band e v m p 0 =

          ↑(QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.bandSign band * m * v ^ 2 /
              QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.energy v m p 0) *
        Complex.I
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.bastinXYBandBlockTrace_opposite_source_radial
docString: The natural radial `x-y` Bastin block at a target-band pole is purely imaginary.

statement:

  QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.berryCurvature QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.Band.lower v m
      px py =
    m * v ^ 2 / (2 * QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.energy v m px py ^ 3)
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.berryCurvature_lower
docString: Lower-band Berry curvature `Ω₋ = +m v²/(2E³)`.

statement:
∀ (band : QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.Band) (v px py : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.berryCurvature band v 0 px py = 0
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.berryCurvature_massless

statement:
∀ (band : QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.Band) (v m px py : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.berryCurvature band v (-m) px py =
    -QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.berryCurvature band v m px py
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.berryCurvature_neg_mass
docString: Reversing the time-reversal-breaking mass reverses the Berry curvature.

statement:
∀ (band : QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.Band) (v m px py : ℝ),

action, preserving the complete coefficient vector until the operator boundary.

docString:
Massive-Dirac intrinsic AHE closed form,
`σxy^int = -(e²/2h) (m/εF)`, stated for the totalized real-field operations.

docString:
The physical-momentum measure normalization reduces the Berry/Kubo prefactor to `-e²/h` as an
identity of totalized real-field expressions.

docString: Solving the scalar ladder equation gives the transport-over-single-particle lifetime factor.

statement:

  QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.inversionSymmetrizedPauliGreenOperatorOfRegulator v m px py probeEnergy
      regulator =
    QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.pauliGreenScalarCoefficientOfRegulator v m px py probeEnergy regulator •
        1 +
      QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.pauliGreenPauliCoefficientOfRegulator InternalSpace.PauliAxis.z v m px

        QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.matrixOperator QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.sigmaZ
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.inversionSymmetrizedPauliGreenOperatorOfRegulator_eq_evenChannels
docString:
Exact arbitrary-regulator momentum-inversion symmetrization retains only the scalar and `σ_z`
Pauli channels.

statement:
∀ (v m fermiEnergy : ℝ),
  v ≠ 0 →
    |m| ≤ fermiEnergy →
      fermiEnergy ≠ 0 →
        QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.isotropicFermiSurfaceMeanSquareVelocityX v m fermiEnergy =
          v ^ 2 * (1 - m ^ 2 / fermiEnergy ^ 2) / 2
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.isotropicFermiSurfaceMeanSquareVelocityX_eq
docString:
In the metallic-or-band-edge regime, the isotropic Fermi-surface factor is

`<v_x²>_FS = (v² / 2) * (1 - m² / ε_F²)`.

statement:
∀ (v m fermiEnergy : ℝ),
  v ≠ 0 →
    |m| < fermiEnergy →
      0 < QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.isotropicFermiSurfaceMeanSquareVelocityX v m fermiEnergy
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.isotropicFermiSurfaceMeanSquareVelocityX_pos
docString:
In the strictly metallic regime `|m| < ε_F`, the isotropic Fermi-surface `v_x²` factor is
strictly positive when `v ≠ 0`.

statement:
∀ (v m p : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.isotropicMeanSquareRadialGroupVelocityX v m p =
    QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.radialEnergyDerivative v m p ^ 2 / 2
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.isotropicMeanSquareRadialGroupVelocityX_eq
docString:
In two dimensions, the isotropic angular mean of `v_x²` is one half of the squared radial
velocity.  The factor `1/2` is the explicit full-circle `cos² θ` average.

statement:
∀ (v m fermiEnergy : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.isotropicUpperBandSingleParticleAngularWeight v m fermiEnergy =
    (1 + m ^ 2 / fermiEnergy ^ 2) / 2
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.isotropicUpperBandSingleParticleAngularWeight_eq
docString: The unweighted scalar-disorder overlap average is `(1 + m²/ε_F²)/2`.

statement:
∀ (v m fermiEnergy : ℝ),
  QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.isotropicUpperBandTransportAngularWeight v m fermiEnergy =
    (1 + 3 * (m ^ 2 / fermiEnergy ^ 2)) / 4
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.isotropicUpperBandTransportAngularWeight_eq
docString: The scalar-disorder transport angular weight is `(1 + 3 m²/ε_F²)/4`.

docString: Any massive-Dirac lower band is filled when the Fermi energy is positive.

docString: Every lower-band state has unit zero-temperature occupation at positive Fermi energy.

∀ (v m fermiEnergy : ℝ) (p : ℝ × ℝ),

name: QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.mem_upperBand_fermiSurface_iff
docString: The upper-band Fermi surface is the level set of the positive Dirac energy.

statement:
∀ (v m fermiEnergy : ℝ) (p : ℝ × ℝ),

      QuantumTheory.Transport.occupiedRegion (QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.bandEnergyOnMomentum v m)

docString:
The upper-band zero-temperature occupied region is exactly the region where the positive Dirac
energy lies below the Fermi energy.

statement:
∀ (v m fermiEnergy p : ℝ),
  v ≠ 0 →
    |m| ≤ fermiEnergy →
      0 ≤ p →
        (p ∈
            QuantumTheory.Transport.fermiSurface (QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.radialBandEnergy v m)

          p = QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.metallicFermiRadius v m fermiEnergy)
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.mem_upperBand_radialFermiSurface_iff_eq_metallicFermiRadius
docString:
On the nonnegative radial axis in `|m| ≤ ε_F`, the generic upper-band Fermi surface is the
single explicit `metallicFermiRadius` value.

statement:
∀ (v m fermiEnergy p : ℝ),
  v ≠ 0 →
    |m| ≤ fermiEnergy →
      0 ≤ p →
        (p ∈
            QuantumTheory.Transport.occupiedRegion (QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.radialBandEnergy v m)
              fermiEnergy QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.Band.upper ↔
          p < QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.metallicFermiRadius v m fermiEnergy)
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.mem_upperBand_radialOccupiedRegion_iff_lt_metallicFermiRadius
docString:
On the nonnegative radial axis in `|m| ≤ ε_F`, generic upper-band occupation is exactly
`p < p_F`; at the band edge `ε_F = |m|` this set is empty.

statement: ∀ (v m fermiEnergy : ℝ), 0 ≤ QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.metallicFermiRadius v m fermiEnergy
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.metallicFermiRadius_nonneg
docString: The expression used for the metallic Fermi radius is always nonnegative.

statement:
∀ (v m fermiEnergy : ℝ),
  |m| ≤ fermiEnergy →
    QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.metallicFermiRadius v m fermiEnergy ^ 2 =
      (fermiEnergy ^ 2 - m ^ 2) / v ^ 2
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.metallicFermiRadius_sq
docString:
Squaring the explicit metallic Fermi radius removes the square root and absolute value whenever
the Fermi energy lies at or above the mass magnitude.

statement:
∀ (v m probeEnergy regulator pMax : ℝ),
  probeEnergy ≠ 0 →
    regulator ≠ 0 →
      -2 * ↑v ^ 2 *
          QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.finiteCutoffContinuumBornDenominatorIntegralOfRegulator v m
            probeEnergy regulator pMax =
        Complex.log
            (QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.pauliGreenDenominatorOfRegulator v m pMax 0 probeEnergy
              regulator) -
          Complex.log
            (QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.pauliGreenDenominatorOfRegulator v m 0 0 probeEnergy regulator)
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.neg_two_mul_velocitySq_mul_finiteCutoffContinuumBornDenominatorIntegralOfRegulator_eq_log_sub_log
docString:
Before dividing by `-2v²`, the arbitrary-regulator finite-cutoff denominator integral is the
endpoint principal-log difference.

statement:
∀ (band : QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.Band) (v m p offset radius broadening : ℝ),
  radius < 2 * |m| →
    |offset| ≤ radius →
      ‖(↑(QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.interbandEnergyGap band v m p 0 + offset) -
              ↑broadening * Complex.I)⁻¹‖ ≤
        (QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.radialBastinMassWindowMargin m radius)⁻¹
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.norm_advancedRadialSpectatorResolvent_le_inv_margin
docString:
The advanced opposite-band resolvent obeys the same momentum- and broadening-independent
inverse-margin bound.

statement:
∀ (band : QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.Band) (e v m p offset radius broadening : ℝ),
  m ≠ 0 →
    radius < 2 * |m| →
      |offset| ≤ radius →
        0 ≤ broadening →

        QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.pauliGreenPauliCoefficientOfRegulator InternalSpace.PauliAxis.x v m

    QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.targetCenteredInterbandSpectatorCurrentFactor band e v m p 0

statement:
∀ (e hbar v m fermiEnergy disorderStrength : ℝ) (hvelocity : v ≠ 0) (hhbar : 0 < hbar)
  (hdisorder : 0 < disorderStrength) (hmF : |m| < fermiEnergy),
  QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.zeroTemperatureRelaxationTimeLongitudinalConductivity e hbar v m
      fermiEnergy
      (QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.continuumBornUpperBandPositiveTransportLifetime v m fermiEnergy
        disorderStrength hbar hvelocity hhbar hdisorder hmF) =
    e ^ 2 * hbar * v ^ 2 * (fermiEnergy ^ 2 - m ^ 2) / (Real.pi * disorderStrength * (fermiEnergy ^ 2 + 3 * m ^ 2))
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.zeroTemperatureRelaxationTimeLongitudinalConductivity_bornTransportLifetime_eq
docString:
The zero-temperature massive-Dirac RTA benchmark evaluated on the microscopic Born transport
lifetime has the explicit `1/W` form

`σxx = e² ℏ v² (εF² - m²) / [π W (εF² + 3 m²)]`.

The positivity assumptions are exactly those used to package the microscopic lifetime as a
`PositiveTransportLifetime`; no finite clean-disorder limit is asserted.

statement:
∀ (e hbar v m fermiEnergy : ℝ) (transportLifetime : QuantumTheory.Transport.PositiveTransportLifetime),
  hbar ≠ 0 →
    v ≠ 0 →
      |m| < fermiEnergy →
        QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.zeroTemperatureRelaxationTimeLongitudinalConductivity e hbar v m
            fermiEnergy transportLifetime =
          e ^ 2 * transportLifetime.lifetime * (fermiEnergy ^ 2 - m ^ 2) / (4 * Real.pi * hbar ^ 2 * fermiEnergy)
name: QuantumTheory.Transport.Models.MassiveDirac.zeroTemperatureRelaxationTimeLongitudinalConductivity_eq
docString:
Closed single-cone zero-temperature massive-Dirac relaxation-time benchmark

`σxx^RTA = e² τ_tr (ε_F² - m²) / (4π ℏ² ε_F)`.

statement:

docString:

is positive in the strict metallic regime.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  [inst_3 : FiniteDimensional ℂ H] {hamiltonian current₁ current₂ : H →L[ℂ] H} {broadening lowerEnergy upperEnergy : ℝ}
  {occupation occupationDerivative : ℝ → ℂ},
  QuantumTheory.Transport.TracedStredaAnalyticData hamiltonian current₁ current₂ broadening lowerEnergy upperEnergy
      occupation occupationDerivative →
    occupation upperEnergy *
          QuantumTheory.Transport.regularizedStredaSurfacePrimitiveTrace hamiltonian current₁ current₂ upperEnergy
            broadening -
        occupation lowerEnergy *
          QuantumTheory.Transport.regularizedStredaSurfacePrimitiveTrace hamiltonian current₁ current₂ lowerEnergy

      (QuantumTheory.Transport.finiteStaticKuboBastinChannelVertexResponse system data channel eta)),

    QuantumTheory.Transport.regularizedStredaFermiSurface representation.toRegularizedStredaIntegralData +

        channel.observableVariation

representation, the complete generalized response is its surface-plus-sea decomposition plus the
unchanged observable-variation expectation.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} {N : ℕ} [inst : Fintype Mode] [inst_1 : DecidableEq Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  (hpos : ∀ (i : Mode), 0 < β * ε i)
  (admissible : (r : ℕ) → (Fin (2 * r) → SecondQuantization.Bosonic.FreeThermalField Mode) → Prop),
  (∀ (r : ℕ) (C : Fin (2 * r) → SecondQuantization.Bosonic.FreeThermalField Mode),
      admissible r C →
        SecondQuantization.Bosonic.FreeThermalField.orderedProduct (List.ofFn C) ∈
          SecondQuantization.Bosonic.freeGibbsDomain ε β) →
    (∀ (r : ℕ) (C : Fin (2 * (r + 1)) → SecondQuantization.Bosonic.FreeThermalField Mode),
        admissible (r + 1) C → ∀ (j : Fin (2 * r + 1)), admissible r fun i => C (j.succAbove i).succ) →
      (∀ (r : ℕ) (C : Fin (2 * (r + 1)) → SecondQuantization.Bosonic.FreeThermalField Mode),
          admissible (r + 1) C →
            (SecondQuantization.Bosonic.freeGibbsFunctional ε β hpos).value
                (SecondQuantization.Bosonic.FreeThermalField.orderedProduct (List.ofFn C)) =
              ∑ j,
                SecondQuantization.Bosonic.freeThermalPairValue ε β (C 0) (C j.succ) *
                  (SecondQuantization.Bosonic.freeGibbsFunctional ε β hpos).value
                    (SecondQuantization.Bosonic.FreeThermalField.orderedProduct
                      (List.ofFn fun i => C (j.succAbove i).succ))) →
        ∀ {S : Finset (Fin N)} (d : SecondQuantization.Bosonic.QuarticDiagram Mode N S)
          (order : SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticVertexOrder S),
          admissible (2 * S.card) (d.orderedFreeThermalFieldFamily order) →
            (SecondQuantization.Bosonic.freeGibbsFunctional ε β hpos).value
                (SecondQuantization.Bosonic.quarticFreeThermalOrderedProduct fun i => d.vertexLabel (order i)) =
              SecondQuantization.Bosonic.QuarticDiagram.orderedThermalWickSum ε β d order
name: SecondQuantization.Bosonic.QuarticDiagram.freeGibbsExpectation_eq_orderedThermalWickSum
docString:
The convergence-aware Gibbs expectation of the ordered quartic local-leg product is exactly the
sum over the pairing amplitudes carried by the existing quartic diagram combinatorics.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} {N : ℕ} [inst : DecidableEq Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ) {S : Finset (Fin N)}
  (d : SecondQuantization.Bosonic.QuarticDiagram Mode N S)
  (orders : SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticDiagram.ComponentVertexOrders d)
  (shuffle : SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticDiagram.ComponentShuffle d)
  (B : ↥(SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticDiagram.componentPartition d).parts) (a b : Fin (2 * (2 * (↑B).card))),
  SecondQuantization.Bosonic.freeThermalPairValue ε β
      (d.orderedFreeThermalFieldFamily (SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticDiagram.assembleVertexOrder d orders shuffle)
        (SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticDiagram.componentOrderedLeg d shuffle B a))
      (d.orderedFreeThermalFieldFamily (SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticDiagram.assembleVertexOrder d orders shuffle)
        (SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticDiagram.componentOrderedLeg d shuffle B b)) =
    SecondQuantization.Bosonic.freeThermalPairValue ε β
      (SecondQuantization.Bosonic.QuarticDiagram.orderedFreeThermalFieldFamily
        (SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticDiagram.restrictComponent d ⋯) (orders B) a)
      (SecondQuantization.Bosonic.QuarticDiagram.orderedFreeThermalFieldFamily
        (SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticDiagram.restrictComponent d ⋯) (orders B) b)
name: SecondQuantization.Bosonic.QuarticDiagram.freeThermalPairValue_componentOrderedLeg
docString:
The free thermal pair kernel agrees between a component-local ordered pair and its image in an
assembled global order.

docString:

statement:

  (admissible : (n : ℕ) → (Fin (2 * n) → SecondQuantization.Bosonic.FreeThermalField Mode) → Prop),
  (∀ (n : ℕ) (C : Fin (2 * n) → SecondQuantization.Bosonic.FreeThermalField Mode),
      admissible n C →
        SecondQuantization.Bosonic.FreeThermalField.orderedProduct (List.ofFn C) ∈
          SecondQuantization.Bosonic.freeGibbsDomain ε β) →
    (∀ (n : ℕ) (C : Fin (2 * (n + 1)) → SecondQuantization.Bosonic.FreeThermalField Mode),
        admissible (n + 1) C → ∀ (j : Fin (2 * n + 1)), admissible n fun i => C (j.succAbove i).succ) →
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (C : Fin (2 * (n + 1)) → SecondQuantization.Bosonic.FreeThermalField Mode),
          admissible (n + 1) C →
            (SecondQuantization.Bosonic.freeGibbsFunctional ε β hpos).value
                (SecondQuantization.Bosonic.FreeThermalField.orderedProduct (List.ofFn C)) =
              ∑ j,
                SecondQuantization.Bosonic.freeThermalPairValue ε β (C 0) (C j.succ) *
                  (SecondQuantization.Bosonic.freeGibbsFunctional ε β hpos).value
                    (SecondQuantization.Bosonic.FreeThermalField.orderedProduct
                      (List.ofFn fun i => C (j.succAbove i).succ))) →
        ∀ (n : ℕ) (C : Fin (2 * n) → SecondQuantization.Bosonic.FreeThermalField Mode),
          admissible n C →
            (SecondQuantization.Bosonic.freeGibbsFunctional ε β hpos).value
                (SecondQuantization.Bosonic.FreeThermalField.orderedProduct (List.ofFn C)) =
              ∑ pairing,
                Combinatorics.Pairing.weight SecondQuantization.Common.Statistics.boson pairing *
                  ∏ pr ∈ pairing.pairs, SecondQuantization.Bosonic.freeThermalPairValue ε β (C pr.1) (C pr.2)

statement:
∀ {Config : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Config] [inst_1 : Nonempty Config] (s : SecondQuantization.Common.Statistics)
  (energy : Config → ℝ) (β : ℝ),
  SecondQuantization.Common.traceFock (SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy (-β)) ≠ 0 →
    ∀ (n : ℕ)
      (C :
        Fin (2 * n) →
          SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config)
      (q : Fin (2 * n) → ℝ) (c : Fin (2 * n) → Fin (2 * n) → ℂ),
      (∀ (i : Fin (2 * n)),
          SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy (-β) (C i) = Complex.exp ↑(q i * -β) • C i) →
        (∀ (i j : Fin (2 * n)), i ≠ j → LinearMap.zetaCommutator (↑s.zetaInt) (C i) (C j) = c i j • LinearMap.id) →
          (∀ (i : Fin (2 * n)), 1 - ↑s.zetaInt * Complex.exp ↑(q i * β) ≠ 0) →
            SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β
                (SecondQuantization.Common.prodComp (List.ofFn C)) =
              ∑ pairing,
                Combinatorics.Pairing.weight s pairing *
                  ∏ pr ∈ pairing.pairs, SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β (C pr.1 ∘ₗ C pr.2)

docString: **The general finite-temperature Bloch–de Dominicis theorem.**

  0 ≤ β →

          SecondQuantization.Common.analyticDysonExponentialCandidate energy V τ lam

docString:
On every compact nonnegative time interval, the analytic Dyson sum equals the exact ordered

statement:
∀ {Config : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Config] (energy : Config → ℝ)
  (V : SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config) {β τ : ℝ},
  0 ≤ β →
    τ ∈ Set.Icc 0 β →
      ∀ (lam : ℂ),
        SecondQuantization.Common.analyticDysonEvolution energy V τ lam =
          1 -
            lam •
              ∫ (σ : ℝ) in 0..τ,
                SecondQuantization.Common.continuousInteractionPicture energy V σ ∘SL
                  SecondQuantization.Common.analyticDysonEvolution energy V σ lam

docString:
The finite analytic Dyson evolution solves the Volterra equation by specialization of the
generic bounded-algebra theorem.

statement:

  0 ≤ τ →
    ∀ (lam : ℂ),
      SecondQuantization.Common.analyticDysonEvolution energy V τ lam =
        NormedSpace.exp (τ • SecondQuantization.Common.continuousDiagonalHamiltonian energy) *
          NormedSpace.exp (τ • -SecondQuantization.Common.continuousInteractingHamiltonian energy V lam)

  (C : SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config),
  SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy τ C = Complex.exp ↑(q * τ) • C →
    C ∘ₗ SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy τ =
      Complex.exp ↑(-(q * τ)) • SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy τ ∘ₗ C
name: SecondQuantization.Common.comp_diagonalEvolution_eq_smul_diagonalEvolution_comp
docString:
**`C e^{τH₀} = e^{-qτ} e^{τH₀} C`**, the KMS-type relation with `C` on the left — the algebraic
rearrangement of `diagonalEvolution_comp_eq_smul_comp_diagonalEvolution` needed by the rotation
theorems below, obtained by multiplying both sides of that lemma by the (nonzero) reciprocal
exponential factor. Config-general — no `[Fintype Config]` needed.

statement:
∀ {Config : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Config]
  (L : SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config)
  (F : ℝ → SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config)
  (a b : ℝ),
  (∀ (k n : Config),
      IntervalIntegrable (fun σ => SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff (F σ) k n) MeasureTheory.volume a b) →
    L ∘ₗ SecondQuantization.Common.operatorIntervalIntegral F a b =
      SecondQuantization.Common.operatorIntervalIntegral (fun σ => L ∘ₗ F σ) a b
name: SecondQuantization.Common.comp_operatorIntervalIntegral
docString:
**Left-composition with a fixed operator commutes with `operatorIntervalIntegral`**:
`L ∘ (∫ F) = ∫ (L ∘ F)`, given interval-integrability of every matrix coefficient `F` contributes.
Both sides reduce, via `matrixCoeff_comp`/`matrixCoeff_operatorIntervalIntegral`, to the same
`∑ k, matrixCoeff L m k * ∫ σ, matrixCoeff (F σ) k n` vs. `∫ σ, ∑ k, matrixCoeff L m k *
matrixCoeff (F σ) k n` — the finite-sum/integral interchange `intervalIntegral.integral_finsetSum`
supplies, after pulling the constant `matrixCoeff L m k` in/out of each summand's integral
(`intervalIntegral.integral_const_mul`). Needed to move an already-evaluated interaction-picture
vertex factor past the ordered-simplex integral over the *remaining* Dyson coefficient.

statement:
∀ {Config : Type u_1} (ζ : ℂ)
  (C1 : SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config)
  (l :
    List ((SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config) × ℂ)),
  (∀ p ∈ l, LinearMap.zetaCommutator ζ C1 p.1 = p.2 • LinearMap.id) →
    C1 ∘ₗ SecondQuantization.Common.prodComp (List.map Prod.fst l) =
      SecondQuantization.Common.peelSum ζ l +
        ζ ^ l.length • SecondQuantization.Common.prodComp (List.map Prod.fst l) ∘ₗ C1
name: SecondQuantization.Common.comp_prodComp_eq_of_zetaCommutator
docString:
**Peeling `C₁` through an arbitrary-length product**: repeatedly rewriting `C₁Bⱼ` via each
pair's `ζ`-commutator coefficient and pushing `C₁` rightward, `C₁` lands at the very end having
picked up `ζ^{l.length}`.

∀ {Config : Type u_1} (energy : Config → ℝ) (τ q : ℝ)
  (C : SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config),
  SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy τ C = Complex.exp ↑(q * τ) • C →
    SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy τ ∘ₗ C =
      Complex.exp ↑(q * τ) • C ∘ₗ SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy τ
name: SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution_comp_eq_smul_comp_diagonalEvolution
docString:
**The KMS-type relation**: if a linear map `C` picks up an exponential eigenvalue-shift factor
`e^{qτ}` under `heisenbergEvolve` (as every `create`/`annihilate` operator does, with `q` the
eigenvalue shift `∓ε_i`), then `e^{τH₀}` and `C` satisfy `e^{τH₀} C = e^{qτ} C e^{τH₀}` — the exact
statistics-agnostic algebraic ingredient the finite-temperature Bloch–de Dominicis theorem's
KMS-rotation step needs (`ĉ_α e^{-βĤ} = e^{-βξ_α} e^{-βĤ} ĉ_α` in the project's physics reference
notes, `quantum-statistical-mechanics.tex`'s "product-of-KMS-state-and-ladder-op"), obtained purely
by rearranging the already-proved semigroup law and mutual inversion
(`diagonalEvolution_neg_comp`) — no new physical input beyond the eigenvalue-shift hypothesis
`hC`, and in particular no dependence on the concrete occupation-state type or exchange statistics.
Both `Fermionic.imaginaryTimeEvolve_annihilate`/`_create` and
`Bosonic.imaginaryTimeEvolve_annihilate`/`_create` supply exactly this hypothesis (with
`q := -ε i`/`q := ε i` respectively), so this single `Common/` lemma gives the KMS relation for
`create`/`annihilate` in both statistics at once.

statement:
∀ {Config : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Config] [inst_1 : Nonempty Config] (energy : Config → ℝ) (β q1 : ℝ)
  (ζ c12 c13 c14 : ℂ)
  (C1 C2 C3 C4 : SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config),
  SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy (-β) C1 = Complex.exp ↑(q1 * -β) • C1 →
    C1 ∘ₗ C2 - ζ • C2 ∘ₗ C1 = c12 • LinearMap.id →
      C1 ∘ₗ C3 - ζ • C3 ∘ₗ C1 = c13 • LinearMap.id →
        C1 ∘ₗ C4 - ζ • C4 ∘ₗ C1 = c14 • LinearMap.id →
          SecondQuantization.Common.traceFock (SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy (-β)) ≠ 0 →
            1 - ζ ^ 3 * Complex.exp ↑(q1 * β) ≠ 0 →
              SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β (C1 ∘ₗ C2 ∘ₗ C3 ∘ₗ C4) =
                (c12 * SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β (C3 ∘ₗ C4) +
                      ζ * c13 * SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β (C2 ∘ₗ C4) +
                    ζ ^ 2 * c14 * SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β (C2 ∘ₗ C3)) /
                  (1 - ζ ^ 3 * Complex.exp ↑(q1 * β))
name: SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation_comp_comp_comp_eq_div_of_zetaCommutator
docString: The normalized 4-point first-operator reduction.

statement:
∀ {Config : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Config] [inst_1 : Nonempty Config] (energy : Config → ℝ) (β q1 : ℝ)
  (s : SecondQuantization.Common.Statistics) (c1j : ℂ)
  (C1 Cj : SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config),
  SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy (-β) C1 = Complex.exp ↑(q1 * -β) • C1 →
    SecondQuantization.Common.exchangeCommutator s C1 Cj = c1j • LinearMap.id →
      SecondQuantization.Common.traceFock (SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy (-β)) ≠ 0 →
        1 - ↑s.zetaInt * Complex.exp ↑(q1 * β) ≠ 0 →
          SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β (C1 ∘ₗ Cj) =
            c1j / (1 - ↑s.zetaInt * Complex.exp ↑(q1 * β))
name: SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation_comp_eq_div_of_exchangeCommutator
docString:
**The `Statistics`-indexed presentation**, in terms of `exchangeCommutator s` rather than a
raw `ζ : ℂ` bracket — the form callers already holding a `Statistics` value should reach for.

statement:
∀ {Config : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Config] [inst_1 : Nonempty Config] (energy : Config → ℝ) (β q1 : ℝ) (ζ c1j : ℂ)
  (C1 Cj : SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config),
  SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy (-β) C1 = Complex.exp ↑(q1 * -β) • C1 →
    LinearMap.zetaCommutator ζ C1 Cj = c1j • LinearMap.id →
      SecondQuantization.Common.traceFock (SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy (-β)) ≠ 0 →
        1 - ζ * Complex.exp ↑(q1 * β) ≠ 0 →
          SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β (C1 ∘ₗ Cj) = c1j / (1 - ζ * Complex.exp ↑(q1 * β))
name: SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation_comp_eq_div_of_zetaCommutator
docString:
**The genuine normalized 2-point Bloch–de Dominicis value**: `⟨C₁Cⱼ⟩ = c₁ⱼ/(1 - ζw₁)`,
dividing `Unnormalized/TwoPoint.lean`'s `(1 - ζw₁) Tr[e^{-βH₀}(C₁Cⱼ)] = c₁ⱼ Tr[e^{-βH₀}]` through
by the genuine (nonzero) partition function and by the (assumed nonzero) `1 - ζw₁` factor —
matching the physics reference notes' `⟨Ĉ₁Ĉⱼ⟩ = C_{1,j}/(1 - ζw₁)` letter-for-letter rather than
leaving it as an un-divided trace equation.

statement:
∀ {Config : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Config] [inst_1 : Nonempty Config] (energy : Config → ℝ) (β q1 : ℝ)
  (ζ c12 c13 c14 : ℂ)
  (C1 C2 C3 C4 : SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config),
  SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy (-β) C1 = Complex.exp ↑(q1 * -β) • C1 →
    C1 ∘ₗ C2 - ζ • C2 ∘ₗ C1 = c12 • LinearMap.id →
      C1 ∘ₗ C3 - ζ • C3 ∘ₗ C1 = c13 • LinearMap.id →
        C1 ∘ₗ C4 - ζ • C4 ∘ₗ C1 = c14 • LinearMap.id →
          ζ ^ 2 = 1 →
            SecondQuantization.Common.traceFock (SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy (-β)) ≠ 0 →
              1 - ζ * Complex.exp ↑(q1 * β) ≠ 0 →
                SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β (C1 ∘ₗ C2 ∘ₗ C3 ∘ₗ C4) =
                  SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β (C1 ∘ₗ C2) *
                        SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β (C3 ∘ₗ C4) +
                      ζ * SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β (C1 ∘ₗ C3) *
                        SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β (C2 ∘ₗ C4) +
                    SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β (C1 ∘ₗ C4) *
                      SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β (C2 ∘ₗ C3)
name: SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation_four_point
docString: The genuine normalized 4-point Bloch–de Dominicis expansion.

  (a b : ℝ),
  (∀ (n : Config),
      IntervalIntegrable (fun τ => SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff (F τ) n n) MeasureTheory.volume a b) →
    SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β
        (SecondQuantization.Common.operatorIntervalIntegral F a b) =
