statement:
∀ {Config : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Config] [inst_1 : Nonempty Config] (energy : Config → ℝ) (β q1 : ℝ) (ζ : ℂ)
  (C1 : SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config)
  (l :
    List ((SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config) × ℂ)),
  SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy (-β) C1 = Complex.exp ↑(q1 * -β) • C1 →
    (∀ p ∈ l, LinearMap.zetaCommutator ζ C1 p.1 = p.2 • LinearMap.id) →
      SecondQuantization.Common.traceFock (SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy (-β)) ≠ 0 →
        1 - ζ ^ l.length * Complex.exp ↑(q1 * β) ≠ 0 →
          SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β
              (C1 ∘ₗ SecondQuantization.Common.prodComp (List.map Prod.fst l)) =
            SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β (SecondQuantization.Common.peelSum ζ l) /
              (1 - ζ ^ l.length * Complex.exp ↑(q1 * β))
name: SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation_peel
docString: The normalized peel-first identity in the canonical finite Gibbs density state.

statement:
∀ {Config : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Config] [inst_1 : Nonempty Config] (energy : Config → ℝ) (β : ℝ) (ζ : ℂ)
  (l :
    List ((SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config) × ℂ)),
  SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β (SecondQuantization.Common.peelSum ζ l) =
    ∑ j,
      ζ ^ ↑j * l[↑j].2 *
        SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β
          (SecondQuantization.Common.prodComp (List.map Prod.fst (l.eraseIdx ↑j)))
name: SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation_peelSum_eq_sum

statement:
∀ {Config : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Config] [inst_1 : Nonempty Config] (energy : Config → ℝ) (β q1 : ℝ) (ζ : ℂ)
  (C1 : SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config)
  (l :
    List ((SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config) × ℂ)),
  SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy (-β) C1 = Complex.exp ↑(q1 * -β) • C1 →
    (∀ p ∈ l, LinearMap.zetaCommutator ζ C1 p.1 = p.2 • LinearMap.id) →
      SecondQuantization.Common.traceFock (SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy (-β)) ≠ 0 →
        1 - ζ ^ l.length * Complex.exp ↑(q1 * β) ≠ 0 →
          SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β
              (C1 ∘ₗ SecondQuantization.Common.prodComp (List.map Prod.fst l)) =
            (∑ j,
                ζ ^ ↑j * l[↑j].2 *
                  SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation energy β
                    (SecondQuantization.Common.prodComp (List.map Prod.fst (l.eraseIdx ↑j)))) /
              (1 - ζ ^ l.length * Complex.exp ↑(q1 * β))
name: SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation_peel_indexed
docString: The normalized peel identity, as an indexed `Finset.sum`.

    SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy τ A ∘ₗ SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy τ B
name: SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve_comp
docString:
**`heisenbergEvolve` distributes over composition**: `(AB)(τ) = A(τ) B(τ)`, since the
`e^{-τH₀} e^{τH₀}` inserted between `A` and `B` cancels. Purely algebraic — no `Fintype Config`
needed, since it only rearranges `LinearMap.comp` associativity and cancels
`diagonalEvolution_neg_comp`.

statement:
∀ {Config : Type u_1} (energy : Config → ℝ) (s t : ℝ)
  (A : SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config),
  SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy t (SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy s A) =
    SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy (s + t) A
name: SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve_heisenbergEvolve
docString:
**`heisenbergEvolve` is a one-parameter semigroup**: `A(s)(t) = A(s + t)`, i.e.
`heisenbergEvolve energy t (heisenbergEvolve energy s A) = heisenbergEvolve energy (s + t) A`.
The coefficient formula above is valid for arbitrary `Config`, so no global finiteness assumption
is needed.

  (create annihilate :
    Mode → SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config)
  (g : SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticVertexLabel Mode → ℂ),
  SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy τ
      (SecondQuantization.Common.quarticInteraction create annihilate g) =
    ∑ q,
      g q •
        SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy τ
          (SecondQuantization.Common.quarticVertexOperator create annihilate q)

docString: Diagonal Heisenberg evolution distributes over the all-label finite-mode interaction.

statement:

    Mode → SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config)
  (g : SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticVertexLabel Mode → ℂ),
  SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy τ
      (SecondQuantization.Common.quarticInteractionOn support create annihilate g) =
    ∑ q ∈ support,
      g q •
        SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy τ
          (SecondQuantization.Common.quarticVertexOperator create annihilate q)

docString: Diagonal Heisenberg evolution distributes over a finitely supported quartic interaction.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} {Config : Type u_2} (energy : Config → ℝ) (ε : Mode → ℝ)
  (create annihilate :
    Mode → SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config)
  (q : SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticVertexLabel Mode) (l : Fin 4) (τ : ℝ),
  (∀ (i : Mode),
      SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy τ (create i) = Complex.exp (↑τ * ↑(ε i)) • create i) →
    (∀ (i : Mode),
        SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy τ (annihilate i) =
          Complex.exp (-↑τ * ↑(ε i)) • annihilate i) →
      SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy τ
          (SecondQuantization.Common.quarticLocalLegOperator create annihilate q l) =
        Complex.exp ↑(τ * SecondQuantization.Common.quarticLocalLegEnergyShift ε q l) •
          SecondQuantization.Common.quarticLocalLegOperator create annihilate q l

docString: A local quartic leg assembled from ladder eigenoperators evolves with its signed energy shift.

statement:

      SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy τ (create i) = Complex.exp (↑τ * ↑(ε i)) • create i) →
    (∀ (i : Mode),
        SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy τ (annihilate i) =

          (SecondQuantization.Common.quarticVertexOperator create annihilate q) =

          SecondQuantization.Common.quarticVertexOperator create annihilate q

`AlgebraicFock Config` vector is finitely supported even when `Config` itself is infinite.

**`diagonalEvolution`'s matrix coefficients**: diagonal, `exp(τ · energy n)` on the diagonal
and `0` off it — the algebraic content of "`diagonalEvolution` acts on each basis state by a
scalar". Specialized to `energy := freeEigenvalue`/`fermionEnergy`, `τ := -β`, the same formula
provides the basis-diagonal Gibbs-weight coefficients.

statement:
∀ {Config : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Config] (energy : Config → ℝ)
  (V : SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config) (n : ℕ)
  (τ : ℝ) (m n' : Config),
  SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff (SecondQuantization.Common.dysonCoeff energy V (n + 1) τ) m n' =
    -∫ (σ : ℝ) in 0..τ,
        ∑ k,
          SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff (SecondQuantization.Common.interactionPicture energy V σ) m k *
            SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff (SecondQuantization.Common.dysonCoeff energy V n σ) k n'

docString: Matrix-coefficient form of the finite Dyson successor recursion.

name: SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff_ext

statement:
∀ {Config : Type u_1} (energy : Config → ℝ) (τ : ℝ)
  (A : SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config)
  (m n : Config),
  SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff (SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy τ A) m n =
    Complex.exp ↑(τ * (energy m - energy n)) * SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff A m n

**`heisenbergEvolve`'s matrix coefficients**: `A(τ)`'s `(m, n)` entry is `A`'s own `(m, n)`
entry, rescaled by `exp(τ(energy m - energy n))` — the interaction-picture matrix-coefficient
formula, for an arbitrary configuration type. The proof evaluates the two diagonal evolutions
directly on a finitely supported algebraic-Fock vector, rather than summing over all configurations.

    Complex.exp ↑(τ * (energy m - energy n)) * SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff V m n

Matrix coefficients acquire the exponential of the free energy difference.  No `Fintype`
assumption on `Config` is needed.

∀ {Config : Type u_1} (ζ : ℂ)

docString:
**`peelSum` is the sum of its `peelTerms`** — the closed-form counterpart of `peelSum`'s
recursive definition, `Σⱼ ζʲcⱼ•(remaining product with `Bⱼ` erased)` as a `List.sum` rather than
an index/`Finset.sum`-over-erasures formula (`l.eraseIdx`) matching the physics notes'
`Σⱼ ζʲc₁ⱼ⟨…Ĉⱼ…⟩` presentation letter-for-letter (`PeelTermsIndexed.lean`'s `peelTerms_eq_ofFn`
gives that indexed form).

statement:

  (l :
    List ((SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config) × ℂ)),
  SecondQuantization.Common.peelTerms ζ l =
    List.ofFn fun j => ζ ^ ↑j • l[↑j].2 • SecondQuantization.Common.prodComp (List.map Prod.fst (l.eraseIdx ↑j))
name: SecondQuantization.Common.peelTerms_eq_ofFn
docString:
**`peelTerms`'s `j`-th term, in closed form**: `ζʲ • cⱼ • (remaining product with the `j`-th
operator erased)`, matching the physics reference notes' `Σⱼ ζʲc₁ⱼ⟨…Ĉⱼ…⟩` presentation
term-by-term.

      Combinatorics.permutationConnectedCycleSeries ζ (SecondQuantization.Common.freeBoltzmannModeKernel ε β) =
        -ζ⁻¹ • ∑ i, (PowerSeries.rescale (-ζ * Complex.exp (-↑β * ↑(ε i)))) (PowerSeries.log ℂ)

For the shared diagonal free Boltzmann kernel and nonzero exchange weight `ζ`, the connected-cycle
series is the modewise formal trace-log

docString:
**Swapping the pair of operators (with their times) and multiplying by the exchange sign
returns the same time-ordered product**:
`T_τ[B(τ_B) A(τ_A)] = s.zetaInt · T_τ[A(τ_A) B(τ_B)]`.
`Statistics.zeta_sq` supplies the fact that the exchange sign squares to one. See the module
docstring's scope note on which operators admit the usual physical reading.

  (A : SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config),

docString: `Tr[e^{-βH₀}A]` is the Boltzmann-weighted diagonal trace of `A`.

statement:
∀ {Config : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Config] (energy : Config → ℝ) (β q1 : ℝ) (ζ : ℂ)
  (C1 : SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config)
  (l :
    List ((SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config) × ℂ)),
  SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy (-β) C1 = Complex.exp ↑(q1 * -β) • C1 →
    (∀ p ∈ l, LinearMap.zetaCommutator ζ C1 p.1 = p.2 • LinearMap.id) →
      (1 - ζ ^ l.length * Complex.exp ↑(q1 * β)) *
          SecondQuantization.Common.traceFock
            (SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy (-β) ∘ₗ
              C1 ∘ₗ SecondQuantization.Common.prodComp (List.map Prod.fst l)) =
        SecondQuantization.Common.traceFock
          (SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy (-β) ∘ₗ SecondQuantization.Common.peelSum ζ l)
name: SecondQuantization.Common.traceFock_diagonalEvolution_comp_peel
docString:
**The trace-level peel-first identity**: `Common.traceFock_diagonalEvolution_comp_rotate`
applied to the whole remaining product `B₁⋯Bₖ` (rotating `C₁` from the end back to the front)
combined with `comp_prodComp_eq_of_zetaCommutator`'s operator identity, solving the resulting
self-referential equation for `Tr[e^{-βH₀}(C₁B₁⋯Bₖ)]`.

statement:
∀ {Config : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Config] (energy : Config → ℝ) (β q : ℝ)
  (A C : SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config),
  SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy (-β) C = Complex.exp ↑(q * -β) • C →
    SecondQuantization.Common.traceFock (SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy (-β) ∘ₗ A ∘ₗ C) =
      Complex.exp ↑(q * β) •
        SecondQuantization.Common.traceFock (SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy (-β) ∘ₗ C ∘ₗ A)
name: SecondQuantization.Common.traceFock_diagonalEvolution_comp_rotate
docString:
**The KMS-type trace rotation**: `Tr[e^{-βH₀} (A C)] = e^{qβ} Tr[e^{-βH₀} (C A)]`, for any
operator `A` and any operator `C` with eigenvalue-shift `q` under `heisenbergEvolve`. Combines
`traceFock_comp_comm` (cyclicity) with `comp_diagonalEvolution_eq_smul_diagonalEvolution_comp` (the
KMS-type relation) exactly as the physics reference notes' `⟨Ĉ₂⋯Ĉ_{2n}Ĉ₁⟩ = w₁⟨Ĉ₁Ĉ₂⋯Ĉ_{2n}⟩` step
does.

statement:
∀ {Config : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Config] (energy : Config → ℝ) (β q1 : ℝ) (ζ c1j : ℂ)
  (C1 Cj : SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config),
  SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy (-β) C1 = Complex.exp ↑(q1 * -β) • C1 →
    LinearMap.zetaCommutator ζ C1 Cj = c1j • LinearMap.id →
      (1 - ζ * Complex.exp ↑(q1 * β)) *
          SecondQuantization.Common.traceFock (SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy (-β) ∘ₗ C1 ∘ₗ Cj) =
        c1j * SecondQuantization.Common.traceFock (SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy (-β))
name: SecondQuantization.Common.traceFock_diagonalEvolution_comp_two_point
docString:
**The 2-point Bloch–de Dominicis base case**: `(1 - ζw₁) Tr[e^{-βH₀}(C₁Cⱼ)] = c₁ⱼ
Tr[e^{-βH₀}]`, where `c₁ⱼ` is the (assumed scalar) `ζ`-commutator `[C₁, Cⱼ]_ζ := C₁Cⱼ - ζCⱼC₁`,
and `w₁ := e^{q₁β}` is `C₁`'s thermal factor (`q₁` its eigenvalue shift). This is the
un-normalized, un-divided form of the physics reference notes' `⟨Ĉ₁Ĉⱼ⟩ = C_{1,j}/(1 - ζw₁)`
(`quantum-statistical-mechanics.tex`, the `n = 1` base case inside the general Bloch–de Dominicis
induction): derived from the assumed c-number commutator (rewriting `C₁Cⱼ` as `c₁ⱼ • id + ζ•(CⱼC₁)`)
and `traceFock_diagonalEvolution_comp_rotate` (rotating `CⱼC₁` back to `w₁•(C₁Cⱼ)`), then solving
the resulting self-referential equation for the trace — left un-divided (rather than requiring
`1 - ζw₁ ≠ 0` as a further hypothesis) so the caller decides how to use it.

statement:

name: SecondQuantization.Common.traceFock_diagonalEvolution_eq_weightSum
docString: The trace of the free diagonal evolution is the complex Boltzmann weight sum.

statement:
∀ {Config : Type u_1}
  {A B : SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config},
  (Summable fun n => SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff A n n) →
    (Summable fun n => SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff B n n) →
      SecondQuantization.Common.tsumTrace (A + B) =
        SecondQuantization.Common.tsumTrace A + SecondQuantization.Common.tsumTrace B
name: SecondQuantization.Common.tsumTrace_add
docString: `tsumTrace` is additive when both diagonal families are summable.

  (A B : SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config),
  Summable
      (Function.uncurry fun n k =>
        SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff A n k * SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff B k n) →
    SecondQuantization.Common.tsumTrace (A ∘ₗ B) = SecondQuantization.Common.tsumTrace (B ∘ₗ A)
name: SecondQuantization.Common.tsumTrace_comp_comm
docString:
**Cyclicity under a two-operator swap**, assuming absolute double summability:
`Tr'[AB] = Tr'[BA]`.

statement:
∀ {Config : Type u_1} (energy : Config → ℝ) (β q1 : ℝ) (ζ : ℂ)
  (C1 : SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config)
  (l :
    List ((SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config) × ℂ)),
  SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy (-β) C1 = Complex.exp ↑(q1 * -β) • C1 →
    (∀ p ∈ l, LinearMap.zetaCommutator ζ C1 p.1 = p.2 • LinearMap.id) →
      (Summable fun n =>
          SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff
            (SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy (-β) ∘ₗ SecondQuantization.Common.peelSum ζ l) n n) →
        Summable
            (Function.uncurry fun n k =>
              SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff
                  (SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy (-β) ∘ₗ
                    SecondQuantization.Common.prodComp (List.map Prod.fst l))
                  n k *
                SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff C1 k n) →
          (1 - ζ ^ l.length * Complex.exp ↑(q1 * β)) *
              SecondQuantization.Common.tsumTrace
                (SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy (-β) ∘ₗ
                  C1 ∘ₗ SecondQuantization.Common.prodComp (List.map Prod.fst l)) =
            SecondQuantization.Common.tsumTrace
              (SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy (-β) ∘ₗ SecondQuantization.Common.peelSum ζ l)
name: SecondQuantization.Common.tsumTrace_diagonalEvolution_comp_peel
docString:
**The `tsum` trace-level peel-first identity**: the `[Fintype Config]`-free analogue of
`traceFock_diagonalEvolution_comp_peel`, given the same `ζ`-commutator and KMS eigenvalue-shift
hypotheses plus explicit summability of `peelSum`'s own diagonal series (`hPeel`) and of the
rotation's double series (`hRotate`). Summability of the rotated tail's diagonal series (`n ↦
(e^{-βH₀}(B₁⋯Bₖ)C₁)ₙₙ`) is *not* a separate hypothesis — it follows from `hRotate` alone via
`summable_matrixCoeff_diag_comp_of_summable_uncurry`, mirroring `TwoPoint.lean`'s own `tsum`
theorem.

statement:
∀ {Config : Type u_1} (energy : Config → ℝ) (β q : ℝ)
  (A C : SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config),
  SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy (-β) C = Complex.exp ↑(q * -β) • C →
    Summable
        (Function.uncurry fun n k =>
          SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff (SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy (-β) ∘ₗ A) n k *
            SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff C k n) →
      SecondQuantization.Common.tsumTrace (SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy (-β) ∘ₗ A ∘ₗ C) =
        Complex.exp ↑(q * β) •
          SecondQuantization.Common.tsumTrace (SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy (-β) ∘ₗ C ∘ₗ A)
name: SecondQuantization.Common.tsumTrace_diagonalEvolution_comp_rotate
docString:
**The `tsum` KMS-type trace rotation**: the `[Fintype Config]`-free analogue of
`traceFock_diagonalEvolution_comp_rotate`, built from `Common.tsumTrace_comp_comm` instead of
`traceFock_comp_comm`. This lets the rotation step operate on a genuine bosonic occupation type at
the cost of the explicit double-summability hypothesis `h`, unlike the `[Fintype Config]` case
where summability is automatic.

statement:
∀ {Config : Type u_1} (energy : Config → ℝ) (β q1 : ℝ) (ζ c1j : ℂ)
  (C1 Cj : SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Common.AlgebraicFock Config),
  SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve energy (-β) C1 = Complex.exp ↑(q1 * -β) • C1 →
    LinearMap.zetaCommutator ζ C1 Cj = c1j • LinearMap.id →
      (Summable fun n =>
          SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff (SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy (-β)) n n) →
        Summable
            (Function.uncurry fun n k =>
              SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff (SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy (-β) ∘ₗ Cj) n
                  k *
                SecondQuantization.Common.matrixCoeff C1 k n) →
          (1 - ζ * Complex.exp ↑(q1 * β)) *
              SecondQuantization.Common.tsumTrace
                (SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy (-β) ∘ₗ C1 ∘ₗ Cj) =
            c1j * SecondQuantization.Common.tsumTrace (SecondQuantization.Common.diagonalEvolution energy (-β))
name: SecondQuantization.Common.tsumTrace_diagonalEvolution_comp_two_point
docString:
**The `tsum` 2-point Bloch–de Dominicis base case**: the `[Fintype Config]`-free analogue of
`traceFock_diagonalEvolution_comp_two_point`, given the same c-number-commutator and KMS-weight
hypotheses plus explicit summability of the partition-function diagonal series
(`n ↦ (e^{-βH₀})ₙₙ`, `hSummD`) and of the rotation's double series (`h`). Summability of the
rotated two-point diagonal series (`n ↦ (e^{-βH₀}CⱼC₁)ₙₙ`) is *not* a separate hypothesis — it
follows from `h` alone via `summable_matrixCoeff_diag_comp_of_summable_uncurry`, so only two
summability witnesses are needed rather than three.

For an odd tail, completed CAR exchange followed by KMS rotation solves the wrapped term.
The coefficient `g / (1 + g)` is the Fermi thermal factor attached to the leading ladder.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  (hsum : QuantumTheory.PurePointGibbsSummable (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fermionEnergy ε) β)
  (C₁ : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder Mode)
  (l : List (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder Mode)),
  SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder.completedFreeGibbsExpectation ε β hsum (C₁ :: l) =
    (QuantumTheory.purePointGibbsDensityOperator SecondQuantization.Fermionic.completedOccupationHilbertBasis
            (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fermionEnergy ε) β hsum).expectation
        (C₁.thermalPeelSum l) +
      (-1) ^ l.length *
        SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder.completedFreeGibbsExpectation ε β hsum (l ++ [C₁])
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder.completedFreeGibbsExpectation_cons_eq_peel_add_rotated

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  (hsum : QuantumTheory.PurePointGibbsSummable (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fermionEnergy ε) β) (n : ℕ)
  (C : Fin (2 * n) → SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder Mode),
  SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder.completedFreeGibbsAdmissible ε β n C →
    SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder.completedFreeGibbsExpectation ε β hsum (List.ofFn C) =
      ∑ pairing,
        Combinatorics.Pairing.weight SecondQuantization.Common.Statistics.fermion pairing *
          ∏ pr ∈ pairing.pairs,
            SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder.completedFreeGibbsExpectation ε β hsum [C pr.1, C pr.2]

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  (hsum : QuantumTheory.PurePointGibbsSummable (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fermionEnergy ε) β)
  (C : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder Mode)
  (A :
    ↥(SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedFockSpace Mode) →L[ℂ]
      ↥(SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedFockSpace Mode)),
  (QuantumTheory.purePointGibbsDensityOperator SecondQuantization.Fermionic.completedOccupationHilbertBasis
          (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fermionEnergy ε) β hsum).expectation
      (C.operator ∘SL A) =
    SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder.gibbsFactor ε β C *
      (QuantumTheory.purePointGibbsDensityOperator SecondQuantization.Fermionic.completedOccupationHilbertBasis
            (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fermionEnergy ε) β hsum).expectation
        (A ∘SL C.operator)
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder.completedFreeGibbsExpectation_operator_comp
docString:
Completed free-Gibbs KMS rotation for one thermal ladder and an arbitrary bounded operator:
`⟨C A⟩β = gβ(C) ⟨A C⟩β`.  The scalar `gβ(C)` is the same factor appearing in
`ρβ C = gβ(C) C ρβ`.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  (hsum : QuantumTheory.PurePointGibbsSummable (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fermionEnergy ε) β)
  (C D : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder Mode),
  1 + SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder.gibbsFactor ε β C ≠ 0 →
    SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder.completedFreeGibbsExpectation ε β hsum [C, D] =
      SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder.gibbsFactor ε β C /
          (1 + SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder.gibbsFactor ε β C) *
        C.anticommutatorValue D

The normalized two-point completed Gibbs expectation is the scalar CAR coefficient multiplied

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  (hsum : QuantumTheory.PurePointGibbsSummable (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fermionEnergy ε) β)
  (C₁ : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder Mode)
  (l : List (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder Mode)),
  (QuantumTheory.purePointGibbsDensityOperator SecondQuantization.Fermionic.completedOccupationHilbertBasis
          (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fermionEnergy ε) β hsum).expectation
      (C₁.thermalPeelSum l) =
    ∑ j,
      (-1) ^ ↑j * C₁.anticommutatorValue l[↑j] *
        SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedThermalLadder.completedFreeGibbsExpectation ε β hsum (l.eraseIdx ↑j)

Hamiltonian or continuum multiplication operator belong to the weak-continuity layer.

  (g : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.QuarticVertexLabel Mode → ℂ) (τ τ' : ℝ) (σ : Fin n → ℝ),
  d.dysonFixedTimeAmplitude ε β g τ τ' σ =
    d.mixedExternalDysonFixedTimeValue ε β g τ τ' σ *
      (SecondQuantization.Common.TwoPointDiagram.vacuumComponentParts ↑d).prod
        (d.mixedComponentDysonFixedTimeValue ε β g τ τ' σ)
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.FixedExternalTwoPointWickDiagram.dysonFixedTimeAmplitude_eq_external_mul_prod_vacuum
docString: External/vacuum factorization of the signed pointwise fixed-time amplitude.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] {n : ℕ} {i j : Mode}
  (d : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.FixedExternalTwoPointWickDiagram Mode n i j) (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  (g : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.QuarticVertexLabel Mode → ℂ) (τ τ' : ℝ) (σ : Fin n → ℝ),
  d.fixedTimeAmplitude ε β g τ τ' σ =

name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.FixedExternalTwoPointWickDiagram.fixedTimeAmplitude_eq_externalSign_mul_prod_components
docString:
The global fixed-time amplitude is the external ordering sign times the product of all
component-local fixed-time values.

docString: The signed pointwise amplitude of one diagram is measurably locally bounded.

statement:

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] {n : ℕ} {i j : Mode}

The Dyson-signed external factor is the standalone external piece's Dyson-signed fixed-time
amplitude at its inherited interaction times.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] {n : ℕ} {i j : Mode}

  (σ : Fin n → ℝ) (pr : (SecondQuantization.Common.TwoPointDiagram.pairingInMixedOrder (↑d) τ τ' σ).NormalizedPair),
  d.mixedPairContractionValue ε β τ τ' σ pr =
    SecondQuantization.Fermionic.orderedTwoPointLegPairContraction ε β i j τ τ' d.vertexLabelSequence σ
      ((SecondQuantization.Common.mixedTimeOrderedAtomicLegEquiv τ τ' σ) (↑pr).1)
      ((SecondQuantization.Common.mixedTimeOrderedAtomicLegEquiv τ τ' σ) (↑pr).2)

docString:
The contraction used by a normalized mixed pair is the density-state contraction of the two
fixed standard legs represented by its endpoints.

∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] {N : ℕ} (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)

  (orders : SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticDiagram.ComponentVertexOrders d)
  (shuffle : SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticDiagram.ComponentShuffle d) (τ : Fin S.card → ℝ),

      SecondQuantization.Fermionic.QuarticWickDiagram.contractionIntegrand ε β

The Wick contraction integrand of an assembled vertex order is the product of the contraction

statement:
∀ {Site : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} {ι : Type u_3} [inst : LinearOrder Site] [inst_1 : Fintype Site]
  [inst_2 : AddCommGroup E] [inst_3 : _root_.Module ℝ E] [inst_4 : Fintype ι]
  {convention : QuantumTheory.Transport.PositiveVolume}
  {system :
    QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.BoundedFreeSystem (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.FiniteLatticeHilbertFock Site)}
  {data : QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.PurePointLehmannData system ι}
  {geometry : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.LatticeGeometry Site E} {direction : E →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ}
  {K : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.LocallyFiniteHopping Site} {q eta lowerEnergy upperEnergy : ℝ}
  {occupation : ℝ → ℂ},
  SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Transport.FiniteStaticPeierlsWardIdentity convention system data geometry direction K q
      eta lowerEnergy upperEnergy occupation →
    SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Transport.finiteStaticKuboBastinCurrentCurrentResponse system data geometry direction K
        q eta =
      ↑convention.volume * -↑eta *
          QuantumTheory.Transport.regularizedTracedBastinEnergyIntegral (↑system.hamiltonian)
            (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalCurrent geometry direction (↑system.hbar) (↑q) K)
            (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalCurrent geometry direction (↑system.hbar) (↑q) K)
            (QuantumTheory.Transport.kuboBastinEnergyBroadening system.hbar eta) lowerEnergy upperEnergy occupation -
        (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.purePointNormalizedExpectation system data).toContinuousLinearMap
          (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalContact geometry direction (↑system.hbar) (↑q) K)
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Transport.FiniteStaticPeierlsWardIdentity.currentCurrent_eq_scaledTracedBastin_sub_contact

  (convention : QuantumTheory.Transport.PositiveVolume)
  (system :
    QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.BoundedFreeSystem (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.FiniteLatticeHilbertFock Site))
  (data : QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.PurePointLehmannData system ι)

  (K : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.LocallyFiniteHopping Site) (q eta lowerEnergy upperEnergy : ℝ)
  (occupation : ℝ → ℂ),
  SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Transport.FiniteStaticPeierlsWardIdentity convention system data geometry direction K q
      eta lowerEnergy upperEnergy occupation →
    0 < eta →
      SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Transport.finiteStaticKuboBastinDirectionalConductivity convention system data
          geometry direction K q eta =
        QuantumTheory.Transport.regularizedBastinSpectralEnergyIntegral system data
          (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalCurrent geometry direction (↑system.hbar) (↑q) K)
          (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalCurrent geometry direction (↑system.hbar) (↑q) K)

docString: The same bridge written directly in the finite pure-point spectral energy-integral form.

          spectralData convention geometry direction K q eta =

∀ {Site : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} [inst : LinearOrder Site] [inst_1 : Fintype Site] [inst_2 : AddCommGroup E]

  (system :

  (expectation :
    QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.NormalizedExpectation
      (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.FiniteLatticeHilbertFock Site))
  (geometry : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.LatticeGeometry Site E) (direction : E →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ)
  (K : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.LocallyFiniteHopping Site),
  K.HasHermitianAmplitudes →
    ∀ (q ω η T : ℝ) {β M : ℝ},
      0 ≤ M →
        (∀ s ∈ Set.Icc 0 β,
            ‖QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.timeDependentInteractionPerturbation system
                  (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.sourceCoupledPerturbation
                    (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.adiabaticCosineSource ω η T)
                    (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalCurrent geometry direction (↑system.hbar)
                      (↑q) K))
                  s‖ ≤
              M) →
          T ∈ Set.Icc 0 β →
            IntervalIntegrable
                (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.timeDependentInteractionPerturbation system
                  (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.sourceCoupledPerturbation
                    (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.adiabaticCosineSource ω η T)
                    (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalCurrent geometry direction (↑system.hbar)
                      (↑q) K)))
                MeasureTheory.volume 0 T →
              HasDerivAt
                (fun lam =>
                  QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.affinePerturbedExpectation system expectation
                    (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.sourceCoupledPerturbation
                      (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.adiabaticCosineSource ω η T)
                      (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalCurrent geometry direction (↑system.hbar)
                        (↑q) K))
                    (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalCurrent geometry direction (↑system.hbar)
                      (↑q) K)
                    (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalContact geometry direction (↑system.hbar)
                      (↑q) K)
                    lam T)
                (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Transport.finiteTimeAdiabaticDirectionalCosineResponse system expectation
                  geometry direction K q ω η T)
                0

∀ {Site : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} [inst : LinearOrder Site] [inst_1 : Fintype Site] [inst_2 : AddCommGroup E]
  [inst_3 : _root_.Module ℝ E]
  (system :
    QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.BoundedFreeSystem (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.FiniteLatticeHilbertFock Site))
  (expectation :
    QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.NormalizedExpectation
      (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.FiniteLatticeHilbertFock Site))
  (f : ℝ → ℝ) (geometry : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.LatticeGeometry Site E) (direction : E →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ)
  (K : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.LocallyFiniteHopping Site),
  K.HasHermitianAmplitudes →
    ∀ (q : ℝ) {β M t : ℝ},
      0 ≤ M →
        (∀ s ∈ Set.Icc 0 β,
            ‖QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.timeDependentInteractionPerturbation system
                  (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.sourceCoupledPerturbation f
                    (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalCurrent geometry direction (↑system.hbar)
                      (↑q) K))
                  s‖ ≤
              M) →
          t ∈ Set.Icc 0 β →
            IntervalIntegrable
                (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.timeDependentInteractionPerturbation system
                  (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.sourceCoupledPerturbation f
                    (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalCurrent geometry direction (↑system.hbar)
                      (↑q) K)))
                MeasureTheory.volume 0 t →
              HasDerivAt
                (fun lam =>
                  QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.affinePerturbedExpectation system expectation
                    (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.sourceCoupledPerturbation f
                      (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalCurrent geometry direction (↑system.hbar)
                        (↑q) K))
                    (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalCurrent geometry direction (↑system.hbar)
                      (↑q) K)
                    (↑(f t) •
                      SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalContact geometry direction (↑system.hbar)
                        (↑q) K)
                    lam t)
                ((∫ (s : ℝ) in 0..t,
                    ↑(f s) *
                      QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.retardedSusceptibility system expectation
                        (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalCurrent geometry direction
                          (↑system.hbar) (↑q) K)
                        (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalCurrent geometry direction
                          (↑system.hbar) (↑q) K)
                        t s) +
                  expectation.toContinuousLinearMap
                    (QuantumTheory.LinearResponse.heisenbergEvolution system
                      (↑(f t) •
                        SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Lattice.boundedDirectionalContact geometry direction (↑system.hbar)
                          (↑q) K)
                      t))
                0

Retarded response of a geometric current component with the source-dependent geometric contact
term retained. Current self-adjointness is derived from Hermitian hopping and the real physical
charge rather than supplied externally.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  (hsum : QuantumTheory.PurePointGibbsSummable (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fermionEnergy ε) β) (i : Mode),
  (QuantumTheory.purePointGibbsDensityOperator SecondQuantization.Fermionic.completedOccupationHilbertBasis
          (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fermionEnergy ε) β hsum).op ∘SL
      SecondQuantization.Fermionic.completedAnnihilate i =
    Complex.exp (↑β * ↑(ε i)) •
      SecondQuantization.Fermionic.completedAnnihilate i ∘SL
        (QuantumTheory.purePointGibbsDensityOperator SecondQuantization.Fermionic.completedOccupationHilbertBasis
            (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fermionEnergy ε) β hsum).op

docString:
Completed free-Gibbs annihilation intertwining:
`ρβ aᵢ = exp (β εᵢ) aᵢ ρβ` as an identity of bounded operators.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  (hsum : QuantumTheory.PurePointGibbsSummable (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fermionEnergy ε) β)
  (A :
    ↥(SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedFockSpace Mode) →L[ℂ]
      ↥(SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedFockSpace Mode)),
  (QuantumTheory.purePointGibbsDensityOperator SecondQuantization.Fermionic.completedOccupationHilbertBasis
          (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fermionEnergy ε) β hsum).expectation
      A =
    ∑' (n : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Occupation Mode),
      ↑(QuantumTheory.purePointGibbsProbability (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fermionEnergy ε) β n) *
        inner ℂ (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.completedBasisState n)
          (A (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.completedBasisState n))
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.completedFreeGibbsDensityOperator_expectation_eq_tsum
docString:
Bounded-operator expectations in the completed free Gibbs state are the absolutely convergent
occupation-basis pure-point Gibbs series.

name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.continuous_matrixCoeff_nestedVertexOperatorComp
docString:
**Joint continuity, in the full time vector `τ`, of a matrix coefficient of
`nestedVertexOperatorComp`** — by induction on `n`: the base case is constant (`nested...Comp ε 0
q τ = LinearMap.id`); the successor case's matrix coefficient is a finite sum of products of a
single-coordinate `Complex.exp` factor (`Common.continuous_matrixCoeff_interactionPicture`,
precomposed with the coordinate-`0` projection) and the inductive hypothesis (precomposed with the
"tail" projection `fun i => τ i.succ`). `[Fintype Mode]` is genuinely used (for the finite sum
`Common.matrixCoeff_comp` needs), just not in the statement itself — the linter can't see that.

name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.create_basisState_of_mem
docString: **Pauli exclusion.** Creating a particle in an already-occupied mode annihilates the state.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] {i : Mode} {n : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Occupation Mode},
  i ∉ n →
    (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.create i) (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.basisState n) =
      ↑(SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fermionSign i n) •
        SecondQuantization.Fermionic.basisState (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.insertOccupation i n)
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.create_basisState_of_not_mem
docString:
**Creation raises the occupation.** Creating a particle in an unoccupied mode `i` produces
(up to the sign `fermionSign i n`) the basis state of `n` with `i` newly occupied — one more
particle than `n` (`particleNumber_insertOccupation_of_not_mem`).

docString: **`cᵢ† cᵢ† = 0`**: the same-mode consequence of `{cᵢ†, cᵢ†} = 0`.

statement:

docString:
**Creating twice in the same mode annihilates the state**, the basis-level shadow of Pauli
exclusion (`{aᵢ†, aᵢ†} = 0`, before the full CAR are stated in
`CanonicalAnticommutationRelations.lean`).

name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.create_fockVacuum
docString:
**Creating a particle in the vacuum** produces the single-particle basis state at mode `i`,
with sign `1` (no modes precede an empty occupation).

statement:

  (g : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.QuarticVertexLabel Mode → ℂ),

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Mode] {α : Type u_2} (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  (V : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.OccupationFock Mode →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Fermionic.OccupationFock Mode),
  SecondQuantization.Fermionic.dysonVertexMoment ε β V ∅ = 1
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.dysonVertexMoment_empty

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Mode] {α : Type u_2} (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  (V : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.OccupationFock Mode →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Fermionic.OccupationFock Mode)
  (S : Finset α),
  SecondQuantization.Fermionic.dysonVertexMoment ε β V S =
    ↑S.card.factorial *
      (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.freeGibbsDensityOperator ε β).expectation
        (SecondQuantization.Common.finiteHilbertOperator
          (SecondQuantization.Common.dysonCoeff (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fermionEnergy ε) V S.card β))
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.dysonVertexMoment_eq_freeGibbsDensityOperator_expectation
docString:
The Dyson vertex moment is the factorial times the canonical free Gibbs density-state
expectation of the bare Dyson coefficient at the corresponding order.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  (g : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.QuarticVertexLabel Mode → ℂ) {N : ℕ} (S : Finset (Fin N)),
  SecondQuantization.Fermionic.dysonVertexMoment ε β (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticInteraction g) S =
    ∑ d, SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticWickDiagramAmplitude ε β g d
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.dysonVertexMoment_quarticInteraction_eq_sum_quarticWickDiagramAmplitude
docString: Canonical direction of the Dyson-to-Wick-diagram expansion.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] {α : Type u_2} (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  (g : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.QuarticVertexLabel Mode → ℂ) (S : Finset α),
  SecondQuantization.Fermionic.dysonVertexMoment ε β (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticInteraction g) S =
    ↑S.card.factorial * (-1) ^ S.card *
      ∑ q,
        (∏ i, g (q i)) *
          ∑ pairing,
            intervalIntegral.orderedSimplexIntegral S.card β fun τ =>
              SecondQuantization.Fermionic.flatVertexLegPairingEvaluation ε β q τ pairing
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.dysonVertexMoment_quarticInteraction_eq_sum_vertexLabel_pairingEvaluation
docString: `dysonVertexMoment` of the quartic interaction in the canonical pairing-evaluator presentation.

statement:

The factorial-normalized coefficient of the formal logarithm of the normalized Dyson partition
series is its finite-set Dyson vertex cumulant.

statement:

  (g : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.QuarticVertexLabel Mode → ℂ) (n : ℕ),

At first order, the factorial-normalized logarithmic coefficient is the first normalized Dyson

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  (g : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.QuarticVertexLabel Mode → ℂ),

      (PowerSeries.coeff 3)
        (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.dysonFormalLogPartitionFunction ε β
          (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticInteraction g)) =
    6 *
          SecondQuantization.Fermionic.normalizedDysonPartitionCoeff ε β
            (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticInteraction g) 3 -

            SecondQuantization.Fermionic.normalizedDysonPartitionCoeff ε β
              (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticInteraction g) 1 *
          SecondQuantization.Fermionic.normalizedDysonPartitionCoeff ε β
            (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticInteraction g) 2 +
      2 *
        SecondQuantization.Fermionic.normalizedDysonPartitionCoeff ε β
            (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticInteraction g) 1 ^
          3
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.factorial_mul_coeff_dysonFormalLogPartitionFunction_order_three
docString: At third order, the logarithm removes the one-plus-two and three-singleton disconnected terms.

statement:

              SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fermionSign i (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.removeOccupation j n) +

`i, j`, the two orders of removing `i` then `j` (vs. `j` then `i`) pick up opposite signs.

statement:

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] {i j : Mode} (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  (g : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.QuarticVertexLabel Mode → ℂ) {n : ℕ} (T : Finset (Fin n))
  (ext : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.FixedExternalTwoPointWickDiagramOn Mode n T i j),
  SecondQuantization.Common.TwoPointDiagram.IsExternallyConnected ↑ext →
    ∀ (vac : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.QuarticWickDiagram Mode n (Finset.univ \ T)) (τ τ' : ℝ) (σ : Fin n → ℝ),
      StrictAnti (σ ∘ SecondQuantization.Common.slotSplitVacuumSlot T) →
        have d := SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fixedExternalOfSlotSplit T ext vac;
        d.dysonFixedTimeAmplitude ε β g τ τ' σ =
          d.externalPiece.dysonFixedTimeAmplitude ε β g τ τ'
              (SecondQuantization.Common.TwoPointDiagram.externalPieceTimes (↑d) σ) *
            ((-1) ^ (Finset.univ \ T).card * vac.couplingWeight g *
              SecondQuantization.Fermionic.QuarticWickDiagram.contractionIntegrand ε β vac
                (SecondQuantization.Common.slotSplitVacuumOrder T)
                (σ ∘ SecondQuantization.Common.slotSplitVacuumSlot T))

statement:

    ∀ (vac : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.QuarticWickDiagram Mode n (Finset.univ \ T)) (τ τ' : ℝ) (σ : Fin n → ℝ),

        have d := SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fixedExternalOfSlotSplit T ext vac;
        (SecondQuantization.Common.TwoPointDiagram.vacuumComponentParts ↑d).prod
            (d.mixedComponentDysonFixedTimeValue ε β g τ τ' σ) =

complete product of ambient vacuum-component Dyson fixed-time values is exactly the standalone
fixed-order quartic vacuum integrand, including its Dyson sign and coupling prefactor.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] {i j : Mode} (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ),
  0 ≤ β →
    ∀ (g : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.QuarticVertexLabel Mode → ℂ) (τ τ' : ℝ) {m k : ℕ}
      (shuffle : Combinatorics.BinaryShuffle.SlotShuffle m k)
      (ext : { d // SecondQuantization.Common.TwoPointDiagram.IsExternallyConnected ↑d })
      (x :
        SecondQuantization.Common.OrderedQuarticDiagramData (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.QuarticVertexLabel Mode) k),
      have p := (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fixedExternalShuffleFiberDataEquiv shuffle).symm (ext, x);
      have d := (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fixedExternalFiberEquiv shuffle.leftSlots).symm p;
      (↑d).dysonAmplitude ε β g τ τ' =
        intervalIntegral.orderedSimplexIntegral (m + k) β
          (shuffle.integrand (fun σ => (↑ext).dysonFixedTimeAmplitude ε β g τ τ' σ)
            (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.orderedVacuumDysonIntegrand ε β g x))

docString: **One fixed shuffle fiber is exactly the corresponding binary shuffled product integral.**

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] {n : ℕ} (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  (q : Fin n → SecondQuantization.Fermionic.QuarticVertexLabel Mode) (τ : Fin n → ℝ) (a b : Fin (2 * (2 * n))),
  SecondQuantization.Fermionic.flatVertexLegPairValue ε β q τ a b =
    Complex.exp
          ↑(τ (SecondQuantization.Common.flatVertexIndex n a) *
              SecondQuantization.Fermionic.flatVertexLegEnergyShift ε q a) *
        Complex.exp
          ↑(τ (SecondQuantization.Common.flatVertexIndex n b) *
              SecondQuantization.Fermionic.flatVertexLegEnergyShift ε q b) *
      (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.freeGibbsDensityOperator ε β).expectation
        (SecondQuantization.Common.finiteHilbertOperator
          (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticLocalLegOperator (q (SecondQuantization.Common.flatVertexIndex n a))
              (SecondQuantization.Common.flatLocalLeg n a) ∘ₗ
            SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticLocalLegOperator (q (SecondQuantization.Common.flatVertexIndex n b))
              (SecondQuantization.Common.flatLocalLeg n b)))

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  (g : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.QuarticVertexLabel Mode → ℂ) (n : ℕ) (t : ℝ)
  (L : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.OccupationFock Mode →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Fermionic.OccupationFock Mode),

        (L ∘ₗ

    HasSum (fun n => QuantumTheory.purePointGibbsProbability (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fermionEnergy ε) β n * a n)
      (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.completedFreeGibbsDiagonalExpectation ε β a)
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.hasSum_completedFreeGibbsDiagonalExpectation
docString: An integrable real diagonal observable has the expected occupation-basis `HasSum`.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ),
  SecondQuantization.Fermionic.CompletedFreeTotalNumberIntegrable ε β →
    HasSum
      (fun n =>
        QuantumTheory.purePointGibbsProbability (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fermionEnergy ε) β n *
          ↑(SecondQuantization.Fermionic.particleNumber n))
      (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.completedFreeTotalNumberExpectation ε β)
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.hasSum_completedFreeTotalNumberExpectation
docString:
Under the explicit number-integrability hypothesis, the total particle-number expectation is
represented by an absolutely convergent occupation-basis series.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) {β : ℝ},
  0 ≤ β →
    ∀ (V : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.OccupationFock Mode →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Fermionic.OccupationFock Mode)
      (lam : ℂ),
      HasSum
        (fun n =>
          lam ^ n * SecondQuantization.Common.dysonTraceCoeff (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fermionEnergy ε) β V n)
        (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.analyticDysonPartitionFunction ε β V lam)
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.hasSum_dysonTraceCoeff_eq_analyticDysonPartitionFunction
docString: The specialized Common Dyson trace coefficients sum to the analytic partition function.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  (q : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.QuarticVertexLabel Mode) (l : Fin 4) (τ : ℝ),
  SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fermionEnergy ε) (-β)
      (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.imaginaryTimeEvolve ε τ
        (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticLocalLegOperator q l)) =
    Complex.exp ↑(SecondQuantization.Common.quarticLocalLegEnergyShift ε q l * -β) •
      SecondQuantization.Fermionic.imaginaryTimeEvolve ε τ (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticLocalLegOperator q l)
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.heisenbergEvolve_imaginaryTimeEvolve_quarticLocalLegOperator
docString:
**A single evolved atomic leg operator is an eigenoperator of `heisenbergEvolve (fermionEnergy
ε) (-β)`, with an eigenvalue shift *independent of the dressing time* `τ`** — the fact the general
Bloch–de Dominicis theorem needs after specializing to each flattened leg. Proved via
`Common.heisenbergEvolve_heisenbergEvolve` (the two evolutions, at `τ` and `-β`, combine into a
single evolution at `τ + (-β)`) and `imaginaryTimeEvolve_quarticLocalLegOperator` (applied twice:
once at `τ + (-β)` to evaluate the combined evolution, once at `τ` in reverse to factor the
`τ`-dependent piece back out) — the two resulting `Complex.exp`s combine via `exp_add`/`ring`,
leaving only the `-β`-dependent factor.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  (field : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.TimedField Mode),
  SecondQuantization.Common.heisenbergEvolve (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fermionEnergy ε) (-β)
      (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.timedFieldOperator ε field) =
    Complex.exp ↑(SecondQuantization.Fermionic.externalFieldLabelEnergyShift ε field.label * -β) •
      SecondQuantization.Fermionic.timedFieldOperator ε field
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.heisenbergEvolve_timedFieldOperator
docString: A time-labelled field remains an eigenoperator after a further evolution by `-β`.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} (ε : Mode → ℝ) (τ : ℝ) (n : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Occupation Mode),
  (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.imaginaryTimeEvolveFree ε τ) (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.basisState n) =
    Complex.exp (↑τ * ∑ i ∈ n, ↑(ε i)) • SecondQuantization.Fermionic.basisState n
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.imaginaryTimeEvolveFree_basisState

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) (τ : ℝ) (i : Mode),
  SecondQuantization.Fermionic.imaginaryTimeEvolveFree ε τ ∘ₗ SecondQuantization.Fermionic.annihilate i =
    Complex.exp (-↑τ * ↑(ε i)) •
      SecondQuantization.Fermionic.annihilate i ∘ₗ SecondQuantization.Fermionic.imaginaryTimeEvolveFree ε τ
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.imaginaryTimeEvolveFree_comp_annihilate
docString:
**The KMS-type relation for the annihilation operator**: `e^{τH₀} c_i = e^{-τε_i} c_i e^{τH₀}`
— an instance of `Common.diagonalEvolution_comp_eq_smul_comp_diagonalEvolution`, from
`imaginaryTimeEvolve_annihilate`'s eigenvalue-shift `q := -ε_i`. Setting `τ := -β` and rearranging
gives the physics reference notes' `ĉ_i e^{-βĤ} = e^{-βε_i} e^{-βĤ} ĉ_i}`
(`quantum-statistical-mechanics.tex`'s "product-of-KMS-state-and-ladder-op"), the algebraic
ingredient the finite-temperature Bloch–de Dominicis theorem's induction needs to move a ladder
operator through the (would-be) Gibbs weight `e^{-βH₀}`.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) (τ : ℝ) (i : Mode),
  SecondQuantization.Fermionic.imaginaryTimeEvolveFree ε τ ∘ₗ SecondQuantization.Fermionic.create i =
    Complex.exp (↑τ * ↑(ε i)) •
      SecondQuantization.Fermionic.create i ∘ₗ SecondQuantization.Fermionic.imaginaryTimeEvolveFree ε τ
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.imaginaryTimeEvolveFree_comp_create
docString:
**The KMS-type relation for the creation operator**: `e^{τH₀} c_i† = e^{τε_i} c_i† e^{τH₀}`,
the creation-side mirror of `imaginaryTimeEvolveFree_comp_annihilate`.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) (τ : ℝ) (i : Mode),
  SecondQuantization.Fermionic.imaginaryTimeEvolve ε τ (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.annihilate i) =
    Complex.exp (-↑τ * ↑(ε i)) • SecondQuantization.Fermionic.annihilate i
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.imaginaryTimeEvolve_annihilate
docString:
**The imaginary-time-evolved annihilation operator**: `c_i(τ) = e^{-τε_i} c_i`. The physical
content of the free-theory Heisenberg equation of motion `d/dτ c_i(τ) = [H₀, c_i(τ)] = -ε_i c_i(τ)`,
proved here directly from the basis-level action rather than by solving that ODE.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} (ε : Mode → ℝ) (τ : ℝ)
  (A : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.OccupationFock Mode →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Fermionic.OccupationFock Mode)
  (x : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.OccupationFock Mode),
  (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.imaginaryTimeEvolve ε τ A) x =
    (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.imaginaryTimeEvolveFree ε τ)
      (A ((SecondQuantization.Fermionic.imaginaryTimeEvolveFree ε (-τ)) x))
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.imaginaryTimeEvolve_apply
docString:
Unfolds `imaginaryTimeEvolve` back down to `imaginaryTimeEvolveFree`, matching the shape most
proofs below need — `A(τ) := e^{τH₀} A e^{-τH₀}`, applied to a vector.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) (τ : ℝ) (i : Mode),
  SecondQuantization.Fermionic.imaginaryTimeEvolve ε τ (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.create i) =
    Complex.exp (↑τ * ↑(ε i)) • SecondQuantization.Fermionic.create i
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.imaginaryTimeEvolve_create
docString: **The imaginary-time-evolved creation operator**: `c_i†(τ) = e^{τε_i} c_i†`.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} (ε : Mode → ℝ) (τ : ℝ),
  SecondQuantization.Fermionic.imaginaryTimeEvolve ε τ (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.freeHamiltonian ε) =
    SecondQuantization.Fermionic.freeHamiltonian ε
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.imaginaryTimeEvolve_freeHamiltonian
docString:
**The free Hamiltonian evolves trivially under its own flow**: `H₀(τ) = H₀`, since `H₀` is
diagonal in the very basis `e^{τH₀}` acts on by a scalar.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_2} (ε : Mode → ℝ) (Vint : Mode → Mode → ℝ) (τ : ℝ),
  SecondQuantization.Fermionic.imaginaryTimeEvolve ε τ (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.interactionHamiltonian Vint) =
    SecondQuantization.Fermionic.interactionHamiltonian Vint
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.imaginaryTimeEvolve_interactionHamiltonian
docString: `interactionHamiltonian` is time-independent under free imaginary-time evolution.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) (q : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.QuarticVertexLabel Mode)
  (l : Fin 4) (τ : ℝ),
  SecondQuantization.Fermionic.imaginaryTimeEvolve ε τ (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticLocalLegOperator q l) =
    Complex.exp ↑(τ * SecondQuantization.Common.quarticLocalLegEnergyShift ε q l) •

name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.imaginaryTimeEvolve_quarticLocalLegOperator
docString: A local leg is an eigenoperator of the free imaginary-time evolution.

statement:

Inner product with a completed occupation basis vector in the first slot evaluates the
corresponding coordinate.

statement:

name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.interactionHamiltonian_basisState

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ)
  (g : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.QuarticVertexLabel Mode → ℂ) (τ : ℝ),
  SecondQuantization.Fermionic.interactionPicture ε (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticInteraction g) τ =
    ∑ q,
      g q • SecondQuantization.Fermionic.interactionPicture ε (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticVertexOperator q) τ
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.interactionPicture_quarticInteraction
docString: **The quartic interaction's interaction-picture expansion** as the evolved all-label finite sum.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) (q : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.QuarticVertexLabel Mode)
  (τ : ℝ),
  SecondQuantization.Fermionic.interactionPicture ε (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticVertexOperator q) τ =
    Complex.exp (↑τ * (↑(ε q.create₁) + ↑(ε q.create₂) - ↑(ε q.annihilate₁) - ↑(ε q.annihilate₂))) •
      SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticVertexOperator q
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.interactionPicture_quarticVertexOperator
docString: **A single quartic vertex's interaction-picture expansion** with the total free-energy shift.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) (q : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.QuarticVertexLabel Mode)
  (τ : ℝ),
  SecondQuantization.Fermionic.interactionPicture ε (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticVertexOperator q) τ =
    SecondQuantization.Common.prodComp
      (List.ofFn fun l =>
        SecondQuantization.Fermionic.imaginaryTimeEvolve ε τ (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticLocalLegOperator q l))
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.interactionPicture_quarticVertexOperator_eq_prodComp
docString:
**A single vertex's evolved operator, flattened into a `Common.prodComp` of its four
individually-evolved atomic legs**: unfolds `quarticVertexOperator`'s own definition
(`c₁† c₂† a₂ a₁`) via `Common.heisenbergEvolve_comp`, three times, matching
`quarticLocalLegOperator`'s `0 ↦ create₁, 1 ↦ create₂, 2 ↦ annihilate₂, 3 ↦ annihilate₁`
convention exactly.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) {β : ℝ},
  0 ≤ β →
    ∀ (V : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.OccupationFock Mode →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Fermionic.OccupationFock Mode)
      (n : ℕ),
      iteratedDeriv n (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.analyticNormalizedLogPartitionFunction ε β V) 0 =
        ↑n.factorial * (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.analyticNormalizedLogFPowerSeries ε β V).coeff n
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.iteratedDeriv_analyticNormalizedLogPartitionFunction_eq_factorial_mul_coeff
docString:
The `n`-th derivative of the analytic logarithm is `n!` times the scalar coefficient of its
composed Taylor series.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) {β : ℝ},
  0 ≤ β →
    ∀ (V : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.OccupationFock Mode →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Fermionic.OccupationFock Mode)
      (n : ℕ),
      iteratedDeriv n (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.analyticNormalizedLogPartitionFunction ε β V) 0 =
        ↑n.factorial * (PowerSeries.coeff n) (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.dysonFormalLogPartitionFunction ε β V)
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.iteratedDeriv_analyticNormalizedLogPartitionFunction_eq_factorial_mul_formalCoeff
docString: Taylor-coefficient form of the analytic/formal logarithm bridge.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) {β : ℝ},
  0 ≤ β →
    ∀ (V : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.OccupationFock Mode →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Fermionic.OccupationFock Mode)
      (n : ℕ),
      iteratedDeriv n (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.analyticNormalizedLogPartitionFunction ε β V) 0 =
        Combinatorics.powerSeriesCumulantCoeff
          (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.dysonPartitionSeries ε β V).normalizeByConstantCoeff n
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.iteratedDeriv_analyticNormalizedLogPartitionFunction_eq_powerSeriesCumulantCoeff
docString:
The analytic logarithmic derivatives equal the exponential-generating coefficients of the
formal logarithm of the normalized Dyson partition series.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) {β : ℝ},
  0 ≤ β →
    ∀ (g : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.QuarticVertexLabel Mode → ℂ),
      iteratedDeriv 1
          (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.analyticNormalizedLogPartitionFunction ε β
            (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticInteraction g))
          0 =
        SecondQuantization.Fermionic.normalizedDysonPartitionCoeff ε β
          (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticInteraction g) 1
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.iteratedDeriv_analyticNormalizedLogPartitionFunction_order_one
docString: First derivative of the analytic normalized logarithm.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) {β : ℝ},
  0 ≤ β →
    ∀ (g : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.QuarticVertexLabel Mode → ℂ),
      iteratedDeriv 3
          (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.analyticNormalizedLogPartitionFunction ε β
            (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticInteraction g))
          0 =
        6 *
              SecondQuantization.Fermionic.normalizedDysonPartitionCoeff ε β
                (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticInteraction g) 3 -
            6 *
                SecondQuantization.Fermionic.normalizedDysonPartitionCoeff ε β
                  (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticInteraction g) 1 *
              SecondQuantization.Fermionic.normalizedDysonPartitionCoeff ε β
                (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticInteraction g) 2 +
          2 *
            SecondQuantization.Fermionic.normalizedDysonPartitionCoeff ε β
                (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticInteraction g) 1 ^
              3
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.iteratedDeriv_analyticNormalizedLogPartitionFunction_order_three
docString:
Third derivative of the analytic normalized logarithm, with all disconnected partitions
subtracted explicitly.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) {β : ℝ},
  0 ≤ β →
    ∀ (g : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.QuarticVertexLabel Mode → ℂ),
      iteratedDeriv 2
          (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.analyticNormalizedLogPartitionFunction ε β
            (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticInteraction g))
          0 =
        2 *
            SecondQuantization.Fermionic.normalizedDysonPartitionCoeff ε β
              (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticInteraction g) 2 -
          SecondQuantization.Fermionic.normalizedDysonPartitionCoeff ε β
              (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticInteraction g) 1 ^
            2
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.iteratedDeriv_analyticNormalizedLogPartitionFunction_order_two
docString:
Second derivative of the analytic normalized logarithm, with the disconnected square
subtracted explicitly.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) {β : ℝ},
  0 ≤ β →
    ∀ (g : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.QuarticVertexLabel Mode → ℂ) (n : ℕ),
      n ≠ 0 →
        iteratedDeriv n
            (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.analyticNormalizedLogPartitionFunction ε β
              (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticInteraction g))
            0 =
          ∑ d, SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticWickDiagramAmplitude ε β g ↑d
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.iteratedDeriv_log_normalizedAnalyticPartitionFunction_eq_sum_connectedAmplitude
docString:
Analytic fermionic Dyson linked-cluster theorem: derivatives of the local normalized log
partition function are sums of connected quartic Wick-diagram amplitudes.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) {β : ℝ},
  0 ≤ β →
    ∀ (V : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.OccupationFock Mode →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Fermionic.OccupationFock Mode)
      (n : ℕ),
      iteratedDeriv n (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.normalizedAnalyticDysonPartitionFunction ε β V) 0 =
        Combinatorics.powerSeriesMomentCoeff
          (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.dysonPartitionSeries ε β V).normalizeByConstantCoeff n
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.iteratedDeriv_normalizedAnalyticDysonPartitionFunction_eq_powerSeriesMomentCoeff
docString:
Derivatives of the normalized analytic partition function are the exponential-generating
coefficients of the normalized formal Dyson partition series.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) {β : ℝ},
  0 ≤ β →
    ∀ (V : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.OccupationFock Mode →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Fermionic.OccupationFock Mode)
      (n : ℕ),
      iteratedDeriv (n + 1) (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.normalizedAnalyticDysonPartitionFunction ε β V) 0 =
        ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (n + 1),
          ↑(n.choose k) *
              iteratedDeriv (k + 1) (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.analyticNormalizedLogPartitionFunction ε β V) 0 *
            iteratedDeriv (n - k) (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.normalizedAnalyticDysonPartitionFunction ε β V) 0
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.iteratedDeriv_normalizedAnalyticDysonPartitionFunction_succ_eq_sum_log
docString:
Leibniz recurrence obtained from the local identity `(log F)' * F = F'`, where `F` is the
normalized analytic partition function.

statement:

name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.logOf_freeGrandPartitionSeries_eq_permutationConnectedCycleSeries
docString:
Free-fermion formal linked-cluster identity: the logarithm of the finite grand product equals the
`ζ = -1` connected-cycle series.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ),
  (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.freeGrandPartitionSeries ε β).logOf =

name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.logOf_freeGrandPartitionSeries_eq_sum_log
docString:
The formal logarithm of the free-fermion grand product is the sum of the modewise
`log(1 + t exp(-β εᵢ))` series.

statement:

statement:

docString:

the composed product of its `4n + 2` atomic creation/annihilation operators.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode]
  (w : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Occupation Mode → ℂ),
  SecondQuantization.Common.weightSum w ≠ 0 →
    ∀ (i : Mode),
      SecondQuantization.Common.normalizedWeightedDiagonal w
          ((SecondQuantization.Fermionic.annihilate i ∘ₗ SecondQuantization.Fermionic.create i) ∘ₗ
            SecondQuantization.Fermionic.annihilate i ∘ₗ SecondQuantization.Fermionic.create i) =
        SecondQuantization.Common.normalizedWeightedDiagonal w
                (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.annihilate i ∘ₗ SecondQuantization.Fermionic.create i) *
              SecondQuantization.Common.normalizedWeightedDiagonal w
                (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.annihilate i ∘ₗ SecondQuantization.Fermionic.create i) +
            ↑SecondQuantization.Common.Statistics.fermion.zetaInt *
              (SecondQuantization.Common.normalizedWeightedDiagonal w
                  (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.annihilate i ∘ₗ SecondQuantization.Fermionic.annihilate i) *
                SecondQuantization.Common.normalizedWeightedDiagonal w
                  (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.create i ∘ₗ SecondQuantization.Fermionic.create i)) +
          SecondQuantization.Common.normalizedWeightedDiagonal w
              (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.annihilate i ∘ₗ SecondQuantization.Fermionic.create i) *
            SecondQuantization.Common.normalizedWeightedDiagonal w
              (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.create i ∘ₗ SecondQuantization.Fermionic.annihilate i)
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.normalizedWeightedDiagonal_annihilate_create_annihilate_create_single_mode
docString:
**The single-mode 4-point Wick identity for normalized diagonal weights**:
`⟨cᵢcᵢ†cᵢcᵢ†⟩_w = ⟨cᵢcᵢ†⟩_w² + ζ⟨cᵢcᵢ⟩_w⟨cᵢ†cᵢ†⟩_w + ⟨cᵢcᵢ†⟩_w⟨cᵢ†cᵢ⟩_w`, matching
`Common/Thermal/BlochDeDominicis/PairingWeight.lean`'s four-position pairing weights `1`, `ζ`, `1` term by
term.
The middle term vanishes (`⟨cᵢcᵢ⟩_w = 0` from `annihilate_comp_self`), leaving `⟨cᵢcᵢ†⟩_w(⟨cᵢcᵢ†⟩_w
+ ⟨cᵢ†cᵢ⟩_w) = ⟨cᵢcᵢ†⟩_w · ⟨id⟩_w = ⟨cᵢcᵢ†⟩_w`, which matches the left side by `cᵢcᵢ†`'s
idempotency (`annihilate_comp_create_comp_self`).

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Mode] (w : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Occupation Mode → ℂ) (S : Finset Mode),

    SecondQuantization.Fermionic.occupationMoment w S
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.normalizedWeightedDiagonal_occupationProjector
docString:
**The normalized weighted functional of `occupationProjector S` is `occupationMoment w S`.**
The operator-level bridge promised by `occupationMoment`'s docstring: the simultaneous-occupation
observable's normalized weighted diagonal functional agrees with the direct weighted-sum
definition.

statement:

      (SecondQuantization.Common.timeOrderedProduct SecondQuantization.Common.Statistics.fermion
        (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.imaginaryTimeEvolve ε τ (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.annihilate i))
        (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.imaginaryTimeEvolve ε τ' (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.annihilate j)) τ τ') =

name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.normalizedWeightedDiagonal_timeOrderedProduct_annihilate_annihilate
docString: **`⟨T_τ[c_i(τ) c_j(τ')]⟩_w = 0`** for any occupation-diagonal weight `w`.

name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.numberOperator_basisState
docString:
**The number-operator eigenvalue equation**, on basis states: `Nᵢ` acts as the identity on
occupied modes and as zero on unoccupied ones — occupation-number states are simultaneous
eigenvectors of every `numberOperator i`, with eigenvalue `0` or `1`.

name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.numberOperator_comp_self
docString:
**`Nᵢ` is idempotent**: `Nᵢ ∘ Nᵢ = Nᵢ`, directly from the number-operator eigenvalue equation
(occupation-number basis states are simultaneous eigenvectors with eigenvalue `0` or `1`).

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Mode] {w : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Occupation Mode → ℂ} {A B : Finset Mode},
  SecondQuantization.Fermionic.IsProductWeightAcross w A B →
    SecondQuantization.Common.weightSum w ≠ 0 →
      A ≠ ⊥ → B ≠ ⊥ → SecondQuantization.Fermionic.occupationCumulant w (A ⊔ B) = 0
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.occupationCumulant_eq_zero_of_isProductWeightAcross
docString:
**Occupation-number cumulants vanish across a product-weight bipartition.** The physics-facing
form of `occupationMoment_isIndependentAcross`: under a product weight (e.g. a Gibbs weight for a
Hamiltonian `H = HA + HB` with `[HA, HB] = 0` and no cross-region interaction), the connected
correlator of modes spanning both `A` and `B` vanishes. This packages
`cumulantFromMoment_eq_zero_of_isIndependentAcross` so callers never need to name
`Finpartition.IsIndependentAcross` themselves.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Mode] {w : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Occupation Mode → ℂ},
  SecondQuantization.Common.weightSum w ≠ 0 → SecondQuantization.Fermionic.occupationMoment w ⊥ = 1
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.occupationMoment_bot
docString:
**`occupationMoment` at `⊥` is `1`** (given a nonzero partition function): every occupation
state vacuously contains the empty set of modes, so the numerator is exactly `Z(w)`. This matches
`Finpartition.IsIndependentAcross`'s `m ⊥ = 1` normalization hypothesis.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Mode] {w wA wB : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Occupation Mode → ℂ}
  {A B : Finset Mode},
  Disjoint A B →
    A ∪ B = Finset.univ →
      (∀ (n : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Occupation Mode), w n = wA (n ∩ A) * wB (n ∩ B)) →
        ∀ (T : Finset Mode),
          SecondQuantization.Fermionic.occupationMoment w T =
            ((∑ S ∈ A.powerset with T ∩ A ⊆ S, wA S) * ∑ T' ∈ B.powerset with T ∩ B ⊆ T', wB T') /
              SecondQuantization.Common.weightSum w
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.occupationMoment_eq_of_product_factorization
docString: **`occupationMoment` under a product weight, in terms of the two independent sides.**

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Mode] {w : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Occupation Mode → ℂ} {A B : Finset Mode},
  SecondQuantization.Fermionic.IsProductWeightAcross w A B →
    SecondQuantization.Common.weightSum w ≠ 0 →
      Finpartition.IsIndependentAcross (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.occupationMoment w) A B
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.occupationMoment_isIndependentAcross
docString:
**The main theorem: a product weight makes `occupationMoment` independent across its
bipartition.** Connects the physical independence hypothesis `IsProductWeightAcross` to the
abstract `Finpartition.IsIndependentAcross` condition used by the general cumulant-vanishing
theorem `cumulantFromMoment_eq_zero_of_isIndependentAcross`.

statement:

docString:
**`occupationMoment` at a singleton `{i}` is the normalized weighted diagonal functional of
`numberOperator i`.** This connects the weighted-sum definition to the operator-level normalized
weighted functional.

such observables combine into the observable for their union — direct from
`Common.diagonalOperator_comp`, since `S ∪ T ⊆ n ↔ S ⊆ n ∧ T ⊆ n`.
