statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} {N : ℕ} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  {S : Finset (Fin N)} (d : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.QuarticWickDiagram Mode N S)
  (orders : SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticDiagram.ComponentVertexOrders d)
  (shuffle : SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticDiagram.ComponentShuffle d) (τ : Fin S.card → ℝ)
  (B : ↥(SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticDiagram.componentPartition d).parts) (a b : Fin (2 * (2 * (↑B).card))),
  SecondQuantization.Fermionic.orderedQuarticPairValue ε β d
      (SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticDiagram.assembleVertexOrder d orders shuffle) τ
      (SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticDiagram.componentOrderedLeg d shuffle B a)
      (SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticDiagram.componentOrderedLeg d shuffle B b) =
    SecondQuantization.Fermionic.orderedQuarticPairValue ε β
      (SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticDiagram.restrictComponent d ⋯) (orders B)
      (Combinatorics.FamilySlotShuffleTo.timeAssignment shuffle τ B) a b
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.orderedQuarticPairValue_componentOrderedLeg
docString:
Pair values agree after embedding both component-local ordered legs into the assembled global
ordered-leg enumeration.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] {N : ℕ} (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  {S : Finset (Fin N)} (d : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.QuarticWickDiagram Mode N S)
  (order : SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticVertexOrder S) (τ : Fin S.card → ℝ) (a b : Fin (2 * (2 * S.card))),
  SecondQuantization.Fermionic.orderedQuarticPairValue ε β d order τ a b =
    Complex.exp
          ↑(τ ((SecondQuantization.Common.orderedQuarticLegEquiv S.card) a).1 *
              SecondQuantization.Common.quarticLocalLegEnergyShift ε
                (d.vertexLabel (order ((SecondQuantization.Common.orderedQuarticLegEquiv S.card) a).1))
                ((SecondQuantization.Common.orderedQuarticLegEquiv S.card) a).2) *
        Complex.exp
          ↑(τ ((SecondQuantization.Common.orderedQuarticLegEquiv S.card) b).1 *
              SecondQuantization.Common.quarticLocalLegEnergyShift ε
                (d.vertexLabel (order ((SecondQuantization.Common.orderedQuarticLegEquiv S.card) b).1))
                ((SecondQuantization.Common.orderedQuarticLegEquiv S.card) b).2) *
      (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.freeGibbsDensityOperator ε β).expectation
        (SecondQuantization.Common.finiteHilbertOperator
          (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticLocalLegOperator
              (d.vertexLabel (order ((SecondQuantization.Common.orderedQuarticLegEquiv S.card) a).1))
              ((SecondQuantization.Common.orderedQuarticLegEquiv S.card) a).2 ∘ₗ
            SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticLocalLegOperator
              (d.vertexLabel (order ((SecondQuantization.Common.orderedQuarticLegEquiv S.card) b).1))
              ((SecondQuantization.Common.orderedQuarticLegEquiv S.card) b).2))
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.orderedQuarticPairValue_eq
docString: Closed form of a pair value after extracting the imaginary-time exponential factors.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] {N : ℕ} (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  {S : Finset (Fin N)} (d : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.QuarticWickDiagram Mode N S)
  (order : SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticVertexOrder S) (τ : Fin S.card → ℝ) (a b : Fin (2 * (2 * S.card))),
  SecondQuantization.Fermionic.orderedQuarticPairValue ε β d order τ a b =
    (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.freeGibbsDensityOperator ε β).expectation
      (SecondQuantization.Common.finiteHilbertOperator
        (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.orderedQuarticLegOperator ε d order τ a ∘ₗ
          SecondQuantization.Fermionic.orderedQuarticLegOperator ε d order τ b))
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.orderedQuarticPairValue_eq_freeGibbsDensityOperator_expectation
docString:
The Wick pair value is the canonical free Gibbs density-state expectation of the transported
operator product.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] {N : ℕ} {S : Finset (Fin N)} (ε : Mode → ℝ)
  (β : ℝ) (d : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.QuarticWickDiagram Mode N S)
  (order : SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticVertexOrder S),
  SecondQuantization.Fermionic.QuarticWickDiagram.orderedSimplexContribution ε β d order =
    intervalIntegral.orderedSimplexIntegral S.card β fun τ =>
      SecondQuantization.Fermionic.flatVertexLegPairingEvaluation ε β (fun i => d.vertexLabel (order i)) τ
        (SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticDiagram.pairingInOrder d order)
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.orderedSimplexContribution_eq_pairingEvaluation
docString:
A diagram's fixed-order ordered-simplex contribution is the integral of its canonical pairing
evaluation after transport to the chosen vertex order.

∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) (n : ℕ)
  (q : Fin n → SecondQuantization.Fermionic.QuarticVertexLabel Mode) (τ : Fin n → ℝ),
  SecondQuantization.Common.prodComp (List.ofFn (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticLegOperatorForSequence ε q τ)) =
    SecondQuantization.Fermionic.nestedVertexOperatorComp ε n q τ
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.prodComp_ofFn_quarticLegOperatorForSequence_eq_nestedVertexOperatorComp
docString:
**`nestedVertexOperatorComp`, flattened into a `Common.prodComp` of its `4n` atomic legs** —
by induction on `n`: the base case is trivial (`Fin (2 * (2 * 0))` is empty); the successor case
reduces, via `nestedVertexOperatorComp_succ`,
`interactionPicture_quarticVertexOperator_eq_prodComp`, the inductive hypothesis, and
`Common.prodComp_append`, to the *pure list* equality `List.ofFn (quarticLegOperatorForSequence ε
q τ) = List.ofFn (4 atoms for vertex 0) ++ List.ofFn (quarticLegOperatorForSequence ε (tail q)
(tail τ))`, proved via `List.ofFn_fin_append`/`Fin.addCases` splitting the domain additively into
`4 + 2 * (2 * n)`: the `left` branch matches `quarticLegOperatorForSequence_cast_mul_add` at
vertex `0` directly; the `right` branch uses the Common
`eq_cast_mul_add_orderedQuarticLegEquiv` to express an *arbitrary* position `k` of the smaller
`n`-fold piece in `i' * 4 + j'` form, then matches both sides via
`quarticLegOperatorForSequence_cast_mul_add` (at `n` for the RHS, at `n + 1` and vertex `i'.succ`
for the LHS) — the two positions agree because `4 + (i' * 4 + j') = i'.succ * 4 + j'` as
naturals.

    SecondQuantization.Fermionic.imaginaryTimeEvolve ε (τ i)
      (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticLocalLegOperator (q i) j)

        (SecondQuantization.Common.flatLocalLeg n p)

**Every flattened leg operator is, up to its own `Complex.exp` eigenvalue-shift scalar, a bare
atomic `quarticLocalLegOperator`** — the normal form used by the flattened commutator calculation
and by consumers specializing the general evolved-leg eigenoperator theorem.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] {i j : Mode} (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  (g : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.QuarticVertexLabel Mode → ℂ) {n : ℕ} (T : Finset (Fin n))
  (ext : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.FixedExternalTwoPointWickDiagramOn Mode n T i j),
  SecondQuantization.Common.TwoPointDiagram.IsExternallyConnected ↑ext →
    ∀ (vac : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.QuarticWickDiagram Mode n (Finset.univ \ T)) (τ τ' : ℝ) (σ : Fin n → ℝ),
      StrictAnti (σ ∘ SecondQuantization.Common.slotSplitVacuumSlot T) →
        have d := SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fixedExternalOfSlotSplit T ext vac;
        d.dysonFixedTimeAmplitude ε β g τ τ' σ =
          d.externalPiece.dysonFixedTimeAmplitude ε β g τ τ'
              (SecondQuantization.Common.TwoPointDiagram.externalPieceTimes (↑d) σ) *
            SecondQuantization.Fermionic.orderedVacuumDysonIntegrand ε β g
              ((SecondQuantization.Common.quarticDiagramEquivOrderedData
                  (SecondQuantization.Common.slotSplitVacuumOrder T))
                vac)
              (σ ∘ SecondQuantization.Common.slotSplitVacuumSlot T)

docString:
The canonical fixed-fiber pointwise product can be written with the vacuum factor entirely in

∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] {N : ℕ} {S : Finset (Fin N)} (ε : Mode → ℝ)
  (β : ℝ) (g : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.QuarticVertexLabel Mode → ℂ)
  (order : SecondQuantization.Common.QuarticVertexOrder S),
  ∑ d, d.couplingWeight g * SecondQuantization.Fermionic.QuarticWickDiagram.orderedSimplexContribution ε β d order =
    ∑ q,

          intervalIntegral.orderedSimplexIntegral S.card β fun τ =>
            SecondQuantization.Fermionic.flatVertexLegPairingEvaluation ε β q τ pairing

Summing fixed-order diagram contributions gives the vertex-label/pairing double sum in canonical
evaluator form.

name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.sum_eq_sum_powerset_fixedExternalFiber
docString:
**The diagram sum as a sum over the slot split.** Every fixed-external diagram is a connected
piece on the slots its external component owns and a vacuum diagram on the rest, so the sum over all
diagrams is the sum over that slot set of the sum over both pieces.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype Mode] {A B : Finset Mode},
  Disjoint A B →
    A ∪ B = Finset.univ →
      ∀ (wA wB : Finset Mode → ℂ) (C : Finset Mode),
        ∑ n with C ⊆ n, wA (n ∩ A) * wB (n ∩ B) =
          (∑ S ∈ A.powerset with C ∩ A ⊆ S, wA S) * ∑ T ∈ B.powerset with C ∩ B ⊆ T, wB T
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.sum_filter_subset_eq_mul
docString:
**Reindexing a sum over occupation states restricted to contain `C`, split across a product
weight's two independent sides.** The combinatorial core of this section: every occupation state
`n ⊇ C` corresponds bijectively to a pair `(n ∩ A, n ∩ B)` with `n ∩ A ⊇ C ∩ A` a subset of `A`
and `n ∩ B ⊇ C ∩ B` a subset of `B` (via `Disjoint A B`/`A ∪ B = univ`), so a sum of a product
`wA (n ∩ A) * wB (n ∩ B)` over such `n` splits into a product of two independent sums.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [LinearOrder Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ) (s : Finset Mode),
  ∑ t ∈ s.powerset, SecondQuantization.Fermionic.freeBoltzmannWeight ε β t = ∏ j ∈ s, (1 + Complex.exp (-↑β * ↑(ε j)))
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.sum_freeBoltzmannWeight_powerset_eq_prod
docString:
**The free Boltzmann weight, summed over all subsets of a fixed mode set `s`, factorizes** as
a product over `s`: `Σ_{t ⊆ s} e^{-β E(t)} = ∏_{i ∈ s} (1 + e^{-βε_i})`. The general-`s` form (not
just `s = univ`) is what lets `freeGibbsDensityOperator_expectation_numberOperator` below reuse
this for the mode-`i`-removed partial product `s = univ.erase i`.

∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  (g : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.QuarticVertexLabel Mode → ℂ) (k : ℕ),
  (∑ x,
      ((-1) ^ k * ∏ q, g (x.1 q)) *
        intervalIntegral.orderedSimplexIntegral k β fun σ =>
          SecondQuantization.Fermionic.flatVertexLegPairingEvaluation ε β x.1 σ x.2) =
    SecondQuantization.Fermionic.normalizedDysonPartitionCoeff ε β (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticInteraction g) k
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.sum_orderedVacuumDysonContribution_eq_normalizedDysonPartitionCoeff
docString:
Summing the fixed-order Dyson contribution over ordered vacuum data gives the normalized vacuum
Dyson coefficient.  This is the fixed-order vacuum theorem with the irrelevant ambient vertex set
removed entirely.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  (g : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.QuarticVertexLabel Mode → ℂ) {N M : ℕ} (S : Finset (Fin N)) (T : Finset (Fin M)),
  S.card = T.card →
    ∑ d, SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticWickDiagramAmplitude ε β g d =
      ∑ d, SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticWickDiagramAmplitude ε β g d
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.sum_quarticWickDiagramAmplitude_eq_of_card_eq
docString:
**The total vacuum amplitude depends only on how many vertices there are.** Two vertex sets of
equal size, in possibly different ambient index types, carry the same total Wick-diagram amplitude.

This is what lets a component of a larger diagram be scored by the perturbation coefficient at its
own order without transporting the diagram itself: `dysonVertexMoment` is
`S.card ! * normalizedDysonPartitionCoeff ε β V S.card`, which mentions `S` only through its
cardinality.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] {i j : Mode} (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  (g : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.QuarticVertexLabel Mode → ℂ) (τ τ' : ℝ) {m k : ℕ}
  (ext : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.FixedExternalTwoPointWickDiagram Mode m i j)
  (x : SecondQuantization.Common.OrderedQuarticDiagramData (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.QuarticVertexLabel Mode) k),
  ∑ shuffle,
      intervalIntegral.orderedSimplexIntegral (m + k) β
        (shuffle.integrand (fun σ => ext.dysonFixedTimeAmplitude ε β g τ τ' σ)
          (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.orderedVacuumDysonIntegrand ε β g x)) =
    ext.dysonAmplitude ε β g τ τ' *
      (((-1) ^ k * ∏ q, g (x.1 q)) *
        intervalIntegral.orderedSimplexIntegral k β fun σ =>
          SecondQuantization.Fermionic.flatVertexLegPairingEvaluation ε β x.1 σ x.2)
name: SecondQuantization.Fermionic.sum_slotShuffleDysonIntegral_eq_external_mul_orderedVacuum
docString:
The binary shuffle product theorem in ordered-data coordinates for the vacuum factor.

Unlike a quartic diagram on an ambient complement, `x` is independent of the ambient locations of
those complement slots.  This is the form that can be held fixed while summing the external-slot
shuffles.

  (1 + Complex.exp ↑(-ε i * β)) *
      SecondQuantization.Common.traceFock
        (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.imaginaryTimeEvolveFree ε (-β) ∘ₗ
          SecondQuantization.Fermionic.annihilate i ∘ₗ SecondQuantization.Fermionic.create j) =
    (if i = j then 1 else 0) *
      SecondQuantization.Common.traceFock (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.imaginaryTimeEvolveFree ε (-β))

docString:
**The finite-mode fermionic two-point identity**:
`(1 + e^{-εᵢβ}) Tr[e^{-βH₀}(cᵢcⱼ†)] = δᵢⱼ Tr[e^{-βH₀}]`.

This is the fermionic specialization of `Common.traceFock_diagonalEvolution_comp_two_point`, with
`q₁ := -εᵢ`, exchange sign `ζ := -1`, and c-number exchange term `δᵢⱼ`. At `i = j` it gives
`⟨cᵢcᵢ†⟩ = 1 - ⟨Nᵢ⟩`, matching the closed form in
`Fermionic/Thermal/FreeGibbsGreenFunction.lean`.

docString:
**The order-`n` two-point coefficient is the sum of the integrated diagram amplitudes.**

This is the bridge from the public coefficient, defined as the ordered-simplex integral of the
pointwise diagram sum, to the per-diagram `dysonAmplitude` on which every component and
external/vacuum factorization is stated.

statement:

  0 ≤ β →
    ∀ (g : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.QuarticVertexLabel Mode → ℂ) (i j : Mode) (τ τ' : ℝ) (n : ℕ),
      SecondQuantization.Fermionic.twoPointDysonCoefficient ε β g i j τ τ' =
        ∑ m ∈ Finset.range (n + 1),
          SecondQuantization.Fermionic.connectedTwoPointDysonCoefficient ε β g i j τ τ' m *
            SecondQuantization.Fermionic.normalizedDysonPartitionCoeff ε β
              (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticInteraction g) (n - m)

docString:

At order `n`, the complete operator-defined two-point Dyson coefficient is the Cauchy convolution of
the connected two-point coefficients with the normalized vacuum partition coefficients.

statement:
∀ {Mode : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder Mode] [inst_1 : Fintype Mode] (ε : Mode → ℝ) (β : ℝ)
  (g : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.QuarticVertexLabel Mode → ℂ) (n : ℕ) (t : ℝ)
  (L : SecondQuantization.Fermionic.OccupationFock Mode →ₗ[ℂ] SecondQuantization.Fermionic.OccupationFock Mode),
  SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fermionEnergy ε) β
      (L ∘ₗ
        SecondQuantization.Common.dysonCoeff (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fermionEnergy ε)
          (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.quarticInteraction g) n t) =
    (-1) ^ n *
      ∑ q,
        (∏ i, g (q i)) *
          intervalIntegral.orderedSimplexIntegral n t fun τ =>
            SecondQuantization.Common.finiteGibbsExpectation (SecondQuantization.Fermionic.fermionEnergy ε) β
              (L ∘ₗ SecondQuantization.Fermionic.nestedVertexOperatorComp ε n q τ)
name: _private.LeanCondensedMatter.SecondQuantization.Fermionic.Diagrammatics.DysonDiagramExpansion.Core.0.SecondQuantization.Fermionic.finiteGibbsExpectation_comp_dysonCoeff_quarticInteraction
docString:
**The key induction: `dysonCoeff` of `quarticInteraction`, left-composed with an arbitrary
fixed prefix operator `L`, expands into a `(-1)ⁿ`-signed sum over vertex-label sequences of an
`orderedSimplexIntegral` of `L`-prefixed `nestedVertexOperatorComp` values.** The prefix `L`
generalizes the induction so the successor case can absorb the newly-peeled-off outermost vertex
factor into `L` before invoking the inductive hypothesis on the remaining `n`-fold piece; the
bound `t` likewise generalizes so the inductive step's inner integral (over `[0, σ]` for the
recursion's own integration variable `σ`) is exactly an instance of the same statement, rather
than requiring a separate lemma for non-`β` bounds.

∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  {T : H →L[ℂ] H},
  IsSelfAdjoint T → ∀ {v : H} {c : ℝ}, ↑T v = ↑c • v → ∀ {f : ℝ → ℝ}, Continuous f → (cfc f T) v = ↑(f c) • v
name: cfc_apply_eigenvector
docString:
**The continuous functional calculus acts on eigenvectors by evaluation.** For a
self-adjoint `T` and an eigenvector `v` of `T` with (real) eigenvalue `c`, `cfc f T` acts on
`v` by scaling it by `f c`, for any continuous `f : ℝ → ℝ`. Proved by approximating `f`
uniformly by polynomials on `[-‖T‖, ‖T‖]` (a compact interval containing `spectrum ℝ T`,
via the classical Weierstrass approximation theorem) and passing to the limit using the
isometry of `cfcHom` together with `Polynomial.aeval_apply_eigenvector`.

statement: ∀ (β x₀ x : ℝ), -β * Real.exp (-β * x₀) * x + (Real.exp (-β * x₀) - -β * Real.exp (-β * x₀) * x₀) ≤ Real.exp (-β * x)
name: exp_tangent
docString:
The tangent-line minorant for `x ↦ exp(-β x)` at `x₀`, discharging `peierls_bogoliubov`'s
`htangent` hypothesis for this concrete `g` (the case needed for the Gibbs state
`e^{-βH}`). Proved directly from `Real.add_one_le_exp`, without any general convexity
machinery.

statement:
∀ (β x₀ x : ℝ),
  β ≠ 0 →
    (-β * Real.exp (-β * x₀) * x + (Real.exp (-β * x₀) - -β * Real.exp (-β * x₀) * x₀) = Real.exp (-β * x) ↔ x = x₀)
name: exp_tangent_eq_iff
docString: For nonzero `β`, equality with the tangent line occurs exactly at the tangency point.

statement:
∀ (β x₀ x : ℝ),
  β ≠ 0 → x ≠ x₀ → -β * Real.exp (-β * x₀) * x + (Real.exp (-β * x₀) - -β * Real.exp (-β * x₀) * x₀) < Real.exp (-β * x)
name: exp_tangent_strict
docString:
For nonzero `β`, the tangent line to `x ↦ exp (-β x)` at `x₀` lies strictly below the
exponential away from `x₀`.

statement:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype ι] (β x₀ : ℝ),
  β ≠ 0 →
    ∀ (w E : ι → ℝ),
      (∀ (i : ι), 0 ≤ w i) →
        ∑ i, w i * (-β * Real.exp (-β * x₀) * E i + (Real.exp (-β * x₀) - -β * Real.exp (-β * x₀) * x₀)) =
            ∑ i, w i * Real.exp (-β * E i) →
          ∀ (i : ι), 0 < w i → E i = x₀
name: exp_tangent_weighted_sum_eq_support
docString:
Equality between a finite nonnegative weighted sum of exponential values and the corresponding
weighted tangent values forces every point with positive weight to be the tangency point.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (T : H →L[ℂ] H) (hT : IsSelfAdjoint T) (β : ℝ) (e : H),
  ‖e‖ = 1 → ↑(Real.exp (-β * T.diagonalExpectationValue hT e)) ≤ inner ℂ ((cfc (fun x => Real.exp (-β * x)) T) e) e
name: gibbs_peierls_bogoliubov
docString:
**Peierls–Bogoliubov, specialized to the Gibbs weight `g = exp(-β·)`.** The inequality is
stated directly in the complex positive order, so it also records the reality of the Gibbs
diagonal matrix element.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [FiniteDimensional ℂ H]
  [inst_3 : CompleteSpace H] (T : H →L[ℂ] H) (hT : IsSelfAdjoint T) (β : ℝ),
  β ≠ 0 →
    ∀ (e : H),
      ‖e‖ = 1 →
        (↑(Real.exp (-β * T.diagonalExpectationValue hT e)) = inner ℂ ((cfc (fun x => Real.exp (-β * x)) T) e) e ↔
          ↑T e = ↑(T.diagonalExpectationValue hT e) • e)
name: gibbs_peierls_bogoliubov_eq_iff_eigenvector
docString:
In finite dimension and for `β ≠ 0`, equality in the Gibbs specialization of the
Peierls–Bogoliubov inequality holds exactly when the unit vector is an eigenvector of the original
self-adjoint operator, with eigenvalue equal to its lossless diagonal expectation.

statement: ∀ (x y : ℝ), 0 ≤ x → 0 < y → x.negMulLog + x - y ≤ -x * Real.log y
name: gibbs_scalar_ineq
docString: Gibbs' scalar inequality.

statement: ∀ (x y : ℝ), 0 ≤ x → 0 < y → (x.negMulLog + x - y = -x * Real.log y ↔ x = y)
name: gibbs_scalar_ineq_eq_iff
docString: Equality in Gibbs' scalar inequality holds exactly on the diagonal `x = y`.

A bounded interval-integrable Banach-valued function has an absolutely continuous indefinite
interval integral.

A measurable locally bounded integrand gives a uniform bound for its recursively exposed

The recursively exposed outer boundary of a measurable locally bounded ordered-simplex

Measurable local boundedness is preserved by pointwise multiplication: the product of two
uniform cube bounds bounds the product.

statement: ∀ {β t : ℝ}, t ∈ Set.uIcc 0 β → |t| ≤ |β|

Every point of the unoriented closed interval between `0` and `β` has absolute value at most

name: intervalIntegral.ae_hasDerivAt_intervalIntegral_of_intervalIntegrable
docString: Local Banach-valued Lebesgue differentiation theorem for an interval-integrable function.

statement:
∀ {X : Type u_1} [inst : TopologicalSpace X] (n : ℕ) (bound : X → ℝ) (f : X → (Fin n → ℝ) → ℂ),
  Continuous bound →
    Continuous (Function.uncurry f) → Continuous fun x => intervalIntegral.orderedSimplexIntegral n (bound x) (f x)
name: intervalIntegral.continuous_orderedSimplexIntegral_of_continuous
docString:
**`orderedSimplexIntegral` is continuous in an outer parameter `x`, jointly through both its
own bound and its integrand.** For a continuous `bound : X → ℝ` and a jointly continuous
`f : X → (Fin n → ℝ) → ℂ`, `x ↦ orderedSimplexIntegral n (bound x) (f x)` is continuous — the
*bound itself* (not just the integrand, for a *fixed* bound) is allowed to vary continuously with
`x`. Proved by induction on `n`, generalizing the parameter space `X`/`bound`/`f` at each level
(the successor case's own inner recursion needs the inductive hypothesis at the *bigger* parameter
space `X × ℝ`, pairing the original parameter with the outer integral's own integration variable),
via `intervalIntegral.continuous_parametric_intervalIntegral_of_continuous` (Leibniz-rule-style
joint continuity of a parametrized interval integral with a variable, parameter-dependent, upper
limit) and `Continuous.finCons` (joint continuity of `Fin.cons`).

statement:
∀ (n : ℕ) (f : (Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) → ℂ),

    ∀ (β : ℝ),

        (intervalIntegral.orderedSimplexIntegral n β fun rest => f (Fin.cons β rest)) β
name: intervalIntegral.hasDerivAt_orderedSimplexIntegral_succ
docString:
Fundamental theorem of calculus for an ordered-simplex integral: differentiating in the upper
bound fixes the outermost time coordinate at that bound.

statement:
∀ {F F' : ℝ → ℂ} {a b C : ℝ},

          (∀ᵐ (x : ℝ), x ∈ Set.uIcc a b → HasDerivAt F (F' x) x) → ∫ (x : ℝ) in a..b, F' x = F b - F a
name: intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_absolutelyContinuousOnInterval_of_ae_hasDerivAt_of_norm_le
docString:
Fundamental theorem of calculus for an absolutely continuous complex-valued primitive with a
specified a.e. derivative.  The derivative is assumed bounded only to construct the absolutely
continuous Bochner primitive used in the standard zero-derivative argument.

statement: ∀ {n : ℕ} (c : ℂ), intervalIntegral.MeasurableLocallyBounded fun x => c
name: intervalIntegral.measurableLocallyBounded_const

statement:

docString: A globally measurable finite selection from continuous branches is measurably locally bounded.

docString:
For a measurable integrand, its ordered-simplex integral is measurable as a function of the
recursively oriented upper bound.

A jointly measurable integrand remains measurable after integration from `0` to a measurable
parameter-dependent upper bound.

A uniform norm bound on the centered cube gives a rough `|β|^n` bound for the recursively
oriented ordered-simplex integral.

Changing the presentation of the finite coordinate count only precomposes the integrand with the

  0 ≤ β →
    ∀ (f g : (Fin n → ℝ) → ℂ),

        intervalIntegral.orderedSimplexIntegral n β f = intervalIntegral.orderedSimplexIntegral n β g

docString:
The form the relabel covariance layer consumes: a strictly decreasing assignment is injective,
so an identity available only at injective interaction times still determines the integral.

statement:
∀ (n : ℕ) (β : ℝ),
  0 ≤ β →
    ∀ (f g : (Fin n → ℝ) → ℂ),
      (∀ (τ : Fin n → ℝ), StrictAnti τ → (∀ (i : Fin n), τ i < β) → f τ = g τ) →
        intervalIntegral.orderedSimplexIntegral n β f = intervalIntegral.orderedSimplexIntegral n β g
name: intervalIntegral.orderedSimplexIntegral_congr_of_strictAnti
docString:
**Only strictly decreasing assignments matter.** Two integrands that agree on every strictly
decreasing assignment bounded by `β` have the same ordered-simplex integral.

statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (β : ℝ) (c : ℂ), (intervalIntegral.orderedSimplexIntegral n β fun x => c) = ↑(β ^ n / ↑n.factorial) * c

docString:
**Sanity check**: on a constant function, the ordered-simplex integral reduces to the
elementary-calculus volume `βⁿ/n!` of the simplex, times the constant.

statement:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} (s : Finset ι) (n : ℕ) (β : ℝ) (f : ι → (Fin n → ℝ) → ℂ),
  (∀ i ∈ s, Continuous (f i)) →
    (intervalIntegral.orderedSimplexIntegral n β fun τ => ∑ i ∈ s, f i τ) =
      ∑ i ∈ s, intervalIntegral.orderedSimplexIntegral n β (f i)
name: intervalIntegral.orderedSimplexIntegral_finsetSum
docString:
**A finite sum commutes with `orderedSimplexIntegral`**, given continuity of every summand —
the tailored integrability the module docstring says any such lemma needs. Proved by induction on
`n`, using `intervalIntegral.integral_finsetSum` at each level and
`continuous_orderedSimplexIntegral_of_continuous` to supply that lemma's own
`IntervalIntegrable` hypotheses.

statement:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} (s : Finset ι) (n : ℕ) (β : ℝ) (f : ι → (Fin n → ℝ) → ℂ),
  (∀ i ∈ s, intervalIntegral.MeasurableLocallyBounded (f i)) →
    (intervalIntegral.orderedSimplexIntegral n β fun τ => ∑ i ∈ s, f i τ) =
      ∑ i ∈ s, intervalIntegral.orderedSimplexIntegral n β (f i)

docString:
**A finite sum commutes with `orderedSimplexIntegral` under measurable local boundedness.**

The continuity hypothesis of `orderedSimplexIntegral_finsetSum` is unavailable for integrands that
are only chamberwise continuous, which is the situation every mixed-order expansion produces.  Only
interval integrability of each recursively exposed boundary is actually needed, and that is exactly
what `MeasurableLocallyBounded` supplies.

statement:
∀ (n : ℕ) (β : ℝ) (f : (Fin n → ℝ) → ℂ),
  (intervalIntegral.orderedSimplexIntegral n β fun τ => -f τ) = -intervalIntegral.orderedSimplexIntegral n β f
name: intervalIntegral.orderedSimplexIntegral_neg

statement:

name: intervalIntegral.orderedSimplexIntegral_smul

statement:
∀ (n : ℕ) (β : ℝ) (f : (Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) → ℂ),

    ∫ (τ : ℝ) in 0..β, intervalIntegral.orderedSimplexIntegral n τ fun rest => f (Fin.cons τ rest)
name: intervalIntegral.orderedSimplexIntegral_succ

statement:
∀ (m n : ℕ) (β : ℝ) (f : (Fin (m + 1) → ℝ) → ℂ) (g : (Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) → ℂ),
  Continuous f →
    Continuous g →
      intervalIntegral.orderedSimplexIntegral (m + 1) β f * intervalIntegral.orderedSimplexIntegral (n + 1) β g =
        ∫ (t : ℝ) in 0..β,
          (intervalIntegral.orderedSimplexIntegral m t fun rest => f (Fin.cons t rest)) *
              intervalIntegral.orderedSimplexIntegral (n + 1) t g +
            intervalIntegral.orderedSimplexIntegral (m + 1) t f *
              intervalIntegral.orderedSimplexIntegral n t fun rest => g (Fin.cons t rest)
name: intervalIntegral.orderedSimplexIntegral_succ_mul_succ
docString:
Split a product of two positive-dimensional ordered-simplex integrals by the component that
contains the largest time. This is the analytic recurrence underlying the binary shuffle identity:
the first summand fixes the left outermost time, while the second fixes the right outermost time.

statement:

  intervalIntegral.MeasurableLocallyBounded f →
    intervalIntegral.MeasurableLocallyBounded g →

        ∫ (t : ℝ) in 0..β,

              intervalIntegral.orderedSimplexIntegral (n + 1) t g +
            intervalIntegral.orderedSimplexIntegral (m + 1) t f *
              intervalIntegral.orderedSimplexIntegral n t fun rest => g (Fin.cons t rest)
name: intervalIntegral.orderedSimplexIntegral_succ_mul_succ_of_measurableLocallyBounded
docString:
Split a product of two positive-dimensional ordered-simplex integrals under measurable local
boundedness, with no global continuity assumption on either raw integrand.

name: intervalIntegral.orderedSimplexIntegral_zero

Binary shuffle identity: the recursively accumulated contribution of all order-preserving
interleavings equals the product of the two component ordered-simplex integrals.

docString: Binary shuffle identity for measurable locally bounded integrands.

statement: ∀ {n : ℕ} {R S : ℝ}, R ≤ S → intervalIntegral.orderedSimplexTimeCube n R ⊆ intervalIntegral.orderedSimplexTimeCube n S
name: intervalIntegral.orderedSimplexTimeCube_mono
docString: Enlarging the radius enlarges the centered ordered-simplex coordinate cube.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  {T : H →L[ℂ] H},
  IsSelfAdjoint T → IsCompactOperator ⇑T → ∀ {f : ℝ → ℝ}, Continuous f → f 0 = 0 → IsCompactOperator ⇑(cfc f T)
name: isCompactOperator_cfc_of_zero
docString:
If `T` is a compact self-adjoint operator and a continuous real function vanishes at zero,
then its continuous functional calculus `cfc f T` is compact.

The proof approximates `f` uniformly on `[-‖T‖, ‖T‖]` by polynomials and subtracts each
approximant's value at zero. The resulting polynomials still converge uniformly to `f`, have zero
constant coefficient, and therefore evaluate to compact operators. Compact operators are closed in
the operator norm, so the CFC limit is compact.

statement:
∀ {p q Z u : ℝ},
  0 < p →
    0 < q → 0 < Z → -Real.log q ≤ u → (p.negMulLog = p * u + p * Real.log Z - p + q / Z ↔ p = q / Z ∧ -Real.log q = u)
name: negMulLog_bound_eq_iff
docString:
Equality in the scalar estimate used by the Gibbs–Klein proof forces both constituent
inequalities to be equalities: the probability equals the normalized Gibbs diagonal weight, and
the logarithmic bound is saturated.

statement: ∀ {p q Z u : ℝ}, 0 ≤ p → 0 < q → 0 < Z → -Real.log q ≤ u → p.negMulLog ≤ p * u + p * Real.log Z - p + q / Z
name: negMulLog_le_of_neg_log_le
docString: Combine `gibbs_scalar_ineq` with a bound on `-log q`.

statement: ∀ {u q : ℝ}, Real.exp (-u) ≤ q → -Real.log q ≤ u
name: neg_log_le_of_exp_le
docString: From `exp(-u) ≤ q`, obtain `-log q ≤ u`.

statement:
∀ {H : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup H] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace H]
  (T : H →L[ℂ] H) (hT : IsSelfAdjoint T) (g : ℝ → ℝ),
  ContinuousOn g (spectrum ℝ T) →
    ∀ (e : H),
      ‖e‖ = 1 →
        ∀ (m x₀ : ℝ),
          x₀ = T.diagonalExpectationValue hT e →
            (∀ (x : ℝ), m * x + (g x₀ - m * x₀) ≤ g x) → ↑(g x₀) ≤ inner ℂ ((cfc g T) e) e
name: peierls_bogoliubov
docString:
**The Peierls–Bogoliubov inequality.** For a self-adjoint bounded operator `T`, a unit
vector `e`, and a continuous `g : ℝ → ℝ` admitting a tangent line at the lossless real diagonal
expectation `x₀`, `g x₀` is below the diagonal matrix element of `g(T)` in the complex positive
order.

statement:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq ι] [inst_1 : CommMonoid M] {j : ι} {s : Finset ι},
  j ∉ s → ∀ (g : ↥(insert j s) → M), ∏ i, g i = g ⟨j, ⋯⟩ * ∏ i, g ⟨↑i, ⋯⟩
name: prod_subtype_insert_eq
docString: Split a product over the subtype of an inserted finite set.

name: tsum_div_le_one
docString: The sum of `q i / Z` is at most one when `∑' i, q i ≤ Z` and `Z > 0`.

statement:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {κ : Type u_2} {E : Type u_3} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] {g : ι × κ → E} {row : ι → E}
  {col : κ → E},
  Summable g →
    (∀ (i : ι), HasSum (fun j => g (i, j)) (row i)) →
      (∀ (j : κ), HasSum (fun i => g (i, j)) (col j)) →
        Summable row ∧ Summable col ∧ ∑' (i : ι), row i = ∑' (j : κ), col j
name: tsum_fiberwise_eq_of_summable
docString:
**Row-first and column-first iterated sums of a summable double family agree, with each
individually summable.** Given `g : ι × κ → E` summable, together with `HasSum` data for its row
sums (`row i = Σⱼ g(i,j)`) and column sums (`col j = Σᵢ g(i,j)`), `row` and `col` are themselves
summable and have the same total.
